sentences.zh: 王彌

translations.literal: Wang Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi

sentences.zh: 王彌，東萊人也。

translations.literal: Wang Mi was a man of Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi came from Donglai.

sentences.zh: 家世二千石。

translations.literal: His family for generations had held offices of two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had held governorship-level posts.

sentences.zh: 祖頎，魏玄菟太守，武帝時，至汝南太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qi was Administrator of Xuantu in Wei; under Emperor Wu he reached Administrator of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wang Qi had served Wei as administrator of Xuantu and, under Emperor Wu, rose to administrator of Runan.

sentences.zh: 彌有才幹，博涉書記。

translations.literal: Mi had talent and ability and was broadly versed in documents and records.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was capable and widely read in administrative texts and histories.

sentences.zh: 少遊俠京都，隱者董仲道見而謂之曰：「君豺聲豹視，好亂樂禍，若天下騷擾，不作士大夫矣。

translations.literal: In his youth he roamed as a knight-errant in the capital. The recluse Dong Zhongdao saw him and said to him, "You have the voice of a jackal and the gaze of a leopard; you love turmoil and delight in calamity. If the realm is thrown into disorder, you will not become a gentleman-official."
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he swaggered through the capital like a wandering bravo. The recluse Dong Zhongdao took one look and told him, "You have a jackal's voice and a leopard's stare; you relish chaos and feed on disaster. Once the empire boils over, you will never settle into the life of a proper official."

sentences.zh: 」惠帝末，妖賊劉柏根起於東萊之惤縣，彌率家僮從之，柏根以為長史。

translations.literal: " Toward the end of Emperor Hui's reign, the sorcerer-rebel Liu Baigen rose in Jiao County of Donglai; Mi led his household retainers to follow him, and Baigen made him chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Hui's reign, the rebel leader Liu Baigen rose in Jiao County in Donglai. Mi brought his household retainers to join him, and Baigen appointed him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 柏根死，聚徒海渚，為苟純所敗，亡入長廣山為群賊。

translations.literal: When Baigen died, Mi gathered followers on sea islets; Gou Chun defeated him, and he fled into Mount Changgang and became chief of a band of brigands.
translations.idiomatic: After Baigen died, Mi rallied followers on coastal islets until Gou Chun crushed him; he escaped into Mount Changgang and emerged as the leader of a bandit horde.

sentences.zh: 彌多權略，凡有所掠，必豫圖成敗，舉無遺策，弓馬迅捷，膂力過人，青土號為「飛豹」。

translations.literal: Mi had many stratagems; whenever he plundered, he always planned in advance for success or failure and never missed a tactic; he was swift with bow and horse and his bodily strength surpassed others; the eastern plain called him the "Flying Leopard."
translations.idiomatic: Mi was a master of stratagem: every raid was plotted for how it might end, and he rarely misjudged the odds. He was deadly with bow and horse, stronger than ordinary men, and people along the eastern coast nicknamed him the "Flying Leopard."

sentences.zh: 後引兵入寇青徐，兗州刺史苟晞逆擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Later he led troops to raid Qing and Xu; Governor of Yanzhou Gou Xi met him in attack and routed him badly.
translations.idiomatic: He later led his army to ravage Qingzhou and Xuzhou, but Gou Xi, the inspector of Yanzhou, intercepted him and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 彌退集亡散，眾復大振，晞與之連戰，不能克。

translations.literal: Mi withdrew, gathered the scattered survivors, and his host again swelled greatly; Xi fought him in succession but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Mi regrouped the fugitives, and his army swelled once more; Gou Xi fought him again and again but could not break him.

sentences.zh: 彌進兵寇泰山、魯國、譙、梁、陳、汝南、潁川、襄城諸郡，入許昌，開府庫，取器杖，所在陷沒，多殺守令，有眾數萬，朝廷不能制。

translations.literal: Mi advanced troops to raid the commanderies of Taishan, Lu, Qiao, Liang, Chen, Runan, Yingchuan, and Xiangcheng, entered Xuchang, opened government storehouses, took weapons; wherever he went cities fell, he killed many prefects and magistrates, had a host of several tens of thousands, and the court could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: He marched through Taishan, Lu, Qiao, Liang, Chen, Runan, Yingchuan, and Xiangcheng, seized Xuchang, looted armories, and armed his men. County seats fell in his path; he executed prefects and magistrates until he commanded tens of thousands, and the court was powerless to stop him.

sentences.zh: 會天下大亂，進逼洛陽，京邑大震，宮城門晝閉。

translations.literal: It happened that the realm was in great chaos; he advanced and pressed Luoyang; the capital was greatly shaken and the palace gates were closed by day.
translations.idiomatic: As the empire slid into chaos, he pressed on Luoyang; the capital trembled, and even in daylight the palace gates stayed shut.

sentences.zh: 司徒王衍等率百官距守，彌屯七里澗，王師進擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Wang Yan and others led the hundred officials to defend against him; Mi encamped at Qili Ford; the royal army advanced and struck, routing him badly.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Yan mustered the officials to hold the defenses while Mi camped at Qili Ford; the imperial army attacked and dealt him a severe defeat.

sentences.zh: 彌謂其党劉靈曰：「晉兵尚強，歸無所厝。

translations.literal: Mi said to his partisan Liu Ling, "The Jin troops are still strong; if we return we have nowhere to lodge."
translations.idiomatic: Mi told his follower Liu Ling, "The Jin forces are still formidable; we have nowhere to go if we turn back."

sentences.zh: 劉元海昔為質子，我與之周旋京師，深有分契，今稱漢王，將歸之，可乎？

translations.literal: Liu Yuanhai was once a hostage; I associated with him in the capital and we had deep mutual understanding. Now he styles himself King of Han—if we go to join him, would that do?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan once served as a hostage in Luoyang, and I knew him well in the capital; we were genuinely close. Now he has taken the title King of Han—what if we throw in our lot with him?"

sentences.zh: 」靈然之。

translations.literal: " Ling agreed with this.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ling agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃渡河歸元海。

translations.literal: Thereupon they crossed the river and went to Yuanhai.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the Yellow River and submitted to Liu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 元海聞而大悅，遣其侍中兼御史大夫郊迎，致書於彌曰：「以將軍有不世之功，超時之德，故有此迎耳。

translations.literal: When Yuanhai heard it he was greatly pleased; he sent his palace attendant and concurrent imperial counselor to greet Mi outside the suburbs and sent Mi a letter saying, "Because the general has achievements not met in a generation and virtue beyond the age, therefore there is this welcome."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan was delighted. He sent a palace attendant who also held the post of imperial counselor to welcome Mi beyond the walls, with a letter that read: "You have won a fame seldom seen in any age and a moral stature that towers above your time—hence this reception."

sentences.zh: 遲望將軍之至，孤今親行將軍之館，輒拂席洗爵，敬待將軍。

translations.literal: I long await the general's arrival; I will now personally go to the general's lodging, will sweep the mat and rinse the goblets, and respectfully await the general."
translations.idiomatic: I am eager for your arrival; I shall walk to your quarters myself, sweep the mat, rinse the cups, and wait upon you with all courtesy."

sentences.zh: 」及彌見元海，勸稱尊號，元海謂彌曰：「孤本謂將軍如竇周公耳，今真吾孔明、仲華也。

translations.literal: " When Mi met Yuanhai, he urged him to assume the elevated title; Yuanhai said to Mi, "I originally thought of the general only as the Duke of Dou; now you are truly my Kongming and Zhonghua."
translations.idiomatic: When Mi met Liu Yuan, he urged him to take the imperial title. Liu Yuan told him, "I used to think of you merely as the Duke of Dou; now you are my Zhuge Liang and Deng Yu rolled into one."

sentences.zh: 烈祖有云：'吾之有將軍，如魚之有水。

translations.literal: My martial ancestor had a saying: 'With the general at my side, I am like a fish that has water.'"
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor once said, "With you at my side, I am like a fish returned to water.""

sentences.zh: '」於是署彌司隸校尉，加侍中、特進，彌固辭。

translations.literal: '" Thereupon he appointed Mi Metropolitan Commandant and added palace attendant and specially advanced distinctions; Mi firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: With that, Liu Yuan named him metropolitan commandant and added the titles of palace attendant and specially advanced incumbent; Mi steadfastly refused them.

sentences.zh: 使隨劉曜寇河內，又與石勒攻臨漳。

translations.literal: He had Mi follow Liu Yao to raid Henei and again join Shi Le in attacking Linzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Mi with Liu Yao to strike Henei and later to join Shi Le in the assault on Linzhang.

sentences.zh: 永嘉初，寇上黨，圍壺關，東海王越遣淮南內史王曠、安豐太守衛乾等討之，及彌戰于高都、長平間，大敗之，死者十六七。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongjia era, Mi raided Shangdang and besieged Huguan; Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, sent the interior minister of Huainan Wang Kuang, Administrator of Anfeng Wei Gan, and others to punish him; they fought Mi between Gaodu and Changping and routed him badly; sixty or seventy percent of his men died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongjia era he raided Shangdang and laid siege to Huguan. Sima Yue, prince of Donghai, dispatched Wang Kuang, interior minister of Huainan, Wei Gan, administrator of Anfeng, and others against him. The battle between Gaodu and Changping shattered Mi's army; six or seven men in ten were killed.

sentences.zh: 元海進彌征東大將軍，封東萊公。

translations.literal: Yuanhai advanced Mi to General Who Conquers the East and enfeoffed him as Duke of Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan promoted him to general who conquers the east and enfeoffed him as duke of Donglai.

sentences.zh: 與劉曜、石勒等攻魏郡、汲郡、頓丘，陷五十餘壁，皆調為軍士。

translations.literal: With Liu Yao, Shi Le, and others he attacked Wei and Ji commanderies and Dunqiu; more than fifty fortified places fell, and all were conscripted as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Alongside Liu Yao and Shi Le he overran Wei and Ji commanderies and Dunqiu, took more than fifty walled strongholds, and drafted every able body into the ranks.

sentences.zh: 又與勒攻鄴，安北將軍和郁棄城而走。

translations.literal: Again with Le he attacked Ye; the General Who Pacifies the North He Yu abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Shi Le again in an attack on Ye; He Yu, general who pacifies the north, abandoned the city and ran.

sentences.zh: 懷帝遣北中郎將裴憲次白馬討彌，車騎將軍王堪次東燕討勒，平北將軍曹武次大陽討元海。

translations.literal: Emperor Huai sent the General of the Central Army of the North Pei Xian to camp at Baima to punish Mi, the chariot and cavalry general Wang Kan to camp at Dongyan to punish Le, and the General Who Pacifies the North Cao Wu to camp at Dayang to punish Yuanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai ordered Pei Xian, general of the central army of the north, to encamp at Baima against Wang Mi; Wang Kan, chariot and cavalry general, at Dongyan against Shi Le; and Cao Wu, general who pacifies the north, at Dayang against Liu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 武部將軍彭默為劉聰所敗，見害，眾軍皆退。

translations.literal: Wu's subordinate general Peng Mo was defeated by Liu Cong and killed; all the armies withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wu's subordinate Peng Mo was routed by Liu Cong and killed, and every column fell back.

sentences.zh: 聰渡黃河，帝遣司隸校尉劉暾、將軍宋抽等距之，皆不能抗。

translations.literal: Cong crossed the Yellow River; the emperor sent Metropolitan Commandant Liu Tun, general Song Chou, and others to oppose him, but none could resist.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong crossed the Yellow River; the court sent Liu Tun, metropolitan commandant, Song Chou, and other generals to block him, but none could hold the line.

sentences.zh: 彌、聰以萬騎至京城，焚二學。

translations.literal: Mi and Cong reached the capital with ten thousand horse and burned the two schools.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi and Liu Cong rode into the capital at the head of ten thousand cavalry and put the two imperial academies to the torch.

sentences.zh: 東海王越距戰於西明門，彌等敗走。

translations.literal: The Prince of Donghai, Yue, met them in battle at the Ximing Gate, and Mi and the others were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue, prince of Donghai, gave battle at the Ximing Gate and drove Mi's forces off.

sentences.zh: 彌復以二千騎寇襄城諸縣，河東、平陽、弘農、上党諸流人之在潁川、襄城、汝南、南陽、河南者數萬家，為舊居人所不禮，皆焚燒城邑，殺二千石長吏以應彌。

translations.literal: Mi again led two thousand horse to raid the counties of Xiangcheng; several tens of thousands of refugee households from Hedong, Pingyang, Hongnong, and Shangdang who were in Yingchuan, Xiangcheng, Runan, Nanyang, and Henan were treated ill by the natives; all burned towns and cities, killed two-thousand-picul administrators and chief clerks, and rose in response to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Mi struck again with two thousand horsemen through the Xiangcheng counties. Tens of thousands of refugee families from Hedong, Pingyang, Hongnong, and Shangdang—settled in Yingchuan, Xiangcheng, Runan, Nanyang, and Henan—had been mistreated by locals; they now torched towns, slew magistrates, and rose in Mi's name.

sentences.zh: 彌又以二萬人會石勒寇陳郡、潁川，屯陽曜，遣弟璋與石勒共寇徐兗，因破越軍。

translations.literal: Mi again joined twenty thousand men with Shi Le to raid Chen and Yingchuan commanderies and encamped at Yangyao; he sent his younger brother Zhang and Shi Le together to raid Xu and Yan, and in the process broke Yue's army.
translations.idiomatic: He brought twenty thousand men to join Shi Le in ravaging Chen and Yingchuan and camped at Yangyao. He sent his brother Wang Zhang with Shi Le against Xu and Yan and together they shattered Sima Yue's army.

sentences.zh: 彌後與曜寇襄城，遂逼京師。

translations.literal: Mi later raided Xiangcheng with Yao and then pressed the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later, with Liu Yao, he plundered Xiangcheng and closed in on the capital.

sentences.zh: 時京邑大饑，人相食，百姓流亡，公卿奔河陰。

translations.literal: At that time the capital region was in great famine; people ate one another; commoners fled; dukes and ministers ran to Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped the capital; men fed on one another; commoners scattered; high officials fled toward Heyin.

sentences.zh: 曜、彌等遂陷宮城，至太極前殿，縱兵大掠。

translations.literal: Yao and Mi thereupon took the palace city, reached the front hall of Supreme Ultimate, and let their soldiers plunder on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao and Wang Mi broke into the palace, reached the main hall of the Hall of Supreme Polarity, and unleashed their troops for wholesale looting.

sentences.zh: 幽帝於端門，逼辱羊皇后，殺皇太子詮，發掘陵墓，焚燒宮廟，城府蕩盡，百官及男女遇害者三萬餘人，遂遷帝於平陽。

translations.literal: They shut the emperor up at Duan Gate, humiliated Empress Yang, killed Crown Prince Quan, dug up tombs, burned palaces and temples, so that city and fortifications were swept bare; officials and commoners, men and women, to the number of more than thirty thousand met death, and they then moved the emperor to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: They penned the emperor at Duan Gate, abused Empress Yang, murdered Crown Prince Sima Quan, opened imperial tombs, and burned palace shrines until the capital was a ruin. More than thirty thousand officials and civilians, men and women, perished before the emperor was marched off to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 彌之掠也，曜禁之，彌不從。

translations.literal: When Mi was plundering, Yao forbade it, but Mi did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mi's men began to loot, Liu Yao ordered them to stop; Mi refused.

sentences.zh: 曜斬其牙門王延以徇，彌怒，與曜阻兵相攻，死者千餘人。

translations.literal: Yao executed his gate officer Wang Yan as a warning; Mi was angry and with Yao crossed arms and attacked each other; more than a thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao executed Mi's gate officer Wang Yan as a warning. Enraged, the two turned their armies on each other, and more than a thousand men died.

sentences.zh: 彌長史張嵩諫曰：「明公與國家共興大事，事業甫耳，便相攻討，何面見主上乎！

translations.literal: Mi's chief clerk Zhang Song remonstrated: "The enlightened lord and the state together raised a great enterprise; the undertaking has only just begun, yet you turn to mutual attack—what face have you to see the sovereign!"
translations.idiomatic: Mi's chief clerk Zhang Song urged restraint: "You and the throne raised this great cause together; the work has barely begun, yet you are at each other's throats—how will you face your lord?"

sentences.zh: 平洛之功誠在將軍，然劉曜皇族，宜小下之。

translations.literal: The merit in pacifying Luoyang is indeed the general's, but Liu Yao is of the imperial clan; you should yield to him somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The credit for taking Luoyang is yours, but Liu Yao belongs to the imperial house; you ought to defer to him a little.

sentences.zh: 晉二王平吳之鑒，其則不遠，願明將軍以為慮。

translations.literal: The mirror of the two Jin princes who pacified Wu is not far off; I hope the eminent general will take it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: The lesson of the two Jin princes who conquered Wu is still fresh; I beg you, general, to weigh it carefully.

sentences.zh: 縱將軍阻兵不還，其若子弟宗族何！

translations.literal: Even if the general holds his army and does not return, what of your sons, brothers, and kinsmen!
translations.idiomatic: Even if you keep your army in the field and never come home, what becomes of your sons, brothers, and entire clan?

sentences.zh: 」彌曰：「善，微子，吾不聞此過也。

translations.literal: " Mi said, "Good—without you, I would not have heard of this fault."
translations.idiomatic: Mi replied, "Well said—without you I would never have seen my mistake."

sentences.zh: 」於是詣曜謝，結分如初。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he went to Yao to apologize, and their bond was as at first.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Liu Yao to apologize, and the two men patched up their alliance.

sentences.zh: 彌曰：「下官聞過，乃是張長史之功。

translations.literal: Mi said, "My having heard of my fault is owing to Chief Clerk Zhang's merit."
translations.idiomatic: Mi added, "If I have learned of my fault, the credit belongs to Chief Clerk Zhang."

sentences.zh: 」曜謂嵩曰：「君為硃建矣，豈況範生乎！

translations.literal: " Yao said to Song, "You are Zhu Jian—how much more Fan Sheng!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao told Zhang Song, "You are another Zhu Jian—what need to mention Fan Sheng!"

sentences.zh: 」各賜嵩金百斤。

translations.literal: " Each presented Song with a hundred catties of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Each of them rewarded Zhang Song with a hundred catties of gold.

sentences.zh: 彌謂曜曰：「洛陽天下之中，山河四險之固，城池宮室無假營造，可徙平陽都之。

translations.literal: Mi said to Yao, "Luoyang is the center of the realm, firmly defended by four mountain-and-river barriers; its walls and palace halls need no building anew—you could move the capital from Pingyang here."
translations.idiomatic: Mi said to Liu Yao, "Luoyang sits at the heart of the empire, ringed by four natural defenses; the walls and palaces are ready-made. You could move the court here from Pingyang."

sentences.zh: 」曜不從，焚燒而去。

translations.literal: " Yao did not consent but burned the city and left.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao refused, burned the city, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 彌怒曰：「屠各子，豈有帝王之意乎！

translations.literal: Mi said in anger, "That Tougu brat—does he have any intent to be an emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: Mi fumed, "That Tougu upstart—does he imagine he can rule as a true Son of Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 汝柰天下何！

translations.literal: What can you do about the realm!
translations.idiomatic: What does he imagine will become of the realm under him!

sentences.zh: 」遂引眾東屯項關。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he led his host east and encamped at Xiang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He led his troops east and encamped at Xiang Pass.

sentences.zh: 初，曜以彌先入洛，不待己，怨之，至是嫌隙遂構。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yao had resented Mi for entering Luoyang first and not waiting for him; by now the rift was set.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao had long resented Mi for seizing Luoyang ahead of him; now the breach between them was complete.

sentences.zh: 劉暾說彌還據青州，彌然之，乃以左長史曹嶷為鎮東將軍，給兵五千，多齎寶物還鄉里，招誘亡命，且迎其室。

translations.literal: Liu Tun urged Mi to return and hold Qingzhou; Mi agreed. He then appointed his left chief clerk Cao Yi General Who Guards the East, gave him five thousand troops and many treasures to return home, recruit fugitives, and fetch Mi's family.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tun persuaded Mi to go back and secure Qingzhou. Mi agreed, named his left chief clerk Cao Yi general who guards the east, gave him five thousand men and a train of treasure to return home, recruit outlaws, and bring Mi's household out.

sentences.zh: 彌將徐邈、高梁輒率部曲數千人隨嶷去，彌益衰弱。

translations.literal: Mi's generals Xu Miao and Gao Liang thereupon led several thousand retainers of their commands to follow Yi away, and Mi grew weaker still.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Xu Miao and Gao Liang promptly marched several thousand of their own followers off with Cao Yi, leaving Mi weaker than ever.

sentences.zh: 初，石勒惡彌驍勇，常密為之備。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shi Le had hated Mi's fierce bravery and always secretly guarded against him.
translations.idiomatic: For some time Shi Le had feared Mi's ferocity and kept a discreet watch on him.

sentences.zh: 彌之破洛陽也，多遺勒美女寶貨以結之。

translations.literal: When Mi broke Luoyang he sent many beautiful women and treasures to Le to win him over.
translations.idiomatic: After Mi took Luoyang he showered Shi Le with concubines and treasure to buy his goodwill.

sentences.zh: 時勒擒苟晞，以為左司馬，彌謂勒曰：「公獲苟晞而用之，何其神妙！

translations.literal: At that time Le had captured Gou Xi and made him left marshal; Mi said to Le, "Your having captured Gou Xi and employed him—how divinely subtle!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le had just captured Gou Xi and appointed him senior marshal. Mi told him, "To seize Gou Xi and put him to work for you—that is inspired!"

sentences.zh: 使晞為公左，彌為公右，天下不足定也！

translations.literal: If Xi serves at your left and Mi at your right, the realm is not worth settling!"
translations.idiomatic: With Gou Xi on your left and me on your right, the empire would fall into your lap!"

sentences.zh: 」勒愈忌彌，陰圖之。

translations.literal: " Le grew more jealous of Mi and secretly plotted against him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le only grew more suspicious and began plotting Mi's downfall in secret.

sentences.zh: 劉暾又勸彌征曹嶷，藉其眾以誅勒。

translations.literal: Liu Tun again urged Mi to campaign against Cao Yi and use his host to execute Le.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tun again urged Mi to march against Cao Yi and use those troops to destroy Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 於是彌使暾詣青州，令曹嶷引兵會己，而詐要勒共向青州。

translations.literal: Thereupon Mi sent Tun to Qingzhou to order Cao Yi to lead troops to join him, while falsely summoning Le to go with him toward Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mi sent Liu Tun to Qingzhou with orders for Cao Yi to bring an army to rendezvous with him, while he feigned an invitation for Shi Le to join the same expedition.

sentences.zh: 暾至東阿，為勒遊騎所獲。

translations.literal: Tun reached Dong'e and was captured by Le's raiding horse.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tun reached Dong'e, where Shi Le's scouting cavalry took him.

sentences.zh: 勒見彌與嶷書，大怒，乃殺暾。

translations.literal: When Le saw Mi's letter to Yi he was furious and killed Tun.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le read Mi's letter to Cao Yi he flew into a rage and executed Liu Tun.

sentences.zh: 彌未之知，勒伏兵襲彌，殺之，並其眾。

translations.literal: Mi did not know it; Le hid soldiers and ambushed Mi, killed him, and absorbed his host.
translations.idiomatic: Mi never learned of it: Shi Le sprang an ambush, cut him down, and absorbed his army.

sentences.zh: 張昌

translations.literal: Zhang Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang

sentences.zh: 張昌，本義陽蠻也。

translations.literal: Zhang Chang was by origin a Man of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang was a Yiyang tribesman by birth.

sentences.zh: 少為平氏縣吏，武力過人，每自占卜，言應當富貴。

translations.literal: In his youth he was a clerk in Pingshi County; his martial prowess surpassed others; he constantly divined for himself, saying he was fated for wealth and nobility.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served as a clerk in Pingshi County. He was stronger than most men, cast his own divinations, and insisted he was destined for wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 好論攻戰，儕類咸共笑之。

translations.literal: He liked to discuss attack and warfare; his fellows all laughed at him together.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to talk of battle and siege, and his companions mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 及李流寇蜀，昌潛遁半年，聚黨數千人，盜得幢麾，詐言台遣其募人討流。

translations.literal: When Li Liu raided Shu, Chang was in hiding half a year, gathered a party of several thousand men, stole banners and standards, and falsely said the court had sent him to recruit men to punish Liu.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Liu invaded Shu, Zhang Chang went underground for six months, pulled together several thousand followers, stole command banners, and pretended the central government had commissioned him to raise troops against Li Liu.

sentences.zh: 會《壬午詔書》發武勇以赴益土，號曰「壬午兵」。

translations.literal: It happened that the "Renwu edict" called for brave soldiers to go to Yizhou; they were called the "Renwu troops."
translations.idiomatic: Then came the Renwu edict drafting stalwart men for service in Yizhou—the levy known as the "Renwu host."

sentences.zh: 自天下多難，數術者云當有帝王興于江左，及此調發，人咸不樂西征，昌黨因之誑惑，百姓各不肯去。

translations.literal: Since troubles had multiplied in the realm, reckoning masters said a Son of Heaven would rise east of the Yangtze; when this levy was issued, no one wished to campaign west, and Chang's party exploited this to deceive and confuse; the people of each place were unwilling to go.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was already in turmoil, and prognosticators were claiming a true emperor would arise south of the Yangtze. When the draft order went out, no one wanted to march west; Zhang Chang's clique spread rumors and confusion, and commoners everywhere refused to leave.

sentences.zh: 而詔書催遣嚴速，所經之界停留五日者，二千石免。

translations.literal: But the edict urged departure with stern haste: wherever the levy passed, if anyone halted five days, the two-thousand-picul official was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The edict demanded brutal speed: any district where conscripts lingered five days would cost its governor his post.

sentences.zh: 由是郡縣官長皆躬出驅逐，輾轉不遠，屯聚而為劫掠。

translations.literal: Hence county and commandery magistrates all went out in person to drive people on; they circulated not far, massed together, and turned to robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates took to the roads themselves to herd the levies along; people milled about just beyond their homes, banded together, and turned to pillage.

sentences.zh: 是歲江夏大稔，流人就食者數千口。

translations.literal: That year Jiangxia had a great harvest; several thousand mouths of refugees came for food.
translations.idiomatic: That year Jiangxia enjoyed a bumper crop, and thousands of displaced families drifted in seeking food.

sentences.zh: ，昌于安陸縣石岩山屯聚，去郡八十里，諸流人及避戍役者多往從之。

translations.literal: Zhang Chang encamped at Stone Cliff Mountain in Anlu County, eighty li from the commandery seat; many refugees and men avoiding garrison duty went to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang made his stand on Stone Cliff Mountain in Anlu County, eighty li from the prefectural seat; refugees and draft evaders flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 昌乃易姓名為李辰。

translations.literal: Chang then changed his name to Li Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He adopted the alias Li Chen.

sentences.zh: 太守弓欽遣軍就討，輒為所破。

translations.literal: Prefect Gong Qin sent troops to attack him and was repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Gong Qin sent troops against him and was beaten back every time.

sentences.zh: 昌徒眾日多，遂來攻郡。

translations.literal: Chang's followers grew daily more numerous, and he came to attack the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His following swelled until he marched on the commandery seat.

sentences.zh: 欽出戰，大敗，乃將家南奔沔口。

translations.literal: Qin went out to fight, was routed badly, and fled south with his family to Hankou.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Qin gave battle, suffered a crushing defeat, and fled south with his household toward Hankou.

sentences.zh: 鎮南大將軍、新野王歆遣騎督靳滿討昌於隨郡西，大戰，滿敗走，昌得其器杖，據有江夏，即其府庫。

translations.literal: The great general who guards the south, Sima Xin the Prince of Xinye, sent the horse supervisor Jin Man to punish Chang west of Sui commandery; they fought a great battle, Man fled in defeat, Chang acquired his weapons, occupied Jiangxia, and took its government storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xin, prince of Xinye and general who guards the south, dispatched cavalry commander Jin Man against Zhang Chang west of Sui. After a major engagement Jin Man broke and ran; Zhang Chang seized his arms, took Jiangxia, and helped himself to the government granaries and arsenals.

sentences.zh: 造妖言云：「當有聖人出。

translations.literal: He spread sorcerous words: "A sage is going to appear."
translations.idiomatic: He circulated prophecies that a sage would soon appear.

sentences.zh: 」山都縣吏丘沈遇于江夏，昌名之為聖人，盛車服出迎之，立為天子，置百官。

translations.literal: " Qiu Shen, a clerk of Shandu County, encountered him in Jiangxia; Chang called him the sage, welcomed him with lavish carriages and robes, set him up as Son of Heaven, and established the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangxia he encountered Qiu Shen, a clerk from Shandu County, hailed him as that sage, received him with full pomp, enthroned him as emperor, and installed a full bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 沈易姓名為劉尼，稱漢後，以昌為相國，昌兄味為車騎將軍，弟放廣武將軍，各領兵。

translations.literal: Shen changed his name to Liu Ni, claimed descent from the Han, made Chang chancellor of state, Chang's elder brother Wei chariot and cavalry general, and younger brother Fang General Who Expands Martial might, each commanding troops.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shen restyled himself Liu Ni, claimed Han imperial descent, named Zhang Chang chancellor of state, Zhang Wei chariot and cavalry general, and Zhang Fang general who expands martial might—each commanding troops of his own.

sentences.zh: 于石岩中作宮殿，又於岩上織竹為鳥形，衣以五彩，聚肉於其傍，眾鳥群集，詐云鳳皇降，又言珠袍、玉璽、鐵券、金鼓自然而至。

translations.literal: In a stone cliff they built palace halls; moreover above the cliff they wove bamboo into bird shapes, clothed them in five colors, heaped meat beside them, and when many birds gathered in flocks they falsely claimed the phoenix had descended; they also said pearl robes, jade seals, iron tallies, and golden drums had arrived of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They carved palace halls into the cliff face, then wove bamboo birds on the heights, painted them in five colors, and piled meat nearby so flocks would gather; they called it a phoenix's descent and spread word that pearl robes, jade seals, iron tallies, and golden drums had appeared by heaven's gift.

sentences.zh: 乃下赦書，建元神鳳，郊祀、服色依漢故事。

translations.literal: They then issued an amnesty, adopted the reign title Shenfeng, and for suburban sacrifices and dress followed Han precedent.
translations.idiomatic: They proclaimed an amnesty, took the reign title Divine Phoenix, and patterned suburban rites and court dress on Han practice.

sentences.zh: 其有不應其募者，族誅。

translations.literal: Whoever did not answer their recruitment was exterminated to the clan.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who refused their summons faced extermination of his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 又流訛言云：「江淮已南當圖反逆，官軍大起，悉誅討之。

translations.literal: Again wandering rumors said: "South of the Yangtze and Huai they are plotting rebellion; the government armies are mustering in force and will kill and punish everyone."
translations.idiomatic: Fresh rumors claimed that south of the Yangtze and Huai a rebellion was brewing, imperial troops were massing, and every household would be put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 」群小互相扇動，人情惶懼，江沔間一時猋起，豎牙旗，鳴鼓角，以應昌，旬月之間，眾至三萬，皆以絳科頭，撍之以毛。

translations.literal: " Petty men egged one another on; hearts were fearful; along the Yangtze and Han in one surge they rose, planted spears' banners, sounded drums and horns to answer Chang, and within a month they were thirty thousand strong—all wore red forehead bands and tucked in hair with feathers.
translations.idiomatic: Agitators fanned the panic; along the Yangtze and Han people rose in a single rush, raised battle flags, and beat drums in answer to Zhang Chang. Within weeks he had thirty thousand men, all with crimson headbands and feathers stuck in their hair.

sentences.zh: 江夏、義陽士庶莫不從之，惟江夏舊姓江安令王傴、秀才呂蕤不從。

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners of Jiangxia and Yiyang all followed him except the old surname of Jiangxia—Wang Ju, magistrate of Jiang'an, and the licentiate Lu Rui—who did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and commoners across Jiangxia and Yiyang fell in behind him—except Wang Ju, magistrate of Jiang'an, and the student Lu Rui, old Jiangxia families who held out.

sentences.zh: 昌以三公位徵之，傴、蕤密將宗室並奔汝南，投豫州刺史劉喬。

translations.literal: Chang summoned them to the three dukes' rank; Ju and Rui secretly led their clans and all fled to Runan to join Inspector of Yu Province Liu Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang offered them posts among the three dukes; Wang Ju and Lu Rui slipped away with their kin to Runan and placed themselves under Liu Qiao, inspector of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 鄉人期思令李權、常安令吳鳳、孝廉吳暢糾合善士，得五百餘家，追隨傴等，不豫妖逆。

translations.literal: Li Quan, magistrate of Qisi, Wu Feng, magistrate of Chang'an, and the recommended scholar Wu Chang, fellow townsmen, gathered good men, obtained more than five hundred households, followed Ju and the others, and did not join the sorcery and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Their neighbors—Li Quan, magistrate of Qisi, Wu Feng, magistrate of Chang'an, and the filial and incorrupt nominee Wu Chang—rallied more than five hundred households of respectable families and followed Wang Ju, refusing to join the sorcerous revolt.

sentences.zh: 新野王歆上言：「妖賊張昌、劉尼妄稱神聖，犬羊萬計，絳頭毛面，挑刀走戟，其鋒不可當。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xinye, Xin, memorialized: "The sorcerer-rebels Zhang Chang and Liu Ni falsely call themselves sacred; they number like dogs and sheep in the tens of thousands, red-headed and hairy-faced, brandishing knives and running with halberds; their impetus cannot be withstood."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xin, prince of Xinye, reported: "The rebel sorcerers Zhang Chang and Liu Ni pose as heaven's chosen; they swarm like beasts—tens of thousands with crimson headbands and bristling weapons—and their charge cannot be held."

sentences.zh: 請台敕諸軍，三道救助。

translations.literal: I beg the court to order the armies to relieve us along three routes."
translations.idiomatic: I ask the court to order relief along three routes."

sentences.zh: 」於是劉喬率諸軍據汝南以禦賊，前將軍趙驤領精卒八千據宛，助平南將軍羊伊距守。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Liu Qiao led the various armies to hold Runan against the rebels; the front general Zhao Xiang led eight thousand picked troops to hold Wan and assist the General Who Pacifies the South, Yang Yi, in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiao then drew up his forces in Runan to block the rebels; Zhao Xiang, front general, took eight thousand elite troops to Wan to help Yang Yi, general who pacifies the south, hold the line.

sentences.zh: 昌遣其將軍黃林為大都督，率二萬人向豫州，前驅李宮欲掠取汝水居人，喬遣將軍李楊逆擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Chang sent his general Huang Lin as grand commander with twenty thousand men toward Yu Province; the vanguard Li Gong wished to plunder the people living along the Ru River; Qiao sent General Li Yang to meet him in attack and routed him badly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang named Huang Lin supreme commander and sent twenty thousand men into Yu Province. Vanguard Li Gong tried to strip the settlements along the Ru; Liu Qiao ordered Li Yang to intercept him and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 林等東攻弋陽，太守梁桓嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Lin and the others attacked east toward Yiyang; Administrator Liang Huan drew in his walls and held fast.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Lin thrust east against Yiyang, but Administrator Liang Huan barred his gates and held firm.

sentences.zh: 又遣其將馬武破武昌，害太守，昌自領其眾。

translations.literal: He again sent his general Ma Wu to break Wuchang, killed the prefect, and Chang personally led those forces.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Ma Wu to take Wuchang and kill its prefect, then placed the garrison under his own command.

sentences.zh: 西攻宛，破趙驤，害羊伊。

translations.literal: He attacked Wan to the west, defeated Zhao Xiang, and killed Yang Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He struck west at Wan, shattered Zhao Xiang's army, and slew Yang Yi.

sentences.zh: 進攻襄陽，害新野王歆。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Xiangyang and killed Sima Xin, Prince of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed on to Xiangyang and killed Sima Xin, the prince of Xinye.

sentences.zh: 昌別率石冰東破江、揚二州，偽置守長。

translations.literal: Chang separately led Shi Bing east to break Jiang and Yang provinces and falsely appointed prefects and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile he sent Shi Bing east to overrun Jiang and Yang and set up puppet prefects and county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 當時五州之境皆畏逼從逆。

translations.literal: At that time within the borders of five provinces all feared coercion and followed the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Across five provinces people submitted to the rebels out of terror.

sentences.zh: 又遣其將陳貞、陳蘭、張甫等攻長沙、湘東、零陵諸郡。

translations.literal: He again sent his generals Chen Zhen, Chen Lan, Zhang Fu, and others to attack Changsha, Xiangdong, and Lingling commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Chen Zhen, Chen Lan, Zhang Fu, and others against Changsha, Xiangdong, Lingling, and neighboring commanderies.

sentences.zh: 昌雖跨帶五州，樹立牧守，皆桀盜小人而無禁制，但以劫掠為務，人情漸離。

translations.literal: Although Chang spanned five provinces and set up governors and prefects, they were all violent thief petty men without restraint and took plunder as their sole business; popular feeling gradually turned away.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang straddled five provinces and named governors and prefects, but they were nothing more than violent bandits who answered to no law and lived by looting, so the people steadily abandoned him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，詔以甯朔將軍、領南蠻校尉劉弘鎮宛，弘遣司馬陶侃、參軍蒯桓、皮初等率眾討昌於竟陵，劉喬又遣將軍李楊、督護尹奉總兵向江夏。

translations.literal: That year an edict appointed Liu Hong, General Who Pacifies the North and concurrent colonel of the southern Man, to garrison Wan; Hong sent his marshal Tao Kan, aides Kuai Huan and Pi Chu, and others to lead hosts to punish Chang at Jingling, and Liu Qiao again sent General Li Yang and commandant protector Yin Feng with combined forces toward Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: That year the court named Liu Hong—general who calms the north and colonel of the southern tribes—military governor at Wan. Liu Hong dispatched Tao Kan as his marshal, with staff officers Kuai Huan and Pi Chu, to campaign against Zhang Chang at Jingling, while Liu Qiao sent Li Yang and the commandant protector Yin Feng toward Jiangxia with a joint force.

sentences.zh: 侃等與昌苦戰累日，大破之，納降萬計，昌乃沈竄於下俊山。

translations.literal: Kan and the others fought bitterly with Chang for many days, routed him badly, accepted surrenders numbering in the tens of thousands, and Chang then sank into hiding in Mount Xiajun.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan's men fought Zhang Chang day after day until they broke his army, accepted tens of thousands of surrenders, and drove him into the fastness of Mount Xiajun.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，乃擒之，傳首京師，同黨並夷三族。

translations.literal: The next autumn they captured him, sent his head to the capital, and his accomplices were exterminated to the third degree of kin.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn he was taken alive; his head went to the capital, and his followers were extirpated to the third degree of kinship.

sentences.zh: 陳敏

translations.literal: Chen Min.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min

sentences.zh: 陳敏，字令通，廬江人也。

translations.literal: Chen Min, courtesy name Lingtong, was a man of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min, whose courtesy name was Lingtong, came from Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 少有幹能，以郡廉吏補尚書倉部令史。

translations.literal: In youth he had competence and ability; as an honest clerk of the commandery he was appointed clerk in the granary section of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He showed administrative talent early and, starting as a trusted clerk in his home commandery, rose to a clerkship in the Board of Revenue's granary bureau.

sentences.zh: 及趙王篡逆，三王起義兵，久屯不散，京師倉廩空虛，敏建議曰：「南方米穀皆積數十年，時將欲腐敗，而不漕運以濟中州，非所以救患周急也。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Zhao usurped in rebellion, the three princes raised righteous armies and encamped long without dispersing; the capital's granaries were empty, and Min proposed: "The rice and grain of the south have been stored for decades and are about to rot, yet we do not transport them by canal to relieve the central plain—this is not the way to save distress and aid urgency."
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Lun seized power and the three princes raised loyalist armies, the siege lines around the capital held so long that the granaries ran dry. Chen Min proposed: "Grain in the south has sat in store for decades and is spoiling, yet we ship none north by canal to feed the heartland—that is no way to answer a crisis."

sentences.zh: 」朝廷從之，以敏為合肥度支，遷廣陵度支。

translations.literal: " The court followed this and appointed Min granary intendant at Hefei, then transferred him to granary intendant at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed, named him transport intendant at Hefei, and soon moved him to the same post at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 張昌之亂，遣其將石冰等趣壽春，都督劉准憂惶計無所出。

translations.literal: During Zhang Chang's rebellion, Chang sent his generals Shi Bing and others to hurry toward Shouchun; the area commander Liu Zhun was anxious and frightened and had no plan.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhang Chang's uprising, Chang sent Shi Bing and others racing toward Shouchun, leaving the regional commander Liu Zhun frantic and without a strategy.

sentences.zh: 時敏統大軍在壽春，謂准曰：「此等本不樂遠戍，故逼迫成賊。

translations.literal: At that time Min commanded a great army at Shouchun and said to Zhun, "These men originally did not wish to garrison far away, hence coercion made them into bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min held a large force at Shouchun and told Liu Zhun, "Those men never wanted to be shipped off to distant garrisons; you drove them into rebellion."

sentences.zh: 烏合之眾，其勢易離。

translations.literal: A rabble-joined host—its situation is easy to split.
translations.idiomatic: A mob like that can be broken apart without much trouble.

sentences.zh: 敏請合率運兵，公分配眾力，破之必矣。

translations.literal: Min requests to combine and lead the transport troops; if you divide and assign the strength of the host, breaking them is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Let me merge the transport corps with yours and divide our strength wisely—we can shatter them.

sentences.zh: 」准乃益敏兵擊之，破吳弘、石冰等，敏遂乘勝逐北，戰數十合。

translations.literal: " Zhun thereupon reinforced Min's troops to strike them, defeated Wu Hong, Shi Bing, and others, and Min then rode victory to pursue the routed, fighting several tens of engagements.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhun gave Chen Min reinforcements; they crushed Wu Hong, Shi Bing, and their allies, and Chen Min pressed the pursuit through dozens of skirmishes.

sentences.zh: 時冰眾十倍，敏以少擊眾，每戰皆克，遂至揚州。

translations.literal: At that time Bing's host was tenfold; Min used the few to strike the many and prevailed in every battle, and thus reached Yang province.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bing outnumbered him ten to one, yet Chen Min beat him in fight after fight and fought his way clear to Yang province.

sentences.zh: 回討徐州賊封雲，雲將張統斬雲降。

translations.literal: He turned back to punish the Xu province bandit Feng Yun; Yun's general Zhang Tong beheaded Yun and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He wheeled about to deal with the Xu bandit Feng Yun; Feng's officer Zhang Tong cut off Feng's head and came over to the government side.

sentences.zh: 敏以功為廣陵相。

translations.literal: Min became administrator of Guangling on account of merit.
translations.idiomatic: For these services he was named administrator of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 時惠帝幸長安，四方交爭，敏遂有割據江東之志。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Hui was at Chang'an and the four quarters struggled against one another; Min then had the ambition to carve out and hold the lands east of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: With Emperor Hui stranded in Chang'an and the realm tearing itself apart, Chen Min began to dream of ruling the southeast.

sentences.zh: 其父聞之，怒曰：「滅我門者，必此兒也！

translations.literal: His father heard of it and said in anger, "The one who will destroy our house—surely it is this boy!"
translations.idiomatic: His father heard and raged, "This son will be the death of our whole line!"

sentences.zh: 」父亡，去職。

translations.literal: " When his father died, he left office.
translations.idiomatic: When the old man died, Chen Min resigned his post.

sentences.zh: 東海王越當西迎大駕，承制起敏為右將軍、假節、前鋒都督，致書於敏曰：

translations.literal: Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, was about to go west to welcome the great chariot; acting on imperial authority he raised Min to General of the Right, credential-bearing, and front vanguard area commander, and sent Min a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue, prince of Donghai, prepared to ride west to escort the emperor home. Acting with imperial mandate he recalled Chen Min as general of the right, gave him the tally of command, and named him commander of the vanguard, and he sent him this letter:

sentences.zh: 將軍建謀富國，則有大漕之勳。

translations.literal: When the general devised plans to enrich the state, there was then the merit of great canal transport.
translations.idiomatic: You devised the grain policy that enriched the state—that was the great transport achievement.

sentences.zh: 及遭冰昌之亂，則首率義徒，以寡敵眾。

translations.literal: When you encountered the Bing and Chang rebellion, you were first to lead righteous followers, using the few against the many.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Bing and Zhang Chang rose, you were the first to rally loyal militia and pit a small force against a host.

sentences.zh: 外無強兵之援，內無運籌之侶，隻身挺立，雄略從橫，擢奇謀于馬首，奪靈計于臨危，金聲振于江外，精光赫于揚楚。

translations.literal: Without strong troops to aid you from without, without partners to plan within, you stood alone; heroic strategy ranged across the field; you pulled forth strange schemes at the horse's head and seized clever plans in the face of peril; your metal voice shook beyond the Yangtze, your keen brilliance blazed in Yang and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: You had no crack reinforcements from outside, no co-conspirators within—yet you held the line alone, bold strategy flashing on every side, conjuring stratagems in the saddle and snatching victory from the jaws of defeat until your name rang beyond the Yangtze and your fame lit up Yang and Chu.

sentences.zh: 攻堅陷險，三十餘戰，師徒無虧，勍敵自滅。

translations.literal: You assaulted hard points and took perilous places, fought more than thirty battles, your army without loss, and the mighty foe destroyed itself.
translations.idiomatic: You stormed strongholds and defiles, fought more than thirty actions without losing your own ranks, and watched the enemy destroy themselves.

sentences.zh: 五州復全，苞茅入貢，豈非將軍之功力哉！

translations.literal: Five provinces were restored whole, bao-mao tribute entered—is this not the general's labor of merit!
translations.idiomatic: Five provinces were made whole again and ritual tribute flowed to the throne—surely that rests on your exertions!

sentences.zh: 今羯賊屯結，遊魂河濟，鼠伏雉竄，藏匿陳留，始欲奸盜，終圖不軌。

translations.literal: Now the Jie bandits mass and bind; wandering souls are by the Yellow River and Ji; they crouch like rats and scatter like pheasants, hiding in Chenliu; at first they wished to steal and rob, in the end they plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Today Jie raiders swarm along the Yellow River and the Ji, skulking like rats, scattering like startled fowl, holed up in Chenliu—petty thieves at first, would-be usurpers at last.

sentences.zh: 將軍孫吳之術既明，已試之功先著，孤與將軍情分特隆，想割草土之哀，抑難居之思，舍絰執戈，來恤國難。

translations.literal: The general's Sun-Wu art of war is already clear, tested merit stands foremost; I and the general have especially lofty feeling—I hope you will cut short the grief of straw and earth, restrain thoughts hard to bear, cast aside mourning sash and take up spear, and come to relieve the state's distress.
translations.idiomatic: You have mastered the military methods of Sun Wu, and your record proves it. You and I are bound by uncommon trust. I urge you to set aside the sorrows of bereavement, master the reluctance to leave home, lay down mourning garb and take up arms, and march to the nation's rescue.

sentences.zh: 天子遠巡，鑾輿未反，引領東眷，有懷山陵。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven tours far; the imperial carriage has not returned; stretching my neck I gaze east with longing, my heart on the hills and tombs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is still far from the capital; the imperial train has not turned home. I look east with aching heart, thinking of the ancestral shrines.

sentences.zh: 當憑將軍戮力，王輅有旋。

translations.literal: We must rely on the general's combined strength so the royal chariot may return.
translations.idiomatic: We depend on your utmost effort to bring the imperial chariot home.

sentences.zh: 將軍率將所領，承書風發，米布軍資，惟將軍所運。

translations.literal: The general shall lead what he commands; on receiving this letter set out like the wind; rice, cloth, and military supplies—only what the general transports.
translations.idiomatic: Lead the troops under your command: the moment this letter reaches you, march like the wind. Grain, cloth, and materiel will follow whatever route you open.

sentences.zh: 時越討豫州刺史劉喬，敏引兵會之，與越俱敗于蕭。

translations.literal: At that time Yue was punishing Inspector of Yu Province Liu Qiao; Min led troops to join him, and with Yue was defeated together at Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yue moved against Liu Qiao, inspector of Yu, Chen Min brought his army to the rendezvous; both were beaten at Xiao.

sentences.zh: 敏因中國大亂，遂請東歸，收兵據曆陽。

translations.literal: Min, because the central plain was in great chaos, then requested to return east, gathered troops, and held Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: With the heartland in chaos, Chen Min asked leave to go east, regrouped his forces, and seized Liyang.

sentences.zh: 會吳王常侍甘卓自洛至，教卓假稱皇太弟命，拜敏為揚州刺史，並假江東首望顧榮等四十餘人為將軍、郡守，榮並偽從之。

translations.literal: It happened that Gan Zhuo, attendant-in-ordinary of the Prince of Wu, came from Luoyang; Min instructed Zhuo falsely to proclaim orders in the name of the imperial younger brother, appointed Min Inspector of Yang Province, and falsely appointed more than forty leading notables east of the Yangtze such as Gu Rong as generals and prefects; Rong and the rest feigned compliance.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Zhuo, an attendant of the prince of Wu, arrived from Luoyang. Chen Min told him to forge orders in the name of the crown prince and appoint Chen Min inspector of Yang—and to hand out bogus commissions as generals and prefects to more than forty Jiangdong notables, Gu Rong among them. They accepted with false obedience.

sentences.zh: 敏為息娶卓女，遂相為表裏。

translations.literal: Min married a son to Zhuo's daughter, and thus they became inner and outer to each other.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min married his son to Gan Zhuo's daughter, and the two men became inseparable allies.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史劉機、丹陽太守王廣等皆棄官奔走。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yang Province Liu Ji, Administrator of Danyang Wang Guang, and others all abandoned office and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji, the sitting inspector of Yang, Wang Guang, administrator of Danyang, and others threw down their seals and ran.

sentences.zh: 敏弟昶知顧榮等有貳心，勸敏殺之，敏不從。

translations.literal: Min's younger brother Chang knew Gu Rong and others had two hearts and urged Min to kill them; Min did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min's brother Chen Chang saw that Gu Rong and company were playing a double game and begged Chen Min to execute them; Chen Min refused.

sentences.zh: 昶將精兵數萬據烏江，弟恢率錢端等南寇江州，刺史應邈奔走，弟斌東略諸郡，遂據有吳越之地。

translations.literal: Chang led several tens of thousands of picked troops and held Wujiang; younger brother Hui led Qian Duan and others to raid Jiang Province south; Inspector Ying Miao fled; younger brother Bin raided the commanderies east; thus they occupied the lands of Wu and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Chang took tens of thousands of veterans to Wujiang; Chen Hui drove south into Jiangzhou with Qian Duan and routed Inspector Ying Miao; Chen Min's brother Chen Bin swept the eastern commanderies until the brothers held Wu and Yue.

sentences.zh: 敏命寮佐以己為都督江東軍事、大司馬、楚公，封十郡，加九錫，列上尚書，稱自江入河，奉迎鑾駕。

translations.literal: Min ordered his staff to take himself as area commander of Jiangdong military affairs, grand marshal, Duke of Chu, enfeoffing ten commanderies, adding the nine bestowals, listing it upward to the Shangshu, claiming to enter the Yellow River from the Yangtze and welcome the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He had his aides proclaim him commander of all Jiangdong forces, grand marshal, and duke of Chu with ten commanderies and the full nine imperial honors, filed the roster with the imperial secretariat, and announced a march from the Yangtze to the Yellow River to escort the emperor.

sentences.zh: 東海王軍諮祭酒華譚聞敏自相署置，而顧榮等並江東首望，悉受敏官爵，乃遺榮等書曰：

translations.literal: Hua Tan, libationer of the Prince of Donghai's army staff, heard that Min had appointed himself and that Gu Rong and others, together the foremost notables east of the Yangtze, had all accepted Min's offices and noble ranks, and therefore sent Rong and the others a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tan, chief adviser on Sima Yue's staff, learned that Chen Min had seized titles for himself while Gu Rong and the other leading men of Jiangdong had taken his commissions; he wrote them this letter:

sentences.zh: 石冰之亂，朝廷錄敏微功，故加越次之禮，授以上將之任，庶有韓盧一噬之效。

translations.literal: During Shi Bing's rebellion the court recorded Min's slight merit, therefore added him a courtesy beyond the ordinary, entrusted him with a senior general's charge, hoping for the effect of Han Lu's single bite.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Bing rebelled, the court rewarded Chen Min's modest service with honors beyond his station and gave him a top command, hoping he would strike once like a trained hound and bring the quarry down.

sentences.zh: 而本性凶狡，素無識達，貪榮幹運，逆天而動，阻兵作威，盜據吳會，內用凶弟，外委軍吏，上負朝廷寵授之榮，下孤宰輔過禮之惠。

translations.literal: But his nature is fierce and crafty, he has never had insight or breadth, greedy for glory he meddles in transport, moves against heaven, blocks armies and makes a show of power, steals and holds Wu and Hui, within employs fierce younger brothers, without entrusts to military clerks; above he betrays the court's grace of favor and appointment, below he leaves orphaned the chief minister's excessive courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he is vicious and cunning by nature, shallow and grasping; lusting after rank he hijacked the supply corps, defied heaven, waved soldiers like a toy, and seized Wu and Kuaiji. He promotes brutal brothers at home and petty officers abroad. He has betrayed the court's trust above and thrown back in your face the patronage of the regents below.

sentences.zh: 天道伐惡，人神所不祐。

translations.literal: Heaven's way punishes evil; gods and men do not bless it.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven punishes wickedness; neither spirits nor men will shield him.

sentences.zh: 雖阻長江，命危朝露。

translations.literal: Although he blocks the long Yangtze, his life is perilous as morning dew.
translations.idiomatic: Even behind the Yangtze he is as doomed as dew at sunrise.

sentences.zh: 忠節令圖，君子高行，屈節附逆，義士所恥。

translations.literal: Loyal integrity and fine design are the gentleman's high conduct; bending one's integrity to attach to rebellion is what men of principle shame.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty and honor are a gentleman's crown; groveling to a traitor is what every man of principle despises.

sentences.zh: 王蠋匹夫，志不可屈；

translations.literal: Wang Zhu was a mere commoner, yet his resolve could not be bent;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhu was only a commoner, yet his will could not be broken;

sentences.zh: 於期慕義，隕首燕庭。

translations.literal: Yu Qi admired righteousness and lost his head in Yan's court.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yuqi gave his head for a righteous cause in the palace at Yan.

sentences.zh: 況吳會仁人並受國寵，或剖符名郡，或列為近臣，而便辱身奸人之朝，降節逆叛之黨，稽顙屈膝，不亦羞乎！

translations.literal: How much more the humane men of Wu and Hui, who together received the state's favor—some split tallies in famed commanderies, some stood listed as close ministers—yet readily shame their persons in a villain's court, lower their integrity to a rebellious faction's party, knock forehead and bend knee—is it not shameful!
translations.idiomatic: You are men of Wu and Kuaiji whom the state has honored—some of you governed great commanderies, some served at the emperor's side—yet you abase yourselves in the court of a thug, bend the knee to traitors, and grovel in the dust. Have you no shame?

sentences.zh: 昔龔勝絕粒，不食莽朝；

translations.literal: Formerly Gong Sheng cut off grain and did not eat of Mang's court;
translations.idiomatic: Gong Sheng starved himself rather than serve Wang Mang;

sentences.zh: 魯連赴海，恥為秦臣。

translations.literal: Lu Zhong went to the sea, shamed to be Qin's subject.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhong threatened to drown himself rather than bow to Qin.

sentences.zh: 君子義行，同符千載，遙度雅量，豈獨是安！

translations.literal: The gentleman's righteous conduct matches a thousand years; measuring from afar your magnanimous capacity—surely it is not only this peace!
translations.idiomatic: Such deeds are the measure of a gentleman for a thousand years. Knowing your breadth of mind, I cannot believe you find this tolerable!

sentences.zh: 昔吳之武烈，稱美一代，雖奮奇宛葉，亦受折襄陽。

translations.literal: Formerly Wu's Martial Splendor was praised for a generation; although he roused wonder at Wan and Ye, he also suffered setback at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian, Wu's Martial Emperor, was the marvel of his age, yet even he was checked at Xiangyang after his feats at Wan and Ye.

sentences.zh: 討逆雄氣，志存中夏，臨江發怒，命訖丹徒。

translations.literal: The Queller of Rebellion's heroic spirit aimed to hold the central plain; facing the river he vented wrath; his life ended at Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce burned to conquer the heartland; he raged along the river—and died young at Dantu.

sentences.zh: 賴先主承運，雄謀天挺，尚內倚慈母仁明之教，外杖子布廷爭之忠，又有諸葛、顧、步、張、硃、陸、全之族，故能鞭笞百越，稱制南州。

translations.literal: Thanks to the late lord receiving the mandate, heroic plans heaven-bestowed, still within relying on a kind mother's benevolent and clear teaching, without leaning on Zibu Zhang Zhao's loyalty in court debate, and also having the clans of Zhuge, Gu, Bu, Zhang, Zhu, Lu, and Quan, therefore they could whip the Hundred Yue and claim regency in the southern province.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan inherited the mandate, heaven-touched in strategy, guided at home by a wise mother and abroad by Zhang Zhao's blunt counsel, with the houses of Zhuge, Gu, Bu, Zhang, Zhu, Lu, and Quan at his back—only thus could Wu subdue the southern tribes and rule the south.

sentences.zh: 然兵家之興，不出三世，運未盈百，歸命入臣。

translations.literal: Yet the rise of a military house does not go beyond three generations; the fortune did not fill a hundred years; they submitted and entered as subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Yet no warrior dynasty outlasts three generations; before a century was out they bowed as vassals of Jin.

sentences.zh: 今以陳敏倉部令史，七第頑冗，六品下才，欲躡桓王之高蹤，蹈大皇之絕軌，遠度諸賢，猶當未許也。

translations.literal: Now for Chen Min, a clerk in the granary section, seventh-rank stupid mediocrity, talent below the sixth rank, to wish to tread the lofty tracks of the Prince Huan and follow the supreme ruts of the Great Emperor—measuring from afar you worthy men, still ought not to consent.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min is a seventh-rank granary clerk, a mediocrity beneath the sixth grade, yet he imagines he can retrace Sun Ce's footsteps and Sun Quan's path. Measured against true worthies, that ambition should not pass.

sentences.zh: 諸君垂頭，不能建翟義之謀；

translations.literal: You gentlemen hang your heads, unable to raise Zhai Yi's plot;
translations.idiomatic: You hang your heads when you should be plotting like Zhai Yi;

sentences.zh: 而顧生俯眉，已受羈絆之辱。

translations.literal: while Master Gu lowers his brows, already suffering the humiliation of halter and bond.
translations.idiomatic: and Gu Rong has lowered his eyes only to wear the halter of shame.

sentences.zh: 皇輿東軒，行即紫館，百僚垂纓，雲翔鳳闕，廟勝之謨，潛運帷幄。

translations.literal: The imperial chariot's east pavilion, proceeding soon to the purple lodge; hundred officials with pendants on caps, cloud-soaring at the phoenix tower; temple-victory plans secretly move within the tent curtain.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial train is turning east toward the capital; officials throng the phoenix towers; victory is already being charted in the inner councils.

sentences.zh: 然後發荊州武旅，順流東下，徐州銳鋒，南據堂邑；

translations.literal: Then dispatch Jing Province's martial host, flow east downcurrent; Xu Province's sharp point, seize Tangyi to the south;
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou's armies will sweep downriver; Xuzhou's spearhead will thrust south to Tangyi;

sentences.zh: 征東勁卒，耀威曆陽；

translations.literal: the east-campaigning crack troops display might at Liyang;
translations.idiomatic: the eastern expedition's veterans will flash steel at Liyang;

sentences.zh: 飛橋越橫江之津，泛舟涉瓜步之渚；

translations.literal: flying bridges cross the Hengjiang ford; boats float to ford Guabu islet;
translations.idiomatic: flying bridges will span the Hengjiang crossing; fleets will beach at Guabu;

sentences.zh: 威震丹陽，擒寇建鄴，而諸賢何顏見中州之士邪！

translations.literal: might shakes Danyang, bandits are seized at Jianye—yet you worthy men, what face to see the gentlemen of the central plain!
translations.idiomatic: their shock wave will roll through Danyang and take the rebels at Jianye—how will you face the scholars of the north then?

sentences.zh: 小寇隔津，音符道闊，引領南望，情存舊懷。

translations.literal: A petty bandit blocks the ford; music-signs and the way are wide; stretching the neck gazing south, feeling preserves old cherishing.
translations.idiomatic: A petty rebel holds the crossing while letters grow scarce; I gaze south, thinking of old friendships.

sentences.zh: 忠義之人，何世蔑有！

translations.literal: Men of loyalty and righteousness—in what age are they lacking!
translations.idiomatic: Loyal hearts are never lacking in any age!

sentences.zh: 夫危而不能安，亡而不能存，將何貴乎！

translations.literal: If in peril one cannot bring peace, if in ruin one cannot preserve—what is to be valued!
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot save the realm from peril or preserve it from ruin, what good are you?

sentences.zh: 永長宿德，情所素重；

translations.literal: Yongchang of long-standing virtue, whom feeling has always esteemed;
translations.idiomatic: To Yongchang, whose virtue you have always honored;

sentences.zh: 彥先垂發，分著金石；

translations.literal: Yanxian's hanging hair, distinction carved in metal and stone;
translations.idiomatic: to Yanxian, whose name should be cut in bronze and stone;

sentences.zh: 公胄早交，恩紀特隆；

translations.literal: Gongzhou's early friendship, favor and bond especially lofty;
translations.idiomatic: to Gongzhou, your friend of many years;

sentences.zh: 令伯義聲，親好密結。

translations.literal: Lingbo's righteous fame, intimate good ties closely bound.
translations.idiomatic: to Lingbo, whose integrity rings clear—I speak as one close to you all.

sentences.zh: 上欲與諸賢效冀紫宸，建功帝籍。

translations.literal: Above I wish with you worthy men to strive toward the Purple Forbidden City and establish merit on the imperial register.
translations.idiomatic: I had hoped we might serve together within the purple palace and win a place on the rolls of honor.

sentences.zh: 如其不爾，亦可泛舟河渭，擊楫清歌。

translations.literal: If it is not thus, one may also float boats on the He and Wei, beat the oar and sing a clear song.
translations.idiomatic: If not, we might still drift on the Yellow and Wei, tapping the oars and singing—free men on the river.

sentences.zh: 何為辱身小寇之手，以蹈逆亂之禍乎！

translations.literal: Why shame your persons in a petty bandit's hands, to tread into the calamity of rebellion and disorder!
translations.idiomatic: Why soil yourselves in the grip of a petty bandit and stumble into treason?

sentences.zh: 昔為同志，今已殊域；

translations.literal: Formerly we were same purpose; now already different regions;
translations.idiomatic: Once we were comrades; now a whole realm lies between us;

sentences.zh: 往為一體，今成異身。

translations.literal: In the past we were one body; now we have become different persons.
translations.idiomatic: once we were one body, now we stand as strangers.

sentences.zh: 瞻江長歎，非子誰思！

translations.literal: Gazing on the Yangtze I sigh long—if not you, whom do I think of!
translations.idiomatic: I stare across the Yangtze and sigh—who else should I long for but you?

sentences.zh: 願圖良策，以存嘉謀也。

translations.literal: I hope you will plan good strategy, to preserve fine counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Find a worthy plan, I beg you, and keep faith with your better selves.

sentences.zh: 敏凡才無遠略，一旦據有江東，刑政無章，不為英俊所服，且子弟凶暴，所在為患。

translations.literal: Min was ordinary talent without far-reaching strategy; once he held Jiangdong, punishments and government lacked order, he was not obeyed by the talented, and moreover his sons and younger kin were fierce and violent, becoming a scourge wherever they were.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min was a mediocrity with no long view. Once he seized Jiangdong his rule was lawless, the gentry despised him, and his kinsmen terrorized every district they touched.

sentences.zh: 周玘、顧榮之徒常懼禍敗，又得譚書，皆有慚色。

translations.literal: Zhou Qi, Gu Rong, and their sort constantly feared disaster and defeat; when they again obtained Tan's letter, all had ashamed expressions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qi, Gu Rong, and their circle had long feared a reckoning; Hua Tan's letter left them red-faced.

sentences.zh: 玘、榮遣使密報征東大將軍劉准遣兵臨江，己為內應。

translations.literal: Qi and Rong sent envoys secretly to report to Grand General Who Conquers the East Liu Zhun to dispatch troops to the Yangtze, they themselves being inner responders.
translations.idiomatic: They sent word in secret to Liu Zhun, grand general who conquers the east, asking him to bring troops to the river while they acted as fifth columnists.

sentences.zh: 准遣揚州刺史劉機、甯遠將軍衡彥等出曆陽，敏使弟昶及將軍錢廣次烏江以距之，又遣弟閎為曆陽太守，戍牛渚。

translations.literal: Zhun sent Inspector of Yang Province Liu Ji, General Who Keeps the Distance Heng Yan, and others out of Liyang; Min sent younger brother Chang and General Qian Guang to camp at Wujiang to oppose them, and again sent younger brother Hong as administrator of Liyang to garrison Niuzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhun ordered Liu Ji, inspector of Yang, and Heng Yan, general who keeps the distance, out from Liyang. Chen Min sent Chen Chang and Qian Guang to Wujiang to block them and named another brother, Chen Hong, administrator of Liyang to hold Niuzhu.

sentences.zh: 錢廣家在長城，玘鄉人也，玘潛使圖昶。

translations.literal: Qian Guang's home was in Changcheng; he was Qi fellow townsman; Qi secretly had him plot against Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Guang came from Changcheng, Zhou Qi's home district; Zhou Qi secretly set him to turn against Chen Chang.

sentences.zh: 廣遣其屬何康、錢象投募送白事於昶，昶俯頭視書，康揮刀斬之，稱州下已殺敏，敢有動者誅三族，吹角為內應。

translations.literal: Guang sent his subordinates He Kang and Qian Xiang to join recruitment and deliver a white document to Chang; Chang bent his head to read the document, Kang swung a blade and beheaded him, declared that below the province they had already killed Min, whoever dared move would be exterminated to three clans, and blew the horn as inner response.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Guang sent He Kang and Qian Xiang under cover of enlistment with a routine memo for Chen Chang. When Chang lowered his head to read, He Kang struck off his head. They proclaimed that Chen Min was already dead at the provincial capital, threatened death to the third degree on anyone who stirred, and sounded the horn as the agreed signal.

sentences.zh: 廣先勒兵在硃雀橋，陳兵水南、玘、榮又說甘卓，卓遂背敏。

translations.literal: Guang first restrained troops at Zhuque Bridge, arrayed troops south of the water; Qi and Rong again persuaded Gan Zhuo, and Zhuo thereupon turned against Min.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Guang had already drawn up his men at the Zhuque Bridge and south of the river. Zhou Qi and Gu Rong won over Gan Zhuo, who then broke with Chen Min.

sentences.zh: 敏率萬餘人將與卓戰，未獲濟，榮以白羽扇麾之，敏眾潰散。

translations.literal: Min led more than ten thousand men about to fight Zhuo, had not yet managed to cross, Rong with a white feather fan signaled them, and Min's host scattered in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min marched over ten thousand men against Gan Zhuo but never reached the crossing. Gu Rong stepped forward and waved a white feather fan; Chen Min's army melted away.

sentences.zh: 敏單騎東奔至江乘，為義兵所斬，母及妻子皆伏誅，於是會稽諸郡並殺敏諸弟無遺焉。

translations.literal: Min fled east alone on horse to Jiangcheng, was beheaded by righteous troops, his mother, wife, and children all were executed, and thereupon the commanderies of Kuaiji together killed Min's younger brothers leaving none.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min fled alone east to Jiangcheng, where loyalist militia cut him down. His mother, wife, and children were put to death, and the Kuaiji commanderies hunted his brothers to extinction.

sentences.zh: 王如

translations.literal: Wang Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ru

sentences.zh: 王如，京兆新豐人也。

translations.literal: Wang Ru was a man of Xinfeng in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ru came from Xinfeng in the Jingzhao region.

sentences.zh: 初為州武吏，遇亂流移至宛。

translations.literal: At first he was a military clerk of the province; encountering chaos he drifted and moved to Wan.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a clerical soldier in the provincial army, then drifted with the refugees to Wan.

sentences.zh: 時諸流人有詔並遣還鄉里，如以關中荒殘，不願歸。

translations.literal: At that time the various refugees had an edict all to be sent back to their home villages; Ru because Guanzhong was desolate and ruined was unwilling to return.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the displaced households home, but Wang Ru refused—the Guanzhong he had left was a wasteland.

sentences.zh: 征南將軍山簡、南中郎將杜蕤各遣兵送之，而促期令發。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the South Shan Jian and General of the Central Army of the South Du Rui each sent troops to escort them, but pressed the deadline ordering departure.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Jian, general who conquers the south, and Du Rui, general of the central army of the south, each sent soldiers to herd them along, driving mercilessly toward the departure date.

sentences.zh: 如遂潛結諸無賴少年，夜襲二軍，破之。

translations.literal: Ru thereupon secretly joined various worthless youths, night-attacked the two armies, and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ru secretly rallied the young ruffians among the refugees, fell on both escort forces by night, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 杜蕤悉眾擊如，戰于涅陽，蕤軍大敗。

translations.literal: Du Rui used all his host to strike Ru, fought at Nieyang, and Rui's army was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Du Rui threw his whole command against Wang Ru at Nieyang and suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 山簡不能禦，移屯夏口，如又破襄城。

translations.literal: Shan Jian could not withstand him, moved camp to Xiakou, and Ru again broke Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Jian could not contain him and pulled back to Xiakou; Wang Ru went on to storm Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 於是南安龐實、馮翊嚴嶷、長安侯脫等各帥其党攻諸城鎮，多殺令長以應之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Pang Shi of Nan'an, Yan Yi of Fengyi, Hou Tuo of Chang'an, and others each led their parties to attack the various walled towns, killing many magistrates and chief clerks in response to him.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Shi of Nan'an, Yan Yi of Fengyi, Hou Tuo of Chang'an, and other local chiefs then stormed garrison towns, executing magistrates to rally to Wang Ru's cause.

sentences.zh: 未幾，眾至四五萬，自號大將軍，領司、雍二州牧。

translations.literal: Before long, the host reached forty or fifty thousand; he styled himself Grand General and acted as shepherd of Si and Yong provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he had forty or fifty thousand men, proclaimed himself grand general, and claimed both Si and Yong provinces.

sentences.zh: 如懼石勒之攻己也，乃厚賄於勒，結為兄弟，勒亦假其強而納之。

translations.literal: Ru feared Shi Le's attacking himself, and therefore heavily bribed Le, swearing brotherhood; Le also pretended to his strength and accepted him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ru feared Shi Le would turn on him, so he sent rich gifts and swore brotherhood; Shi Le, playing to Wang Ru's strength, accepted the alliance.

sentences.zh: 時侯脫據宛，與如不協，如說勒曰：「侯脫雖名漢臣，其實漢賊。

translations.literal: At that time Hou Tuo held Wan and was not in harmony with Ru; Ru said to Le, "Although Hou Tuo bears the name of a Han minister, in truth he is a Han bandit.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Tuo held Wan and quarreled with Wang Ru. Wang Ru told Shi Le, "Hou Tuo may call himself an officer of the court, but he is nothing but a traitor in Han clothing.

sentences.zh: 如常恐其來襲，兄宜備之。

translations.literal: Ru constantly fears he will come raiding; elder brother should guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: I live in dread of his raids—you should be on your guard, elder brother.

sentences.zh: 」勒素怒脫貳己，憚如脣齒，故不攻之。

translations.literal: " Le had always been angry that Tuo was two-minded toward himself, but feared Ru as lips and teeth, therefore did not attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le had long resented Hou Tuo's disloyalty, yet held back because Wang Ru was his shield against him.

sentences.zh: 及聞如言，甚悅，遂夜令三軍蓐食待命，雞鳴而駕，後出者斬，晨壓宛門攻之，旬有二日而克之，勒遂斬脫。

translations.literal: When he heard Ru's words he was very pleased, thereupon by night ordered the three armies to take predawn meal and await command; at cockcrow harness the chariots—whoever came out late was beheaded; at dawn pressed Wan's gate and attacked; on the twelfth day took it; Le thereupon beheaded Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Shi Le ordered his armies fed before dawn; at the first cockcrow they were to march—latecomers faced death. They stormed Wan at sunrise and broke through on the twelfth day. Shi Le executed Hou Tuo.

sentences.zh: 如於是大掠沔漢，進逼襄陽。

translations.literal: Ru thereupon plundered greatly on the Han River and pressed Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ru then ravaged the Han basin and closed in on Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 征南山簡使將趙同帥師擊之，經年不能克，智力並屈，遂嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Shan Jian, who conquers the south, sent general Zhao Tong to lead troops to strike him; a full year could not overcome him; wits and strength were both exhausted, and he then drew in his walls and held self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Jian, general who conquers the south, sent Zhao Tong against him; after a year of stalemate Shan Jian was spent and could only turtle behind the walls.

sentences.zh: 王澄帥軍赴京都，如邀擊破之。

translations.literal: Wang Cheng led an army toward the capital; Ru intercepted and struck, defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Cheng marched toward the capital, Wang Ru ambushed him and broke his army.

sentences.zh: 如連年種穀皆化為莠，軍中大饑，其黨互相攻劫，官軍進討，各相率來降。

translations.literal: For successive years Ru's planted grain all turned to tares; the army was in great famine; his party mutually attacked and robbed; government troops advanced to punish, and each in turn led his followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year his grain fields sprouted only weeds; famine gripped the camp; his followers turned on one another. As imperial columns closed in, bands surrendered piecemeal.

sentences.zh: 如計無所出，歸於王敦。

translations.literal: Ru had no plan left and submitted to Wang Dun.
translations.idiomatic: At his wits' end, Wang Ru threw himself on Wang Dun's mercy.

sentences.zh: 敦從弟棱愛如驍武，請敦配己麾下。

translations.literal: Dun's cousin Ling loved Ru's fierce martial skill and asked Dun to assign him under his own command.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun's cousin Wang Ling admired Wang Ru's fighting prowess and begged to have him under his own banner.

sentences.zh: 敦曰：「此輩虓險難蓄，汝性忌急，不能容養，更成禍端。

translations.literal: Dun said, "This sort are fierce and dangerous, hard to keep; your nature is jealous and hasty, unable to tolerate and nurture them—you will only breed disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun replied, "Men like that are wild beasts—you cannot domesticate them. You are quick-tempered and jealous; you will not indulge them, and that means trouble.

sentences.zh: 」棱固請，與之。

translations.literal: " Ling firmly requested and Dun gave him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling insisted, and Wang Dun relented.

sentences.zh: 棱置諸左右，甚加寵遇。

translations.literal: Ling placed them at his left and right and greatly favored them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling kept Wang Ru at his side and showered him with favor.

sentences.zh: 如數與敦諸將角射，屢鬥爭為過失，棱果不容而杖之，如甚以為恥。

translations.literal: Ru repeatedly competed in archery with Dun's generals and repeatedly quarreled into fault; Ling indeed could not tolerate him and caned him; Ru took it as deep shame.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ru repeatedly quarreled with Wang Dun's officers at shooting matches until Wang Ling lost patience and had him flogged—a humiliation Wang Ru could not stomach.

sentences.zh: 初，敦有不臣之跡，棱每諫之，敦常怒其異己。

translations.literal: Earlier, Dun had traces of disloyalty to the ruler; Ling always remonstrated; Dun often was angry that he differed from himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun had already shown signs of treason; Wang Ling often rebuked him, and Wang Dun resented the dissent.

sentences.zh: 及敦聞如為棱所辱，密使人激怒之，勸令殺棱。

translations.literal: When Dun heard that Ru had been humiliated by Ling, he secretly sent someone to enrage him and urged him to kill Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Wang Ling had shamed Wang Ru, Wang Dun secretly stoked his rage and urged him to murder Wang Ling.

sentences.zh: 如詣棱，因閑宴，請劍舞為歡，棱從之。

translations.literal: Ru went to Ling and, taking advantage of a leisurely banquet, asked to perform sword dance for merriment; Ling consented.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ru visited Wang Ling during a relaxed feast and offered a sword dance for entertainment; Wang Ling agreed.

sentences.zh: 如於是舞刀為戲，漸漸來前。

translations.literal: Ru thereupon danced with the blade as sport and gradually came forward.
translations.idiomatic: He flourished his blade in mock combat and edged closer.

sentences.zh: 棱惡而呵之不止，叱左右使牽去，如直前害棱。

translations.literal: Ling detested it and shouted at him to stop but he did not stop; Ling shouted at left and right to drag him away; Ru went straight forward and killed Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling barked at him to stop; Wang Ru pressed on until Wang Ling ordered guards to drag him off—then Wang Ru closed the distance and cut him down.

sentences.zh: 敦聞而陽驚，亦捕如誅之。

translations.literal: When Dun heard, he feigned shock and also seized Ru and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun put on a show of horror, seized Wang Ru, and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 杜曾

translations.literal: Du Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng

sentences.zh: 杜曾，新野人，南中郎將蕤之從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Du Zeng was a man of Xinye, a second cousin once removed of the General of the Central Army of the South Rui.
