translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng came from Xinye; he was a kinsman of Du Rui, general of the central army of the south.

sentences.zh: 少驍勇絕人，能被甲游于水中。

translations.literal: In youth his fierce bravery surpassed others; he could wear armor and swim in water.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was superhumanly brave—he could swim in full armor.

sentences.zh: 始為新野王歆鎮南參軍，曆華容令，至南蠻司馬。

translations.literal: He began as aide to the south for Sima Xin the Prince of Xinye who guards the south, passed to magistrate of Huarong, reaching colonel of the southern Man.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the staff of Sima Xin, prince of Xinye, as an officer for the south, became magistrate of Huarong, and rose to colonel of the southern tribes.

sentences.zh: 凡有戰陣，勇冠三軍。

translations.literal: Whenever there were battles and formations, his courage crowned the three armies.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle he was the bravest man in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 會永嘉之亂，荊州荒梗，故牙門將胡亢聚眾於竟陵，自號楚公，假曾竟陵太守。

translations.literal: It happened that in the Yongjia turmoil Jing Province was desolate and blocked; therefore the former gate general Hu Kang gathered a host at Jingling, styled himself Duke of Chu, and falsely appointed Zeng Administrator of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongjia upheavals, with Jingzhou in chaos, former gate captain Hu Kang rallied men at Jingling, declared himself duke of Chu, and named Du Zeng administrator of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 亢後與其黨自相猜貳，誅其驍將數十人，曾心不自安，潛謀圖之，乃卑身屈節以事於亢，亢弗之覺，甚信任之。

translations.literal: Later Kang and his party mutually suspected one another in two minds; he executed several tens of his fierce generals; Zeng's heart was not at ease and secretly plotted against him; he humbled body and bent integrity to serve Kang; Kang did not perceive it and greatly trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Kang later turned on his own generals and executed dozens of them. Du Zeng grew uneasy, feigned submission, and won Hu Kang's full trust while plotting his overthrow.

sentences.zh: 會荊州賊王沖自號荊州刺史，部眾亦盛，屢遣兵抄亢所統，亢患之，問計于曾，曾勸令擊之，亢以為然。

translations.literal: It happened that the Jing Province bandit Wang Chong styled himself Inspector of Jing Province; his host was also strong; he repeatedly sent troops to raid what Kang commanded; Kang worried about it and asked Zeng for plan; Zeng urged him to strike; Kang thought it right.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Wang Chong proclaimed himself inspector of Jing and repeatedly raided Hu Kang's territory. Hu Kang asked Du Zeng for advice; Du Zeng urged an attack, and Hu Kang agreed.

sentences.zh: 曾白亢取帳下刀戟付工磨之，因潛引王沖之兵。

translations.literal: Zeng told Kang to take the halberds under the tent and give them to craftsmen to polish, and thereby secretly drew in Wang Chong's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng told Hu Kang to send the guard's halberds out for sharpening—then used the distraction to slip Wang Chong's men into the city.

sentences.zh: 亢遣精騎出距沖，城中空虛，曾因斬亢而並其眾，自號南中郎將、領竟陵太守。

translations.literal: Kang sent picked horse out to oppose Chong; the city was empty within; Zeng thereupon beheaded Kang and absorbed his host, styling himself General of the Central Army of the South and concurrent Administrator of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Kang sent his cavalry out to meet Wang Chong, leaving the town undefended. Du Zeng cut off Hu Kang's head, seized his army, and proclaimed himself general of the central army of the south and administrator of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 曾求南郡太守劉務女不得，盡滅其家。

translations.literal: Zeng sought the daughter of Administrator of Nan Commandery Liu Wu and did not obtain her; he exterminated his whole family.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wu, administrator of Nan commandery, refused him a daughter, Du Zeng slaughtered the entire household.

sentences.zh: 會湣帝遣第五猗為安南將軍、荊州刺史，曾迎猗於襄陽，為兄子娶猗女，遂分據沔漢。

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Min sent the Fifth Yi as General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jing Province; Zeng welcomed Yi at Xiangyang, married a brother's son to Yi's daughter, and thereupon divided holding of the Han basin.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min appointed Fifth Yi general who pacifies the south and inspector of Jing, Du Zeng welcomed him at Xiangyang, married his nephew into Yi's family, and the two split control of the Han River lands.

sentences.zh: 時陶侃新破杜弢，乘勝擊曾，有輕曾之色。

translations.literal: At that time Tao Kan had newly broken Du Tao and, riding victory, struck Zeng, showing contempt for Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan had just crushed Du Tao and, overconfident, underestimated Du Zeng.

sentences.zh: 侃司馬魯恬言於侃曰：「古人爭戰，先料其將，今使君諸將無及曾者，未易可逼也。

translations.literal: Kan's marshal Lu Tian said to Kan, "When ancients contested battle, they first assessed the opposing general; now none of the envoy's generals matches Zeng—it is not easy to press him.
translations.idiomatic: His marshal Lu Tian warned, "The old masters sized up enemy commanders first. None of your generals is a match for Du Zeng—do not press him lightly.

sentences.zh: 」侃不從，進軍圍之於石城。

translations.literal: " Kan did not follow, advanced the army and besieged him at Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan ignored him, advanced, and besieged Du Zeng at Stone City.

sentences.zh: 時曾軍多騎，而侃兵無馬，曾密開門，突侃陣，出其後，反擊其背，侃師遂敗，投水死者數百人。

translations.literal: At that time Zeng's army had many horse while Kan's troops had no horses; Zeng secretly opened the gate, burst Kan's formation, came out behind him, and struck his back; Kan's army was thereupon defeated; several hundred drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng's men were mostly cavalry; Tao Kan had almost none. Du Zeng slipped the gates open, charged through Tao Kan's line, wheeled, and hammered him from the rear. Tao Kan's army collapsed; hundreds drowned.

sentences.zh: 曾將趨順陽，下馬拜侃，告辭而去。

translations.literal: Zeng was about to hurry toward Shunyang; he dismounted and bowed to Kan, took leave, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: As he withdrew toward Shunyang, Du Zeng dismounted, bowed to Tao Kan, and rode off.

sentences.zh: 既而致箋于平南將軍荀崧，求討丹水賊以自效，崧納之。

translations.literal: Afterward he sent a note to General Who Pacifies the South Xun Song, asking to punish the bandits of Danshui to prove loyalty; Song accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote to Xun Song, general who pacifies the south, offering to clear the Danshui bandits as proof of loyalty; Xun Song agreed.

sentences.zh: 侃遺崧書曰：「杜曾凶狡，所將之卒皆豺狼也，可謂鴟梟食母之物。

translations.literal: Kan sent Song a letter saying, "Du Zeng is fierce and crafty; the soldiers he leads are all jackals and wolves; they may be called owls and kites that devour their mothers.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan wrote Xun Song, "Du Zeng is a vicious fox; his troops are jackals—birds of prey that devour their own.

sentences.zh: 此人不死，州土未寧，足下當識吾言。

translations.literal: If this man does not die, the province will not be peaceful; you should remember my words.
translations.idiomatic: While he lives, Jingzhou will never know peace—mark my words.

sentences.zh: 」崧以宛中兵少，藉曾為外援，不從侃言。

translations.literal: " Song because troops in Wan were few, borrowed Zeng as outer aid, and did not follow Kan's words.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Song, short of men in Wan, treated Du Zeng as an ally and ignored Tao Kan.

sentences.zh: 曾復率流亡二千餘人圍襄陽，數日不下而還。

translations.literal: Zeng again led more than two thousand fugitives to besiege Xiangyang; several days could not take it and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng brought two thousand fugitives back to besiege Xiangyang, lifted the siege after a few days, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及王暠為荊州刺史，曾距之，暠使將硃軌、趙誘擊曾，皆為曾所殺。

translations.literal: When Wang Hao became Inspector of Jing Province, Zeng opposed him; Hao sent generals Zhu Gui and Zhao You to strike Zeng, and both were killed by Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Hao took office as inspector of Jing, Du Zeng resisted; Wang Hao sent Zhu Gui and Zhao You against him, and Du Zeng killed both.

sentences.zh: 王敦遣周訪討之，屢戰不能克，訪潛遣人緣山開道，出曾不意以襲之，曾眾潰，其將馬俊、蘇溫等執曾詣訪降。

translations.literal: Wang Dun sent Zhou Fang to punish him; fighting repeatedly could not overcome him; Fang secretly sent men along the mountains to open a road, came out where Zeng did not expect, and raided him; Zeng's host scattered; his generals Ma Jun and Su Wen seized Zeng and brought him to Fang to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun dispatched Zhou Fang, who could not win in open battle. Zhou Fang cut a secret mountain track, caught Du Zeng by surprise, and broke his army. Generals Ma Jun and Su Wen bound Du Zeng and surrendered him to Zhou Fang.

sentences.zh: 訪欲生致武昌，而硃軌息昌、趙誘息胤皆乞曾以復冤，於是斬曾，而昌、胤臠其肉而啖之。

translations.literal: Fang wished to deliver him alive to Wuchang, but Zhu Gui's son Chang and Zhao You's son Yin both begged Zeng to redress their wrongs; thereupon they beheaded Zeng, and Chang and Yin carved his flesh and ate it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang meant to send Du Zeng alive to Wuchang, but Zhu Chang and Zhao Yin, sons of his victims, demanded blood justice. Du Zeng was executed; the two young men cut strips from his corpse and devoured them.

sentences.zh: 杜弢

translations.literal: Du Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Du Tao

sentences.zh: 杜弢，字景文，蜀郡成都人也。

translations.literal: Du Tao, courtesy name Jingwen, was a man of Chengdu in Shu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Du Tao, courtesy name Jingwen, came from Chengdu in Shu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖植，有名蜀土，武帝時為符節令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhi was famous in Shu soil; under Emperor Wu he was tally-and-credential director.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Du Zhi was renowned in Shu and served Emperor Wu as director of tallies and credentials.

sentences.zh: 父眕，略陽護軍。

translations.literal: His father Zhen was protector of Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Du Zhen was protector of Lüeyang.

sentences.zh: 弢初以才學著稱，州舉秀才。

translations.literal: Tao at first was celebrated for talent and learning; the province recommended him as cultivated talent.
translations.idiomatic: Du Tao first made his name as a scholar; the province nominated him as a cultivated talent.

sentences.zh: 遭李庠之亂，避地南平，太守應詹愛其才而禮之。

translations.literal: Encountering Li Xiang's rebellion, he fled south to Nanping; Administrator Ying Zhan loved his talent and treated him with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xiang rose in revolt, he fled to Nanping, where Prefect Ying Zhan admired his gifts and honored him.

sentences.zh: 後為醴陵令。

translations.literal: Later he became magistrate of Liling.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as magistrate of Liling.

sentences.zh: 時巴蜀流人汝班、蹇碩等數萬家，布在荊湘間，而為舊百姓之所侵苦，並懷怨恨。

translations.literal: At that time several tens of thousands of households of Shu refugees such as Ru Ban and Jian Shuo were spread between Jing and Xiang, and were oppressed and tormented by the old commoners; all harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of Shu refugees—Ru Ban, Jian Shuo, and others—were scattered through Jing and Xiang, bullied by locals, and nursed a bitter grudge.

sentences.zh: 會屬賊李驤殺縣令，屯聚樂鄉，眾數百人，弢與應詹擊驤，破之。

translations.literal: It happened that the subordinate bandit Li Xiang killed the magistrate and gathered at Lexiang with several hundred men; Tao with Ying Zhan struck Xiang and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xiang, a local rebel, murdered the magistrate and entrenched at Lexiang with hundreds of men, Du Tao and Ying Zhan attacked and crushed him.

sentences.zh: 蜀人杜疇、蹇撫等復擾湘州，參軍馮素與汝班不協，言于刺史荀眺曰：「流人皆欲反。

translations.literal: Shu men Du Chou and Jian Fu again disturbed Xiang Province; aide Feng Su was not in harmony with Ru Ban and said to Inspector Xun Tiao, "The refugees all wish to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chou and Jian Fu, men from Shu, stirred trouble in Xiangzhou. Staff officer Feng Su, who hated Ru Ban, told Inspector Xun Tiao, "The refugees are plotting revolt.

sentences.zh: 」眺以為然，欲盡誅流人。

translations.literal: " Tiao thought it right and wished to kill all the refugees.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Tiao believed him and prepared to massacre the refugees.

sentences.zh: 班等懼死，聚眾以應疇。

translations.literal: Ban and the others feared death and gathered a host to answer Chou.
translations.idiomatic: Ru Ban and his fellows, fearing execution, rose in support of Du Chou.

sentences.zh: 時弢在湘中，賊眾共推弢為主，弢自稱梁益二州牧、平難將軍、湘州刺史，攻破郡縣，眺委城走廣州。

translations.literal: At that time Tao was in central Xiang; the bandit host together pushed Tao as leader; Tao styled himself shepherd of Liang and Yi provinces, General Who Pacifies Hardship, and Inspector of Xiang Province; he broke commanderies and counties; Tiao abandoned the city and fled to Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: With Du Tao in the Xiang heartland, the rebels made him their chief. He proclaimed himself governor of Liang and Yi, general who pacifies hardship, and inspector of Xiang, overran the region, and drove Xun Tiao to flight toward Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 廣州刺史郭訥遣始興太守嚴佐率眾攻弢，弢逆擊破之。

translations.literal: Inspector of Guang Province Guo Ne sent Administrator of Shixing Yan Zuo to lead a host to attack Tao; Tao met him in attack and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ne, inspector of Guangzhou, sent Yan Zuo, prefect of Shixing, against Du Tao; Du Tao met him in battle and won.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史王澄復遣王機擊弢，敗于巴陵。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jing Province Wang Cheng again sent Wang Ji to strike Tao; he was defeated at Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng, inspector of Jingzhou, sent Wang Ji; Du Tao defeated them at Baling.

sentences.zh: 弢遂縱兵肆暴，偽降于山簡，簡以為廣漢太守。

translations.literal: Tao thereupon let his soldiers rampage unchecked and falsely surrendered to Shan Jian; Jian made him Administrator of Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: Du Tao then unleashed his troops and feigned submission to Shan Jian, who named him administrator of Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 眺之走也，州人推安成太守郭察領州事，因率眾討弢，反為所敗，察死之。

translations.literal: When Tiao fled, the provincials pushed Administrator of Ancheng Guo Cha to lead provincial affairs; he thereupon led a host to punish Tao but was defeated by him; Cha died.
translations.idiomatic: After Xun Tiao ran, locals put Guo Cha, prefect of Ancheng, in charge; Guo Cha marched against Du Tao, was beaten, and died.

sentences.zh: 弢遂南破零陵，東侵武昌，害長沙太守崔敷、宜都太守杜鑒、邵陵太守鄭融等。

translations.literal: Tao thereupon broke Lingling south and raided Wuchang east, killing Administrator of Changsha Cui Fu, Administrator of Yidu Du Jian, Administrator of Shaoling Zheng Rong, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He smashed Lingling in the south, struck east into Wuchang, and killed Cui Fu of Changsha, Du Jian of Yidu, Zheng Rong of Shaoling, and others.

sentences.zh: 元帝命征南將軍王敦、荊州刺史陶侃等討之，前後數十戰，弢將士多物故，於是請降。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan ordered General Who Conquers the South Wang Dun, Inspector of Jing Province Tao Kan, and others to punish him; after several tens of battles front and back, Du Tao's officers and soldiers for the most part perished; thereupon he requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan sent Wang Dun, Tao Kan, and others against him. After dozens of engagements Du Tao's army was so worn that he sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 帝不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 弢乃遺應詹書曰：

translations.literal: Tao thereupon sent Ying Zhan a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: Du Tao then wrote to Ying Zhan:

sentences.zh: 天步艱難，始自吾州；

translations.literal: Heaven's march is hard; it began in our province;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's road turned cruel starting in our home commandery;

sentences.zh: 州党流移，在於荊土。

translations.literal: provincial kin drifted and moved, dwelling in Jing soil.
translations.idiomatic: our people were driven onto Jingzhou soil.

sentences.zh: 其所遇值，蔑之如遺，頓伏死亡者略復過平，備嘗荼毒，足下之所鑒也。

translations.literal: What they met was scorned as cast-off; of those who fell prostrate and died roughly half again passed peace; they fully tasted bitter poison—this is what you have witnessed.
translations.idiomatic: They were treated like refuse; half our number perished in the dust. You saw that suffering yourself.

sentences.zh: 客主難久，嫌隙易構，不謂樂鄉起變出於不意，時與足下思散疑結，求擒其党帥，惟患算不經遠，力不陷堅耳。

translations.literal: Guest and host cannot long endure; suspicion easily forms; I did not expect the Lexiang rising to come beyond expectation; at the time with you I wished to scatter doubt's knot and seek to capture its chieftains—only I worried calculation did not reach far, strength could not pierce hardness.
translations.idiomatic: Hosts and guests cannot live together long without rancor. The Lexiang mutiny caught us unawares; I had hoped, with you, to untangle the plot and seize the ringleaders—if only our plans had been sounder and our arms stronger.

sentences.zh: 及在湘中，懼死求生，遂相結聚，欲守善自衛，天下小定，然後輸誠盟府。

translations.literal: When I was in central Xiang, fearing death I sought life, thereupon mutually bound to gather, wishing to keep good and defend ourselves; when the realm was slightly settled, then submit good faith to the alliance prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered in Xiang, we banded together simply to survive until the realm calmed, then pledge loyalty to the viceroy.

sentences.zh: 尋山公鎮夏口，即具陳之。

translations.literal: Soon Lord Shan garrisoned Xiakou and I set it all out to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shan Jian took Xiakou, I laid the whole matter before him.

sentences.zh: 此公鑒開塞之會，察窮通之運，納吾於眾疑之中，非高識玄睹，孰能若此！

translations.literal: That lord discerned the meeting of blocked and open, examined the luck of exhausted and smooth, and took me in amid universal doubt—if not high insight and dark seeing, who could do thus!
translations.idiomatic: He read the moment, saw our plight, and sheltered me though all doubted him—only a man of vision could do that.

sentences.zh: 西州人士得沐浴于清流，豈惟滌蕩瑕穢，乃骨肉之施。

translations.literal: Men of the western province could bathe in clear flow; was it only washing away stain—it was favor of flesh and bone.
translations.idiomatic: We westerners were allowed to rinse clean in a clear stream; it was more than absolution—it was kinship.

sentences.zh: 此公薨逝，斯事中廢，賢愚痛毒，竊心自悼。

translations.literal: When that lord passed, this affair stopped mid-course; worthy and foolish alike grieved poison; I stole grief in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, that mercy ended; good and simple men alike mourned, and I grieved in secret.

sentences.zh: 欲遣滕永文、張休豫詣大府備列起事以來本末，但恐貪功殉名之徒將讒間於聖主之聽，戮吾使於市朝以彰叛逆之罪，故未敢遣之。

translations.literal: I wished to send Teng Yongwen and Zhang Xiuyu to the great prefecture to set forth in order the beginning and end since the rising, but I feared men greedy for merit and courting fame would slander between the sage ruler's hearing, kill my envoy in the market court to display the crime of rebellion, therefore I did not dare send them.
translations.idiomatic: I meant to send Teng Yongwen and Zhang Xiuyu to the viceroy with a full chronicle of our uprising, yet feared careerists would poison the court's ear and execute my messengers as traitors in the marketplace, so I held back.

sentences.zh: 而王陶卒至，水陸十萬，旌旗曜於山澤，舟艦有盈于三江，威則威矣，然吾眾竊未以為懼。

translations.literal: Yet Wang and Tao arrived in haste, one hundred thousand by land and water; banners dazzled in hills and marshes; boats and hulls filled the three rivers—awesome indeed, yet our host privately did not therefore fear.
translations.idiomatic: Then Wang Dun and Tao Kan arrived—an army of a hundred thousand by land and sea, banners blotting the hills, hulls choking the three rivers. Impressive—but we were not afraid.

sentences.zh: 晉文伐原，以全信為本，故能使諸侯歸之。

translations.literal: Duke Wen of Jin attacked Yuan, taking keeping faith as root; therefore he could make the feudal lords return to him.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen of Jin took Yuan yet kept his word; that is how he won the allegiance of the lords.

sentences.zh: 陶侃宣赦書而繼之以進討，豈所以崇奉明詔，示軌憲于四海！

translations.literal: Tao Kan proclaimed the amnesty edict and followed it with advance punishment—how is this to honor reverently the bright edict and show model law to the four seas!
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan read the amnesty, then attacked—how does that honor an imperial pardon or teach the empire the rule of law?

sentences.zh: 逼向義之夫以為叛逆之虜，踧思善之眾以極不赦之責，非不戰而屈人之算也。

translations.literal: He presses men inclined to righteousness into the captives of rebellion, drives crowds thinking good to the utmost of unpardonable blame—it is not the calculus of subduing others without battle.
translations.idiomatic: He brands the law-abiding as rebels and condemns men who want peace to unforgivable guilt—that is not how you win without a fight.

sentences.zh: 驅略烏合，欲與必死者求一戰，未見爭衡之機權也。

translations.literal: Driving and plundering a crow-joined mass, wishing to seek one battle with those sure to die—I do not see the opportune weight of contending the balance.
translations.idiomatic: He herds a rabble of desperate men into a single suicidal clash—that is not sound strategy.

sentences.zh: 吾之赤心，貫於神明，西州人士，卿粗悉之耳。

translations.literal: My red heart pierces through to the spirits; men of the western province—you roughly know it all.
translations.idiomatic: My loyalty is plain to heaven; the men of the west know it as you do.

sentences.zh: 甯當令抱枉于時，不證於大府邪！

translations.literal: Should I be made to embrace wrong in the times and not prove myself to the great prefect!
translations.idiomatic: Would you have me bear false guilt before the world and never clear my name with the viceroy?

sentences.zh: 昔虞卿不榮大國之相，與魏齊同其安危；

translations.literal: Formerly Yu Qing did not glory in being minister of a great state; he shared safety and peril with Wei Qi;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qing spurned high office in a great kingdom to share Wei Qi's fate;

sentences.zh: 司馬遷明言于李陵，雖刑殘而無慨。

translations.literal: Sima Qian spoke plainly for Li Ling; although mutilated he had no regret.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian spoke truth for Li Ling and accepted mutilation without regret.

sentences.zh: 足下抗威千里，聲播汶衡，進宜為國思靜難之略，退與舊交措枉直之正，不亦綽然有餘裕乎！

translations.literal: You oppose might for a thousand li, fame spreads to Wen and Heng; advancing you should for the state think a plan to still hardship, withdrawing with old friends set right the crooked and straight—is it not then amply ample with surplus!
translations.idiomatic: Your authority spans a thousand li, your name rings to Taishan and Heng—you should advance with a plan to quiet the turmoil, or step back and settle justice among old friends. Surely that leaves room enough for honor.

sentences.zh: 望卿騰吾箋令，時達盟府，遣大使光臨，使吾得披露肝膽，沒身何恨哉！

translations.literal: I hope you will hurry my letter up, that it reach the alliance prefect in time, dispatch a great ambassador to grace us, so that I may lay bare liver and gall—what regret in death!
translations.idiomatic: Forward my letter to the viceroy; send a high envoy so I may lay bare my heart. I would die content.

sentences.zh: 伏想盟府必結紐于紀綱，為一匡於聖世，使吾廁列義徒，負戈前驅，迎皇輿於閶闔，掃長蛇於荒裔，雖死之日，猶生之年也。

translations.literal: I humbly imagine the alliance prefect must tie knots in statutes and cords, make one correction for the sage age, let me rank among the righteous host, bear spear as vanguard, welcome the imperial chariot at Changmen, sweep the long serpent from the wild border—though a day of death, it is like a year of life.
translations.idiomatic: Surely the viceroy will bind the law and set the age right: let me march with the loyalists, spear in the van, escort the throne to the capital, and drive the serpent from the frontier—then death would feel like life.

sentences.zh: 若然，先清方夏，卻定中原，吾得一所之糧，使泝流西歸，夷李雄之逋寇，修《禹貢》之舊獻，展微勞以補往愆，復州邦以謝鄰國，亦其志也，惟所裁處耳。

translations.literal: If it be so, first clear the southern summer, then settle the central plain—I obtain grain from one place, let me go west upstream against the current, level Li Xiong's fleeing bandits, restore the old tribute of the "Tribute of Yu," display slight labor to amend past fault, restore the province to thank neighboring states—that too is my intent; only await what you cut and dispose.
translations.idiomatic: If so, pacify the south, then the heartland—grant me grain, and I will sail west to crush Li Xiong, restore the tribute routes of the "Tribute of Yu," make amends with a little service, and return my province to thank our neighbors—that is my wish; only say the word.

sentences.zh: 吾遠州寒士，與足下出處殊倫，誠不足感神交而濟其傾危。

translations.literal: I am a cold scholar of a distant province; with you I differ in rank of going out and staying—truly insufficient to move spirit-communion to save their overturning peril.
translations.idiomatic: I am a poor scholar from the far west; our stations differ—I cannot claim a soul-bond strong enough to move you.

sentences.zh: 但顯吾忠誠，則汶岳荷忠順之恕，衡湘無伐叛之虞，隆足下宏納之望，拯吾徒陷溺之艱，焉可金玉其音哉！

translations.literal: But if you display my loyalty, then Wen and Yue will bear the forgiveness of loyal submission, Heng and Xiang will have no worry of punishing rebellion, enlarge your hope of grand acceptance, save my kind from drowning hardship—how can I gild my words!
translations.idiomatic: Yet prove my good faith, and Taishan will show mercy, Xiang will fear no revolt, you gain a reputation for generosity, and we escape ruin—why should I flatter you with pretty phrases?

sentences.zh: 然顒顒十餘萬口，亦勞瘁於警備，思放逸于南畝矣。

translations.literal: Yet the gazing-gazing more than one hundred thousand mouths also are worn in alert defense, thinking to roam free in southern acres.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a hundred thousand anxious people stand sleepless on guard, longing only to return to their fields.

sentences.zh: 衡獄、江、湘列吾左右，若往言有貳，血誠不亮，益梁受殃，不惟鄙門而已。

translations.literal: Heng's peak, the Yangtze, and Xiang stand at my left and right; if my words harbor two hearts and blood-sincerity is not bright, Yi and Liang will suffer calamity—not only my humble gate.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Heng, the Yangtze, and the Xiang hem me in; if I lie, may Yi and Liang suffer—not my house alone.

sentences.zh: 詹甚哀之，乃啟呈弢書，並上言曰：「弢益州秀才，素有清望，文理既優，幹事兼美。

translations.literal: Zhan greatly pitied him, thereupon presented Tao's letter and submitted words saying, "Tao is a cultivated talent of Yi Province, of old having clear repute; pattern and principle are already excellent, handling affairs also beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Zhan took pity and forwarded Du Tao's letter with a memorial: "Du Tao, a Shu recommendee, has always been respected; his prose is fine and his administration capable.

sentences.zh: 往因使流寓，居詹郡界，其貞心堅白：詹所委究。

translations.literal: Formerly because of mission he drifted and lodged, dwelling in Zhan's commandery bounds; his chaste heart is firm white—Zhan has investigated and exhausted it.
translations.idiomatic: He lodged in my district as a refugee; his integrity is stainless—I know it well.

sentences.zh: 李驤為變樂鄉，劫略良善，弢時出家財，招募忠勇，登壇歃血，義誠慷慨。

translations.literal: Li Xiang made trouble at Lexiang, raiding and seizing the good; Tao at that time used family wealth, recruited the loyal and brave, ascended the altar and smeared blood, righteous sincerity generous.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xiang terrorized Lexiang, Du Tao spent his own fortune, rallied loyal men, and swore oaths on the altar in fierce earnest.

sentences.zh: 會驤攻燒南平，弢遂東下巴漢，與湘中鄉人相遇，推其素望，遂相憑結。

translations.literal: It happened that Li Xiang attacked and burned Nanping; Tao thereupon went east to Ba and Han; meeting fellow townsmen of central Xiang, he pushed his old repute, and thereupon mutually relied and bound.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xiang burned Nanping, Du Tao moved east into Ba and Han, met his Xiang countrymen, and they rallied to him for his old standing.

sentences.zh: 論弢本情，非首作亂階者也。

translations.literal: Judging Tao's original feeling, he was not the first to make the steps of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: By rights Du Tao was not the one who started the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 然破湘川，實弢之罪，亦由兵交其間，遂使滋蔓。

translations.literal: Yet smashing the Xiang riverlands was indeed Tao's crime; also because arms crossed therein, it made the growth spread.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ravaging the Xiang basin was his doing, compounded by the fighting that let the revolt spread.

sentences.zh: 按弢今書，血誠亦至矣。

translations.literal: According to Tao's present letter, blood-sincerity also reaches the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: His letter bleeds sincerity.

sentences.zh: 昔硃鮪自疑於洛陽，光武指河水以明心，鮪感義歸誠，終展力報施，受封侯之寵，由恕過以錄功也。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhu Wei doubted himself at Luoyang; Guangwu pointed to the river water to clarify mind; Wei was moved by righteousness and returned in good faith, in the end displayed strength repaying kindness, received the favor of enfeoffment as marquis—by forgiving fault and recording merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Wei wavered at Luoyang, Emperor Guangwu swore on the Yellow River; Zhu Wei came over, earned a marquisate, and repaid grace—because the throne forgave fault and rewarded merit.

sentences.zh: 詹竊謂今者當圮運之會，思弘遠猷，故齊赦射鉤之誅，晉貰斬袪之戮，用能濟冀戴之高勳，隆一匡之美譽，況弢等素無斯愆而稽顙投命邪！

translations.literal: Zhan privately says that now is the meeting of ruined fortune's conjunction, thinking to enlarge far plans; therefore Qi pardoned the execution for the hook-shot, Jin spared the killing for the cut sleeve—by this they could accomplish the high merit of Ji and Dai, raise the fine fame of one correction—how much more Tao and the rest, who of old lacked this fault yet knocked forehead and cast life!
translations.idiomatic: We live in a broken age that calls for great conciliation: Qi spared Guan Zhong, Jin forgave Pi Zheng—thus they won the mandate. Du Tao and his men have committed no such crimes and kneel for mercy—why not accept them?

sentences.zh: 以為可遣大使宣揚聖旨，雲澤沾之于上，百姓沐浴于下，則上下交泰，江左無風塵之虞矣。

translations.literal: I think one may send a great ambassador to proclaim and raise the sage decree, so cloud-moisture wets from above and the hundred clans bathe below; then high and low inter-thrive and east of the Yangtze has no worry of wind and dust.
translations.idiomatic: Send a high envoy with the imperial word: let grace fall from above and the people refresh below; ruler and ruled will harmonize and the southeast will be spared another war.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃使前南海太守王運受弢降，宣詔書大赦，凡諸反逆一皆除之，加弢巴東監軍。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon sent former Administrator of Nanhai Wang Yun to accept Tao's surrender, proclaimed an edict of great amnesty, all kinds of rebellion were entirely remitted, and added Tao as overseer of the army in Badong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Wang Yun, former prefect of Nanhai, to receive Du Tao's surrender, proclaimed a general amnesty for all rebels, and named him army overseer in Badong.

sentences.zh: 弢受命後，諸將殉功者攻擊之不已，弢不勝憤怒，遂殺運而使其將王真領精卒三千為奇兵，出江南，向武陵，斷官軍運路。

translations.literal: After Tao received the mandate, the various generals who died for merit attacked him without cease; Tao could not bear rage and anger, thereupon killed Yun and sent his general Wang Zhen to lead three thousand picked soldiers as extraordinary troops, out south of the Yangtze toward Wuling, cutting government army transport roads.
translations.idiomatic: But generals greedy for glory kept attacking. Du Tao, furious, slew Wang Yun and sent Wang Zhen with three thousand elite troops across the river toward Wuling to sever supply lines.

sentences.zh: 陶侃使伏波將軍鄭攀邀擊，大破之，真步走湘城。

translations.literal: Tao Kan sent General Who Calms the Waves Zheng Pan to intercept and strike, routed him badly, and Zhen walked in flight to Xiang city.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan ordered Zheng Pan, general who calms the waves, to intercept; Wang Zhen was shattered and fled on foot to Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 於是侃等諸軍齊進，真遂降侃，眾黨散潰。

translations.literal: Thereupon Kan and the various armies advanced together; Zhen thereupon surrendered to Kan, and the host of partisans scattered and collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan closed in; Wang Zhen surrendered, and Du Tao's following melted away.

sentences.zh: 弢乃逃遁，不知所在。

translations.literal: Tao thereupon fled and hid; his whereabouts were unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Du Tao vanished; no one knew where he went.

sentences.zh: 王機

translations.literal: Wang Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji

sentences.zh: 王機，字令明，長沙人也。

translations.literal: Wang Ji, courtesy name Lingming, was a man of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji, courtesy name Lingming, came from Changsha.

sentences.zh: 父毅，廣州刺史，甚得南越之情。

translations.literal: His father Yi was Inspector of Guang Province and greatly won the feeling of the southern Yue.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Yi was inspector of Guangzhou and was beloved in the far south.

sentences.zh: 機美姿儀，亻周儻有度量。

translations.literal: Ji had handsome bearing and was free and easy, having measure.
translations.idiomatic: He was striking in appearance, easygoing, and magnanimous.

sentences.zh: 陳恢之亂，機年十七，率眾擊破之。

translations.literal: During Chen Hui's rebellion, Ji was seventeen and led a host to break him.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he crushed Chen Hui's revolt.

sentences.zh: 嘗慕王澄為人，澄亦雅知之，以為己亞，遂與友善，內綜心膂，外為牙爪。

translations.literal: He once admired Wang Cheng as a man; Cheng also elegantly knew him, thought him second to himself, and thereupon was friendly with him, within binding heart and liver, without being fang and claw.
translations.idiomatic: He modeled himself on Wang Cheng, who in turn esteemed him as a younger peer; they became intimate allies, Wang Cheng's confidant and enforcer.

sentences.zh: 尋用為成都內史。

translations.literal: Soon he was used as interior minister of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named interior minister of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 機終日醉酒，不存政事，由是百姓怨之，人情騷動。

translations.literal: Ji was drunk all day, did not attend to government; hence the hundred clans resented him and human hearts were restless.
translations.idiomatic: He drank his days away and neglected his duties until the people cursed him and unrest spread.

sentences.zh: 會澄遇害，機懼禍及，又屬杜弢所在發墓，而獨為機守塚，機益自疑。

translations.literal: It happened that Cheng met murder; Ji feared disaster reaching him; moreover it fell that Du Tao everywhere opened tombs yet alone for Ji guarded his tomb mound; Ji grew more self-doubting.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Cheng was killed, Wang Ji feared he would be next. Du Tao was looting graves everywhere but spared Wang Ji's family tombs— which only deepened Wang Ji's paranoia.

sentences.zh: 就王敦求廣州，敦不許。

translations.literal: He approached Wang Dun asking for Guang Province; Dun did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: He begged Wang Dun for Guangzhou; Wang Dun refused.

sentences.zh: 會廣州人背刺史郭納，迎機為刺史，機遂將奴客門生千餘人入廣州，州部將溫邵率眾迎機。

translations.literal: It happened that men of Guang Province turned against Inspector Guo Ne and welcomed Ji as inspector; Ji thereupon led more than a thousand household slaves, retainers, and disciples into Guang Province; the provincial subordinate general Wen Shao led a host to welcome Ji.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzhou rose against Guo Ne and hailed Wang Ji as inspector, he marched in with a thousand retainers while Wen Shao brought troops to meet him.

sentences.zh: 郭遣參軍葛幽追之，及於廬陵，機叱幽曰：「何以敢來？

translations.literal: Guo sent aide Ge You in pursuit; they caught up at Luling; Ji shouted at You, "How dare you come?
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ne sent Ge You after him. At Luling Wang Ji roared, "What brings you here?

sentences.zh: 欲取死邪？

translations.literal: Do you wish to seek death?
translations.idiomatic: Do you want to die?

sentences.zh: 」幽不敢逼而歸。

translations.literal: " You did not dare press and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ge You dared not advance and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 郭訥聞邵之納機也，乃遣兵擊邵，反為所破。

translations.literal: When Guo Ne heard that Shao had welcomed Ji, he sent troops to strike Shao and was on the contrary defeated by him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ne attacked Wen Shao for siding with Wang Ji and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 訥又遣機父兄時吏距之，咸倒戈迎機，訥眾皆散，乃握節而避機。

translations.literal: Ne again sent officers who had served Ji's father and elder brothers to oppose them; all turned their spears to welcome Ji; Ne's host all scattered; thereupon he grasped the tally and yielded to avoid Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ne sent old officers of the Wang family against him; they defected en masse. Guo Ne fled, tally in hand, to escape Wang Ji.

sentences.zh: 機遂入城就訥求節，訥歎曰：「昔蘇武不失其節，前史以為美談。

translations.literal: Ji thereupon entered the city and approached Ne seeking the tally; Ne sighed, "Formerly Su Wu did not lose his tally; former histories took it as fine tale.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji entered the city and demanded the official seal. Guo Ne sighed, "Su Wu never surrendered his staff—the histories praise him.

sentences.zh: 此節天朝所假，義不相與，自可遣兵來取之。

translations.literal: This tally the heavenly court lent; by righteousness I cannot give it—you may simply send troops to take it.
translations.idiomatic: This tally belongs to the court, not to me; if you want it, take it by force.

sentences.zh: 」機慚而止。

translations.literal: " Ji was ashamed and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji, shamed, desisted.

sentences.zh: 機自以篡州，懼為王敦所討，乃更來交州。

translations.literal: Ji himself because he had usurped the province feared Wang Dun would punish him, thereupon went again to Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Wang Dun would punish him for seizing Guangzhou, he fled toward Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 時杜弢餘黨杜弘奔臨賀，送金數千兩與機，求討桂林賊以自效。

translations.literal: At that time Du Tao's remaining partisan Du Hong fled to Linhe and sent several thousand liang of gold to Ji, asking to punish Guilin bandits to prove loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong, a remnant of Du Tao's force, offered Wang Ji thousands of ounces of gold to campaign against Guilin bandits as a show of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 機為列上，朝廷許之。

translations.literal: Ji for his part memorialized upward; the court permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji memorialized the throne, which approved.

sentences.zh: 王敦以機難制，又欲因機討梁碩，故以降杜弘之勳轉為交州刺史。

translations.literal: Wang Dun because Ji was hard to control also wished to use Ji to punish Liang Shuo, therefore transferred him to Inspector of Jiao Province on the merit of subduing Du Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun, unable to control Wang Ji and wanting Liang Shuo eliminated, transferred him to Jiaozhou on the pretext of the Du Hong campaign.

sentences.zh: 碩聞而遣子侯侯機于郁林，機怒其迎遲，責云：「須至州當相收拷。

translations.literal: When Shuo heard, he sent his son Hou to await Ji at Yulin; Ji was angry at the late welcome and rebuked saying, "When I reach the province I shall seize and torture you.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shuo sent his son to greet Wang Ji at Yulin. Wang Ji fumed at the slight and swore to flog him once ashore.

sentences.zh: 」碩子馳使報碩，碩曰：「王郎已壞廣州，何可復來破交州也！

translations.literal: " Shuo's son galloped a messenger to report to Shuo; Shuo said, "Lord Wang has already ruined Guang Province—how can he come again to break Jiao Province!
translations.idiomatic: The son warned Liang Shuo, who cried, "Wang Ji wrecked Guangzhou—must he ruin Jiaozhou too?

sentences.zh: 」乃禁州人不許迎之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he forbade the provincials from welcoming him.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the province not to receive Wang Ji.

sentences.zh: 府司馬杜贊以碩不迎機，率兵討碩，為碩所敗。

translations.literal: Prefectural marshal Du Zan because Shuo did not welcome Ji led troops to punish Shuo and was defeated by Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zan, prefectural marshal, attacked Liang Shuo for blocking Wang Ji and was routed.

sentences.zh: 碩恐諸僑人為機，於是悉殺其良者，乃自領交址太守。

translations.literal: Shuo feared the various sojourners would act for Ji; thereupon he killed all the good ones among them and himself acted as Administrator of Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shuo feared the northern settlers would help Wang Ji and massacred the leading families, then named himself administrator of Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 機既為碩所距，遂住郁林。

translations.literal: Ji, already blocked by Shuo, thereupon stopped at Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Blocked by Liang Shuo, Wang Ji stalled at Yulin.

sentences.zh: 時杜弘大破桂林賊還，遇機於道，機勸弘取交州。

translations.literal: At that time Du Hong greatly defeated Guilin bandits returning; he met Ji on the road; Ji urged Hong to take Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong, returning from victory in Guilin, met Wang Ji, who urged him to seize Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 弘素有意，乃執機節曰：「當相與迭持，何可獨捉！

translations.literal: Hong of old had intent; thereupon he seized Ji's tally saying, "We should pass it among each other in turn—how can you alone hold it!
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong seized the tally, saying, "This badge should pass hand to hand—not sit with you alone!

sentences.zh: 」機遂以節與之。

translations.literal: " Ji thereupon gave the tally to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji surrendered the tally.

sentences.zh: 於是機與弘及溫邵、劉沈等並反。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ji with Hong and Wen Shao, Liu Shen, and others together rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji, Du Hong, Wen Shao, Liu Shen, and others then rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 尋而陶侃為廣州，到始興，州人皆諫不可輕進，侃不聽。

translations.literal: Soon Tao Kan became Inspector of Guang Province; arriving at Shixing, the provincials all remonstrated not to advance lightly; Kan did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao Kan took Guangzhou and reached Shixing, locals begged him not to rush; he refused.

sentences.zh: 及至州，諸郡縣皆已迎機矣。

translations.literal: When he reached the province, the various commanderies and counties had all already welcomed Ji.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived, every county had already gone over to Wang Ji.

sentences.zh: 侃先討溫邵、劉沈，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Kan first punished Wen Shao and Liu Shen, killing both.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan first destroyed Wen Shao and Liu Shen.

sentences.zh: 機遣牙門屈藍還州，詐言增糧，密招誘所部，欲以距侃。

translations.literal: Ji sent gate general Qu Lan back to the province, falsely saying to increase grain, secretly recruiting and enticing his command, wishing thereby to oppose Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji sent Qu Lan home on the pretext of gathering grain, secretly rallying troops against Tao Kan.

sentences.zh: 侃即收藍斬之，遣督護許高討機走之，病死於道。

translations.literal: Kan immediately seized Lan and beheaded him, sent commandant protector Xu Gao to punish Ji, drove him off, and he died ill on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan seized Qu Lan, executed him, and sent Xu Gao after Wang Ji, who fled and died on the run.

sentences.zh: 高掘出其屍斬首，並殺其二子焉。

translations.literal: Gao dug out his corpse and beheaded it, and also killed his two sons.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gao exhumed Wang Ji's body, took his head, and killed his two sons.

sentences.zh: 機兄矩，字令式。

translations.literal: Ji's elder brother Ju, courtesy name Lingshi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji's elder brother Wang Ju, courtesy name Lingshi.

sentences.zh: 美姿容，每出遊，觀者盈路。

translations.literal: He had handsome looks; whenever he went out touring, viewers filled the road.
translations.idiomatic: So handsome that crowds choked the streets when he went abroad.

sentences.zh: 初為南平太守，豫討陳恢有功，遷廣州刺史。

translations.literal: At first he was Administrator of Nanping; in the campaign punishing Chen Hui he had merit; was transferred Inspector of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Nanping, earned merit against Chen Hui, and was promoted to inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 將赴職，忽見一人持奏謁矩，自云京兆杜靈之。

translations.literal: About to go to office, he suddenly saw a man holding a memorial visiting Ju, calling himself Du Lingzhi of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of his posting he met a man claiming to be Du Lingzhi of Jingzhao, bearing a document.

sentences.zh: 矩問之，答稱：「天上京兆，被使召君為主簿。

translations.literal: Ju asked him; he answered saying, "Heavenly Jingzhao, dispatched to summon you as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The stranger said heaven had sent him to appoint Wang Ju chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 」矩意甚惡之。

translations.literal: Ju thought it very ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ju took it as a dire omen.

sentences.zh: 至州月餘卒。

translations.literal: After more than a month at the province he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died within a month of taking office.

sentences.zh: 祖約

translations.literal: Zu Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue

sentences.zh: 祖約，字士少，豫州刺史逖之弟也。

translations.literal: Zu Yue, courtesy name Shishao, was the younger brother of Inspector of Yu Province Ti.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue, courtesy name Shishao, was the younger brother of Zu Ti, inspector of Yu.

sentences.zh: 初以孝廉為成皋令，與逖甚相友愛。

translations.literal: At first by filial and incorrupt he became magistrate of Chenggao; with Ti he was greatly mutually friendly and loving.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as filial and incorrupt, he became magistrate of Chenggao and was devoted to his brother Zu Ti.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末，隨逖過江。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongjia he followed Ti across the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Yongjia era he crossed the Yangtze with Zu Ti.

sentences.zh: 元帝稱制，引為掾屬，與陳留阮孚齊名。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan, assuming regency, drew him in as staff, and he was of equal name with Ruan Fu of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan held regency he joined the staff alongside Ruan Fu of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 後轉從事中郎，典選舉。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred attendant-in-ordinary, in charge of selection.
translations.idiomatic: He later became attendant-in-ordinary in charge of appointments.

sentences.zh: 約妻無男而性妒，約亦不敢違忤。

translations.literal: Yue's wife had no sons but was jealous in nature; Yue also did not dare disobey.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was barren and fiercely jealous; Zu Yue dared not cross her.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜寢於外，忽為人所傷，疑其妻所為，約求去職，帝不聽，約便從右司馬營東門私出。

translations.literal: He once slept outside at night; suddenly he was wounded by someone; he suspected his wife did it; Yue asked to leave office; the emperor did not consent; Yue then privately went out the east gate of the right marshal's camp.
translations.idiomatic: After a night attack he suspected his wife; he begged to resign; the emperor refused; he slipped out through the east gate of the marshal's camp.

sentences.zh: 司直劉隗劾之曰：「約幸荷殊寵，顯位選曹，銓衡人物，眾所具瞻。

translations.literal: Rectifier Liu Wei impeached him saying, "Yue has luckily borne extraordinary favor, eminent position in the selection bureau, weighing persons—the multitude all look up.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wei impeached him: "Zu Yue enjoys imperial favor and heads personnel—everyone watches him.

sentences.zh: 當敬以直內，義以方外，杜漸防萌，式遏寇害。

translations.literal: He should revere with straightness within, act with righteousness without, stop sprouts at the source, check and halt bandit harm.
translations.idiomatic: He should model integrity within and without, nip evil in the bud.

sentences.zh: 而乃變起蕭牆，患生婢妾，身被刑傷，虧其膚髮。

translations.literal: Yet change rose within the screen; disaster came from concubines and maids; his body received wound and injury, marring skin and hair.
translations.idiomatic: Instead scandal broke within his household; he was bloodied by servants and maids.

sentences.zh: 群小噂嚃，囂聲遠被，塵穢清化，垢累明時。

translations.literal: Petty men buzzed; clamor spread far; dust defiled pure transformation; stain encumbered the bright age.
translations.idiomatic: Gossip spread and smeared the court's good order.

sentences.zh: 天恩含垢，猶復慰喻，而約違命輕出，既無明智以保其身，又孤恩廢命，宜加貶黜，以塞眾謗。

translations.literal: Heaven's grace holds filth; still again it comforted and instructed; yet Yue disobeyed orders and lightly went out—he had no clear wisdom to preserve his person, and also orphaned grace and abandoned mandate—he should be degraded and dismissed to stop the multitude's slander.
translations.idiomatic: The throne forgave him once, yet he bolted his post—witless and ungrateful. He should be demoted to silence slander.

sentences.zh: 」帝不之罪。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took no action.

sentences.zh: 隗重加執據，終不許。

translations.literal: Wei again pressed argument; in the end did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wei pressed the case; the emperor still refused.

sentences.zh: 及逖有功於譙沛，約漸見任遇。

translations.literal: When Ti had merit at Qiao and Pei, Yue was gradually seen with trust and favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Ti won glory on the Qiao-Pei front, Zu Yue rose in favor.

sentences.zh: 逖卒，自侍中代逖為平西將軍、豫州刺史，領逖之眾。

translations.literal: When Ti died, from palace attendant he replaced Ti as General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yu Province, commanding Ti's host.
translations.idiomatic: After Zu Ti died, Zu Yue stepped from palace attendant into his brother's shoes as general who pacifies the west and inspector of Yu, inheriting his army.

sentences.zh: 約異母兄光祿大夫納密言於帝曰：「約內懷陵上之心，抑而使之可也。

translations.literal: Yue's elder half-brother the grand master of the golden seal Na secretly spoke to the emperor saying, "Yue within harbors a heart to overawe the ruler; suppress and employ him and it can do.
translations.idiomatic: His half-brother Zu Na warned the emperor, "Zu Yue means to domineer the throne—keep him on a short leash.

sentences.zh: 今顯侍左右，假其權勢，將為亂階矣。

translations.literal: Now plainly attending at left and right, lending him power and influence, will become steps of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Giving him power at court invites rebellion.

sentences.zh: 」帝不納。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored him.

sentences.zh: 時人亦謂納與約異生，忌其寵貴，故有此言。

translations.literal: People of the time also said Na and Yue were born of different mothers; he envied his favor and nobility; therefore there was this speech.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Zu Na, a half-brother, envied Zu Yue's rise—that was why he spoke.

sentences.zh: 而約竟無綏馭之才，不為士卒所附。

translations.literal: Yet Yue in the end had no talent to soothe and control; he was not attached to by officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue proved no leader; his soldiers did not love him.

sentences.zh: 及王敦舉兵，約歸衛京都，率眾次壽陽，逐敦所署淮南太守任台，以功封五等侯，進號鎮西將軍，使屯壽陽，為北境籓捍。

translations.literal: When Wang Dun raised troops, Yue returned to guard the capital region, led a host and camped at Shouyang, expelled Dun's appointed Administrator of Huainan Ren Tai, by merit was enfeoffed a five-ranks marquis, advanced title General Who Guards the West, ordered to garrison Shouyang as northern border fence and shield.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun rebelled, Zu Yue marched to the capital's defense, camped at Shouyang, drove out Ren Tai, earned a five-grade fief, and was named general who guards the west to hold the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 自以名輩不後郗、卞，而不豫明帝顧命，又望開府，及諸所表請多不見許，遂懷怨望。

translations.literal: He himself thought his name and generation did not fall behind Xi and Bian, yet was not in Emperor Ming's deathbed testament, also hoped to open a headquarters, and the various memorial requests were mostly not granted; thereupon he harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked himself with Xi Jian and Bian Kun yet was omitted from Emperor Ming's regency council, denied an independent command, and nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 石聰嘗以眾逼之，約屢表請救，而官軍不至。

translations.literal: Shi Cong once pressed him with a host; Yue repeatedly memorialized begging rescue, yet government troops did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Cong besieged him; his pleas for relief went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 聰既退，朝議又欲作塗塘以遏胡寇，約謂為棄己，彌懷憤恚。

translations.literal: After Cong withdrew, court discussion again wished to build embankment ponds to block Hu raiders; Yue thought it abandoning himself and grew more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: When the court planned dikes against the Hu, he read it as abandoning his sector and fumed.

sentences.zh: 先是，太后使蔡謨勞之，約見謨，瞋目攘袂，非毀朝政。

translations.literal: Earlier, the empress dowager sent Cai Mo to console him; Yue seeing Mo glared eyes and rolled sleeves, slandering court governance.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Yu sent Cai Mo to comfort him, Zu Yue raged and denounced the government.

sentences.zh: 及蘇峻舉兵，遂推崇約而罪執政，約聞而大喜。

translations.literal: When Su Jun raised troops, they thereupon honored Yue and blamed the chief ministers; Yue hearing was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun rose, praising Zu Yue and attacking the ministers, Zu Yue rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 從子智及衍並傾險好亂，又贊成其事，於是命逖子沛內史渙，女婿淮南太守許柳以兵會峻。

translations.literal: His nephew Zhi and Yan were both treacherous and loved turmoil, and again praised accomplishing the matter; thereupon he ordered Ti's son Administrator of Pei Huan, son-in-law Administrator of Huainan Xu Liu to join Jun with troops.
translations.idiomatic: His nephews Zu Zhi and Zu Yan, both troublemakers, egged him on; he ordered Zu Ti's son Zu Huan and his son-in-law Xu Liu to march with Su Jun.

sentences.zh: 逖妻，柳之姊也，固諫不從。

translations.literal: Ti's wife was Liu's elder sister; she firmly remonstrated but he did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti's widow, Xu Liu's sister, begged him to refuse; he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及峻克京都，矯詔以約為侍中、太尉、尚書令。

translations.literal: When Jun took the capital, he forged an edict appointing Yue palace attendant, grand commandant, and director of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Su Jun seized the capital he forged orders naming Zu Yue palace attendant, grand commandant, and director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 穎川人陳光率其屬攻之，約左右閻禿貌類約，光謂為約而擒之，約逾垣護免。

translations.literal: A man of Yingchuan Chen Guang led his followers to attack him; Yue's attendant Yan Tu resembled Yue in appearance; Guang thought it was Yue and seized him; Yue climbed the wall and escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guang of Yingchuan attacked him; a bodyguard resembled Zu Yue and was taken while Zu Yue scaled a wall and escaped.

sentences.zh: 光奔于石勒，而約之諸將復陰結於勒，請為內應。

translations.literal: Guang fled to Shi Le, yet Yue's various generals again secretly bound with Le, asking to be inner responders.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guang fled to Shi Le; Zu Yue's officers secretly offered Shi Le their help.

sentences.zh: 勒遣石聰來攻之，約眾潰，奔曆陽。

translations.literal: Le sent Shi Cong to attack him; Yue's host scattered; he fled to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le sent Shi Cong; Zu Yue's army collapsed and he ran to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 遣兄子渙攻桓宣於皖城，會毛寶援宣，擊渙，敗之。

translations.literal: He sent his brother's son Huan to attack Huan Xuan at Wancheng; it happened that Mao Bao aided Xuan, struck Huan, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zu Huan against Huan Xuan at Wancheng; Mao Bao relieved Huan Xuan and crushed Zu Huan.

sentences.zh: 趙胤復遣將軍甘苗從三焦上曆陽，約懼而夜遁，其將牽騰率眾出降。

translations.literal: Zhao Yin again sent General Gan Miao from Sanjiao onto Liyang; Yue feared and fled by night; his general Qian Teng led a host out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yin sent Gan Miao down from Sanjiao toward Liyang; Zu Yue fled by night while Qian Teng surrendered.

sentences.zh: 約以左右數百人奔于石勒，勒薄其為人，不見者久之。

translations.literal: Yue with several hundred at left and right fled to Shi Le; Le thought lightly of his person and did not see him for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue reached Shi Le with a few hundred followers; Shi Le despised him and left him waiting.

sentences.zh: 勒將程遐說勒曰：「天下粗定，當顯明逆順，此漢高祖所以斬丁公也。

translations.literal: Le's general Cheng Xia urged Le saying, "The realm is roughly settled; one should make clear rebellion and submission—this is why Han Gaozu beheaded Duke Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xia urged, "The realm is stabilizing; reward loyalty and punish treason—like Han Gaozu executing Duke Ding.

sentences.zh: 今忠於事君者莫不顯擢，背叛不臣者無不夷戮，此天下所以歸伏大王也。

translations.literal: Now those loyal to serving the ruler are none not prominently raised; those who betrayed and did not serve as subjects are none not exterminated and killed—this is why the realm submits to the great king.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty is promoted and treason extirpated—that is why the world bows to you.

sentences.zh: 祖約猶存，臣切惑之。

translations.literal: Zu Yue still exists; your servant is deeply puzzled.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zu Yue still lives—I am baffled.

sentences.zh: 且約大引賓客，又占奪鄉里先人田地，地主多怨。

translations.literal: Moreover Yue greatly drew in guests and again seized by force the village lands of elders in his home district; landlords mostly resented.
translations.idiomatic: He keeps a vast household and has seized ancestral fields at home—landowners hate him.

sentences.zh: 」於是勒乃詐約曰：「祖侯遠來，未得喜歡，可集子弟一時俱會。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Le feigned to Yue saying, "Lord Zu has come from afar; we have not yet had joy; you may gather sons and younger kin all at once to meet.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le feigned welcome: "Lord Zu, let us feast your whole clan.

sentences.zh: 」至日，勒辭之以疾，令遐請約及其宗室。

translations.literal: " When the day came, Le declined on grounds of illness, ordered Xia to invite Yue and his clan kin.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the banquet Shi Le pleaded illness and sent Cheng Xia to summon Zu Yue and his family.

sentences.zh: 約知禍及，大飲致醉。

translations.literal: Yue knew disaster reached him; he drank heavily until drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing death coming, Zu Yue drank himself insensible.

sentences.zh: 既至於市，抱其外孫而泣。

translations.literal: When they reached the market, he embraced his daughter's child and wept.
translations.idiomatic: At the execution ground he clutched his grandson and wept.

sentences.zh: 遂殺之，並其親屬中外百餘人悉滅之，婦女伎妾班賜諸胡。

translations.literal: Thereupon they killed him, together with his kin inside and outside more than a hundred persons all exterminated; women, concubines, and singing girls were distributed to the various Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le slaughtered him and over a hundred kinsmen; women and concubines were handed out to Xiongnu lords.

sentences.zh: 初，逖有胡奴曰王安，待之甚厚。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ti had a Hu slave called Wang An, treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti once owned a Xiongnu slave named Wang An whom he treated with great kindness.

sentences.zh: 及在雍丘，告之曰：「石勒是汝種類，吾亦不在爾一人。

translations.literal: When at Yongqiu, he told him, "Shi Le is of your kind; I also do not care about you alone.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongqiu he told him, "Shi Le is your kinsman; I have no wish to keep you bound.

sentences.zh: 」乃厚資遣之，遂為勒將。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he richly supplied and sent him off, and he became a general under Le.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Wang An rich gifts and sent him away; Wang An became a general under Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 祖氏之誅也，安多將從人於市觀省，潛取逖庶子道重，藏之為沙門，時年十歲。

translations.literal: When the Zu clan was executed, An often led followers to the market to watch and inspect; secretly he took Ti's bastard son Daochong, hid him and made him a monk; at the time he was ten years old.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zu clan was wiped out, Wang An often visited the executions, secretly rescued Zu Ti's bastard son Zu Daochong, and hid him as a novice monk—ten years old.

sentences.zh: 石氏滅後來歸。

translations.literal: After the Shi clan was destroyed he came back.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shi regime fell he returned to the Jin court.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻

translations.literal: Su Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun

sentences.zh: 蘇峻，字子高，長廣掖人也。

translations.literal: Su Jun, courtesy name Zigao, was a man of Ye in Changguang.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun, courtesy name Zigao, came from Ye in Changguang.

sentences.zh: 父模，安樂相。

translations.literal: His father Mo was administrator of Anle.
translations.idiomatic: His father Su Mo was prefect of Anle.

sentences.zh: 峻少為書生，有才學，仕郡主簿。

translations.literal: In youth Jun was a book student, had talent and learning, served the commandery as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was a scholar with literary gifts and served as chief clerk of his commandery.

sentences.zh: 年十八，舉孝廉。

translations.literal: At eighteen he was recommended filial and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he was nominated as filial and incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之亂，百姓流亡，所在屯聚，峻糾合得數千家，結壘於本縣。

translations.literal: In the Yongjia turmoil, the hundred clans drifted and fled; wherever they were they massed in camps; Jun gathered and obtained several thousand households and built fortifications in his home county.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongjia disaster refugees banded together; Su Jun rallied thousands of families and walled his home district.

sentences.zh: 于時豪傑所在屯聚，而峻最強。

translations.literal: At that time heroes everywhere massed in camps, but Jun was strongest.
translations.idiomatic: Among the warlords of the day his camp was the strongest.

sentences.zh: 遣長史徐瑋宣檄諸屯，示以王化，又收枯骨而葬之，遠近感其恩義，推峻為主。

translations.literal: He sent chief clerk Xu Wei to proclaim proclamation to the various camps, showing them royal transformation; again he gathered dry bones and buried them; far and near were moved by his grace and righteousness, and pushed Jun as leader.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xu Wei with proclamations preaching imperial virtue, collected bones for burial, and won such gratitude that the camps made him their chief.

sentences.zh: 遂射獵于海邊青山中。

translations.literal: Thereupon he hunted with bow in the green hills by the sea.
translations.idiomatic: He then hunted along the coastal hills.

sentences.zh: 元帝聞之，假峻安集將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan heard of it and credentialled Jun General Who Pacifies and Gathers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan named him general who pacifies and gathers.

sentences.zh: 時曹嶷領青州刺史，表峻為掖令，峻辭疾不受。

translations.literal: At that time Cao Yi held Qing Province and memorialized Jun as magistrate of Ye; Jun declined illness and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yi, governor of Qingzhou, offered him the magistracy of Ye; Su Jun pleaded illness and refused.

sentences.zh: 嶷惡其得眾，恐必為患，將討之。

translations.literal: Yi hated that he won the host and feared he would surely become a scourge and was about to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yi resented his popularity and planned to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 峻懼，率其所部數百家泛海南渡。

translations.literal: Jun feared, led his command of several hundred households and floated the sea south to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun fled south by sea with hundreds of families.

sentences.zh: 既到廣陵，朝廷嘉其遠至，轉鷹揚將軍。

translations.literal: When he reached Guangling, the court praised his coming from afar and transferred him General Who Raises the Hawk.
translations.idiomatic: The court welcomed him at Guangling and promoted him to general who raises the hawk.

sentences.zh: 會周堅反于彭城，峻助討之，有功，除淮陵內史，遷蘭陵相。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhou Jian rebelled at Pengcheng; Jun assisted in punishing him, had merit, was appointed interior minister of Huailing, transferred administrator of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: He helped crush Zhou Jian's revolt at Pengcheng, earned a post as interior minister of Huailing, then prefect of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 王敦作逆，詔峻討敦。

translations.literal: Wang Dun acted in rebellion; an edict ordered Jun to punish Dun.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun rebelled, Su Jun was ordered against him.

sentences.zh: 卜之不吉，遲回不進。

translations.literal: Divining it was not auspicious, he hesitated and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Omens were bad; he stalled.

sentences.zh: 及王師敗績，峻退保盱眙。

translations.literal: When the royal army suffered defeat, Jun withdrew to guard Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: After the imperial army lost, he fell back to Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 淮陵故吏徐深、艾毅重請峻為內史，詔聽之，加奮威將軍。

translations.literal: Huailing's former clerks Xu Shen and Ai Yi earnestly begged Jun to be interior minister; an edict permitted it, adding General Who Rouses Might.
translations.idiomatic: His old Huailing subordinates begged him back as interior minister; the court agreed and added the title general who rouses might.

sentences.zh: 太甯初，更除臨淮內史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taining, he was again appointed interior minister of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taining era he became interior minister of Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 王敦復肆逆，尚書令郗鑒議召峻及劉遐援京都，敦遣峻兄說峻曰：「富貴可坐取，何為自來送死？

translations.literal: Wang Dun again acted in rebellion; Director of the Secretariat Xi Jian proposed summoning Jun and Liu Xia to aid the capital; Dun sent Jun's elder brother to persuade Jun saying, "Wealth and nobility can be taken sitting—why come yourself to deliver death?
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun rebelled again, Xi Jian called Su Jun and Liu Xia to the capital. Wang Dun sent Su Jun's brother to argue, "Riches are yours for the taking—why march to your death?

sentences.zh: 」峻不從，遂率眾赴京師，頓于司徒故府。

translations.literal: " Jun did not follow, thereupon led a host toward the capital and encamped at the former office of the minister of education.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun refused, marched to the capital, and camped at the old ministry of education.

sentences.zh: 道遠行速，軍人疲困。

translations.literal: The road was long and march fast; soldiers were weary and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The forced march exhausted his men.

sentences.zh: 沈充、錢鳳謀曰：「北軍新到，未堪攻戰，擊之必克。

translations.literal: Shen Chong and Qian Feng plotted saying, "The northern army has newly arrived and cannot bear attack and battle; striking them will surely overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong and Qian Feng plotted: "Su Jun's northerners are tired—strike now and we win.

sentences.zh: 若復猶豫，後難犯也」賊於其夜度竹格渚，拔柵將戰，峻率其將韓晃于南塘橫截，大破之。

translations.literal: If again hesitating, later will be hard to attack." The rebels that night crossed Zhuge islet, pulled palisades and were about to fight; Jun led his general Han Huang to block horizontally at South Pond Bridge and routed them badly.
translations.idiomatic: Delay only makes them stronger." That night the rebels crossed Bamboo Ford; Su Jun intercepted them at the South Pond bridge with Han Huang and shattered them.

sentences.zh: 又隨庾亮追破沈充。

translations.literal: Again he followed Yu Liang in pursuit and broke Shen Chong.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Yu Liang in running down Shen Chong.

sentences.zh: 進使持節、冠軍將軍、曆陽內史，加散騎常侍，封邵陵公，食邑一千八百戶。

translations.literal: He was advanced credential-bearing, General Who Crowns the Army, interior minister of Liyang, concurrent palace attendant regular cavalry, enfeoffed Duke of Shaoling with one thousand eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was named credential-bearing general who crowns the army, interior minister of Liyang, concurrent palace attendant, and duke of Shaoling with eighteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 峻本以單家聚眾於擾攘之際，歸順之後，志在立功，既有功于國，威望漸著。

translations.literal: Jun originally from a single family gathered a host at a time of turmoil; after submitting, his aim was to establish merit; once he had merit for the state, his martial fame gradually showed.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner who rose in chaos, he had served the throne loyally and grown formidable.

sentences.zh: 至是有銳卒萬人，器械甚精，朝廷以江外寄之。

translations.literal: By then he had crack troops ten thousand, weapons and gear very fine; the court entrusted him with the lands beyond the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded ten thousand well-armed veterans and held the entire lower Yangtze for the court.

sentences.zh: 而峻頗懷驕溢，自負其眾，潛有異志，撫納亡命，得罪之家有逃死者，峻輒蔽匿之。

translations.literal: Yet Jun quite harbored arrogance and overflow, priding himself on his host, secretly having a different intent, soothing and accepting fugitives from justice—houses that had offended and fled death, Jun always sheltered them.
translations.idiomatic: But success bred arrogance: he hid fugitives and nursed secret ambitions.

sentences.zh: 眾力日多，皆仰食縣官，運漕者相屬，稍有不如意，便肆忿言。

translations.literal: Host strength daily increased; all relied on food from the county office; transport convoys followed one another; slightly not to his wish, he then vented angry words.
translations.idiomatic: His army swelled on state grain; convoys lined the roads, and he cursed at the slightest slight.

sentences.zh: 時明帝初崩，委政宰輔，護軍庾亮欲徵之。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Ming had newly died; government was entrusted to chief ministers; Guard General Yu Liang wished to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died, Yu Liang, as regent's ally, decided to recall him.

sentences.zh: 峻聞將徵，遣司馬何仍詣亮曰：「討賊外任，遠近從命，至於內輔，實非所堪。

translations.literal: When Jun heard he would be summoned, he sent marshal He Reng to Liang saying, "Punishing bandits as outer post, far and near follow orders; as for inner assistance, truly I am not capable.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun sent He Reng to Yu Liang: "I will fight rebels on the frontier, but I am unfit for court duty.

sentences.zh: 」不從，遂下優詔徵峻為大司農，加散騎常侍，位特進，以弟逸代領部曲。

translations.literal: " They did not follow; thereupon they issued a gracious edict summoning Jun as minister of agriculture, adding palace attendant regular cavalry, specially advanced rank, and younger brother Yi to replace command of the host.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused and offered him minister of agriculture, a hollow honor, while his brother Su Yi took his troops.

sentences.zh: 峻素疑帝欲害己，表曰：「昔明皇帝親執臣手，使臣北討胡寇。

translations.literal: Jun always suspected the emperor wished to harm him; he memorialized saying, "Formerly the enlightened emperor personally grasped your servant's hand, ordering your servant to campaign north against Hu bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun suspected a trap and wrote, "The late emperor clasped my hand and bade me fight the Hu.

sentences.zh: 今中原未靖，無用家為，乞補青州界一荒郡，以展鷹犬之用。

translations.literal: Now the central plain is not yet quiet; I have no use for home; I beg to fill a waste commandery in Qing Province's bounds, to display hound and hawk use.
translations.idiomatic: The north is still unsettled—assign me some frontier backwater in Qingzhou instead.

sentences.zh: 」復不許。

translations.literal: " Again not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Again the court refused.

sentences.zh: 峻嚴裝將赴召，而猶豫未決，參軍任讓謂峻曰：「將軍求處荒郡而不見許，事勢如此，恐無生路，不如勒兵自守。

translations.literal: Jun rigged gear about to answer the summons, yet hesitated undecided; aide Ren Rang said to Jun, "The general begged a waste commandery and was not granted; the situation being thus, I fear there is no road to life—better to bind troops and guard yourself.
translations.idiomatic: His aide Ren Rang said, "They deny you even a border post—you are a dead man unless you keep your army.

sentences.zh: 」峻從之，遂不應命。

translations.literal: " Jun followed this; thereupon he did not answer the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun listened and defied the recall.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣使諷諭之，峻曰：「臺下云我欲反，豈得活邪！

translations.literal: The court sent envoys to persuade him; Jun said, "The terrace below says I wish to rebel—how can I stay alive!
translations.idiomatic: When envoys reasoned with him, he snapped, "The court already calls me traitor—what life is left?

sentences.zh: 我甯山頭望廷尉，不能廷尉望山頭。

translations.literal: I would rather watch the commandery of justice from a hilltop than let the commandery of justice watch me from a hilltop.
translations.idiomatic: Better I watch the executioner from a mountain than the other way around.

sentences.zh: 往者國危累卵，非我不濟，狡兔既死，獵犬理自應烹，但當死報造謀者耳。

translations.literal: Formerly the state was perilous as piled eggs; without me it would not have been saved; when the cunning rabbit is dead, the hunting dog by principle should be boiled—only I should die repaying the schemer.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was eggshell-fragile until I saved it; now the rabbit is dead and they mean to stew the hound—I will die cursing the plotters.

sentences.zh: 」於是遣參軍徐會結祖約，謀為亂，而以討亮為名。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he sent aide Xu Hui to bind Zu Yue, plotting to make turmoil, while taking punishing Liang as name.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xu Hui to ally with Zu Yue, planning revolt under the slogan of punishing Yu Liang.

sentences.zh: 約遣祖渙、許柳率眾助峻，峻遣將韓晃、張健等襲姑孰，進逼慈湖，殺于湖令陶馥及振威將軍司馬流。

translations.literal: Yue sent Zu Huan and Xu Liu to lead hosts aiding Jun; Jun sent generals Han Huang and Zhang Jian to raid Gushu, advanced pressing Cihu, killed magistrate of Yuhu Tao Fu and General Who Rouses Might Sima Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue sent Zu Huan and Xu Liu; Su Jun sent Han Huang and Zhang Jian to seize Gushu, push on Cihu, and kill Tao Fu, magistrate of Yuhu, and Sima Liu, general who rouses might.

sentences.zh: 峻自率渙、柳眾萬人，乘風濟自橫江，次於陵口，與王師戰，頻捷，遂據蔣陵覆舟山，率眾因風放火，台省及諸營寺署一時蕩盡。

translations.literal: Jun personally led Huan and Liu's host of ten thousand, crossed from Hengjiang riding the wind, halted at Lingkou, fought the royal army, repeatedly won, thereupon held Fuzhou Mountain by the Jiang mausoleum, led the host setting fire with the wind; terrace offices and the various camp temples and bureaus were in one sweep swept bare.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun himself led ten thousand men across Hengjiang with a fair wind, beat the imperial army at Lingkou, seized Mount Fuzhou east of Moling, and burned the palace quarter to ash.

sentences.zh: 遂陷宮城，縱兵大掠，侵逼六宮，窮凶極暴，殘酷無道。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took the palace city, let soldiers plunder on a great scale, encroached and pressed the six palaces, utterly fierce and violent, cruel without the Way.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed the palace, unleashed looting, terrorized the harem, and ruled with savagery.

sentences.zh: 驅役百官，光祿勳王彬等皆被捶撻，逼令擔負登蔣山。

translations.literal: He drove and conscripted the hundred officials; Director of Retainers Wang Bin and others were all flogged and beaten, forced to shoulder loads and climb Mount Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: He drove ministers like Wang Bin up Mount Jiang under the lash, laden with baggage.

sentences.zh: 裸剝士女，皆以壞席苫草自鄣，無草者坐地以土自覆，哀號之聲震動內外。

translations.literal: Stripping men and women of gentry, all used ruined mats and straw grass to screen themselves; those without grass sat on the ground covering themselves with earth; sounds of wailing shook inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: Noblewomen were stripped and hid behind straw mats or smeared themselves with mud; their wails shook the city.

sentences.zh: 時官有布二十萬匹，金銀五千斤，錢億萬，絹數萬匹，他物稱是，峻盡費之。

translations.literal: At that time the office had two hundred thousand bolts of cloth, five thousand jin of gold and silver, a hundred million cash, several tens of thousands of bolts of silk, other goods matching these; Jun exhausted them all.
translations.idiomatic: He burned through two hundred thousand bolts of cloth, five thousand pounds of bullion, a hundred million cash, and countless silk.

sentences.zh: 矯詔大赦，惟庾亮兄弟不在原例。

translations.literal: He forged an edict of great amnesty; only Yu Liang's brothers were not within the original rule.
translations.idiomatic: He forged a general amnesty that excluded only Yu Liang and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 自為驃騎領軍將軍、錄尚書事，許柳丹陽尹，加前將軍馬雄左衛將軍，祖渙驍騎將軍，復弋陽王羕為西陽王、太宰、錄尚書事，羕息播亦復本官。

translations.literal: He made himself chariot-and-horse cavalry general commanding the army, concurrent recorder of the secretariat; Xu Liu was Danyang intendant; added front general Ma Xiong as left guard general, Zu Huan as fierce cavalry general; restored Prince of Yiyang Sima Yang as Prince of Xiyang, grand tutor, recorder of the secretariat; Yang's son Bo also restored original office.
translations.idiomatic: He named himself cavalry general-in-chief and director of the secretariat, Xu Liu as Danyang governor, Ma Xiong as left guard general, Zu Huan as fierce cavalry general, and restored Sima Yang as prince of Xiyang and grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 於是改易官司，置其親黨，朝廷政事一皆由之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he changed and replaced offices, installed his intimate partisans; court governance all proceeded from him.
translations.idiomatic: He packed the government with his own men and ruled by fiat.

sentences.zh: 又遣韓晃入義興，張健、管商、弘徽等入晉陵。

translations.literal: Again he sent Han Huang into Yixing, Zhang Jian, Guan Shang, Hong Hui and others into Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Han Huang to Yixing and Zhang Jian, Guan Shang, and Hong Hui toward Jinling.

sentences.zh: 時溫嶠、陶侃已唱義于武昌，峻聞兵起，用參軍賈甯計，還據石頭，更分兵距諸義軍，所過無不殘滅。

translations.literal: At that time Wen Jiao and Tao Kan had already raised righteousness at Wuchang; Jun hearing troops rose, used aide Jia Ning's plan, withdrew to hold Stone City, again divided troops to oppose the various righteous armies; wherever they passed none were not destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Jiao and Tao Kan rose at Wuchang, Su Jun took Jia Ning's advice, fell back to Stone City, and savaged every loyalist force in his path.

sentences.zh: 嶠等將至，峻遂遷天子于石頭，逼迫居人，盡聚之後苑，使懷德令匡術守苑城。

translations.literal: When Jiao and the rest were about to arrive, Jun thereupon moved the Son of Heaven to Stone City, pressed the residents, gathered them all in the rear garden, ordered Magistrate of Huaide Kuang Shu to guard the garden city.
translations.idiomatic: As Wen Jiao approached, Su Jun moved the emperor to Stone City, herded citizens into the imperial park, and left Kuang Shu to hold it.

sentences.zh: 嶠等既到，乃築壘于白石，峻率眾攻之，幾至陷沒。

translations.literal: When Jiao and the rest arrived, they then built fortifications at Baishi; Jun led a host attacking them, almost to the point of taking them.
translations.idiomatic: The loyalists walled Baishi; Su Jun nearly overran them.

sentences.zh: 東西抄掠，多所擒虜，兵威日盛，戰無不克，由是義眾沮衄，人懷異計。

translations.literal: East and west raiding and plundering, many captures; military might daily grew; battle none not won; hence the righteous host was dispirited and men harbored different plans.
translations.idiomatic: His raiders swelled his power until the loyalists despaired.

sentences.zh: 朝士之奔義軍者，皆云：「峻狡黠有智力，其徒黨驍勇，所向無敵。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen who fled to the righteous army all said, "Jun is cunning and has wits and strength; his followers are fierce and brave; where they turn none withstand.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees from court called Su Jun a brilliant fighter with invincible troops.

sentences.zh: 惟當以天討有罪，誅滅不久；

translations.literal: Only should heaven punish the guilty; extermination will not be long;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven will destroy him soon enough;

sentences.zh: 若以人事言之，未易除也。

translations.literal: if judged by human affairs, he is not easy to remove.
translations.idiomatic: but by human reckoning he is almost impossible to beat.

sentences.zh: 」溫嶠怒曰：「諸君怯懦，乃是譽賊。

translations.literal: " Wen Jiao angrily said, "You gentlemen are cowardly—this is praising the bandit.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jiao thundered, "You are only glorifying the rebel.

sentences.zh: 」及後累戰不捷，嶠亦深憚之。

translations.literal: " When afterward repeated battles did not succeed, Jiao also deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated defeats Wen Jiao feared him too.

sentences.zh: 管商等進攻吳郡，焚吳縣、海監、嘉興，敗諸義軍。

translations.literal: Guan Shang and the others advanced attacking Wu commandery, burned Wu county, Haijian, Jiaxing, defeated the various righteous armies.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Shang burned Wu, Haijian, and Jiaxing and broke loyalist columns.

sentences.zh: 韓晃又攻宣城，害太守桓彝。

translations.literal: Han Huang again attacked Xuancheng and killed Administrator Huan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang took Xuancheng and killed Huan Yi.

sentences.zh: 商等又焚余杭，而大敗于武康，退還義興。

translations.literal: Shang and the others again burned Yuhang, yet were greatly defeated at Wukang, withdrew returning to Yixing.
