translations.idiomatic: They torched Yuhang but were routed at Wukang and fled to Yixing.

sentences.zh: 嶠與趙胤率步兵萬人，從白石南上，欲以臨之。

translations.literal: Jiao with Zhao Yin led foot soldiers ten thousand, from Baishi south upward, wishing thereby to press him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jiao and Zhao Yin marched ten thousand infantry south from Baishi to pressure Su Jun.

sentences.zh: 峻與匡孝將八千人逆戰，峻遣子碩與孝以數十騎先薄趙胤，敗之。

translations.literal: Jun with Kuang Xiao led eight thousand to meet battle; Jun sent son Shuo with Xiao with several tens of horse first to press Zhao Yin, defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun and Kuang Xiao met them with eight thousand men; Su Shuo and Kuang Xiao rode ahead, broke Zhao Yin.

sentences.zh: 峻望見胤走，曰：「孝能破賊，我更不如乎！

translations.literal: Jun seeing Yin flee said, "Xiao can break bandits—am I still not as good!
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Zhao Yin run, Su Jun cried, "If Kuang Xiao can rout them, surely I can do better!

sentences.zh: 」因舍其眾，與數騎北下突陣，不得入，將回趨白木陂，牙門彭世、李千等投之以矛，墜馬，斬首臠割之，焚其骨，三軍皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he abandoned his host, with several tens of horse charged north into the formation, could not enter, was about to turn toward Baimu slope; gate officer Peng Shi, Li Qian and others threw spears at him; he fell from horse, was beheaded and carved, his bones burned; the three armies all shouted ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: He spurred a handful of riders into the loyalist line, was turned back, and fleeing toward Baimu marsh was speared from the saddle by Peng Shi and Li Qian, beheaded, hacked to pieces, and burned while his men cheered.

sentences.zh: 峻司馬任讓等共立峻弟逸為主。

translations.literal: Jun's marshal Ren Rang and others together set up Jun's younger brother Yi as leader.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Rang and the rest proclaimed Su Jun's brother Su Yi leader.

sentences.zh: 求峻屍不獲，碩乃發庾亮父母墓，剖棺焚屍。

translations.literal: Seeking Jun's corpse they did not obtain it; Shuo thereupon opened Yu Liang's parents' tomb, split the coffins and burned the corpses.
translations.idiomatic: When they could not find Su Jun's body, Su Shuo desecrated Yu Liang's parents' graves.

sentences.zh: 逸閉城自守。

translations.literal: Yi closed the city and held self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Su Yi barred the gates.

sentences.zh: 韓晃聞峻死，引兵赴石頭。

translations.literal: When Han Huang heard Jun had died, he led troops toward Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang raced to Stone City on news of Su Jun's death.

sentences.zh: 管商及弘徽進攻庱亭壘，督護李閎及輕車長史滕含擊破之，斬首千級。

translations.literal: Guan Shang and Hong Hui advanced attacking the Ting fortress; commandant protector Li Hong and light chariot aide Teng Han struck and broke them, beheading a thousand grades.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Shang and Hong Hui assaulted the Ting camp; Li Hong and Teng Han repulsed them with a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 商率眾走延陵，李閎與庱亭諸軍追之，斬獲數千級。

translations.literal: Shang led a host fleeing to Yanling; Li Hong with the Ting armies pursued them, beheading and capturing several thousand grades.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Shang fled toward Yanling; Li Hong ran him down and killed thousands.

sentences.zh: 商詣庾亮降，匡術舉苑城降。

translations.literal: Shang went to Yu Liang to surrender; Kuang Shu raised the garden city to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Shang surrendered to Yu Liang; Kuang Shu yielded the park.

sentences.zh: 韓晃與蘇逸等並力攻術，不能陷。

translations.literal: Han Huang with Su Yi and others together attacked Shu and could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang and Su Yi besieged Kuang Shu in vain.

sentences.zh: 溫嶠等選精銳將攻賊營，碩率驍勇數百渡淮而戰，於陣斬碩。

translations.literal: Wen Jiao and others picked crack generals to attack the bandit camp; Shuo led several hundred fierce brave crossed the Huai to fight; they beheaded Shuo in the formation.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jiao's picked troops stormed the rebel camp; Su Shuo fell in battle on the Huai.

sentences.zh: 晃等震懼，以其眾奔張健于曲阿，門厄不得出，更相蹈藉，死者萬數。

translations.literal: Huang and the rest were shaken and feared, led their host fleeing to Zhang Jian at Qu'e; the gate was narrow and they could not exit; they trampled one another; dead numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang's men stampeded toward Qu'e, jammed the gates, and trampled tens of thousands to death.

sentences.zh: 逸為李湯所執，斬于車騎府。

translations.literal: Yi was seized by Li Tang, beheaded at the chariot-and-horse office.
translations.idiomatic: Su Yi was captured by Li Tang and executed at the cavalry command.

sentences.zh: 管商之降也，餘眾並歸張健。

translations.literal: When Guan Shang surrendered, the remaining host all returned to Zhang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Shang's survivors joined Zhang Jian.

sentences.zh: 健又疑弘徽等不與己同，盡殺之，更以舟軍自延陵向長塘，小大二萬餘口，金銀寶物不可勝數。

translations.literal: Jian again suspected Hong Hui and others did not share his mind, killed them all, again used boat army from Yanling toward Changtang, small and large more than twenty thousand mouths, gold and silver treasures beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian murdered Hong Hui and other waverers, then sailed from Yanling toward Changtang with twenty thousand followers and incalculable loot.

sentences.zh: 揚烈將軍王允之與吳興諸軍擊健，大破之，獲男女萬餘口。

translations.literal: General Who Rouses Might Wang Yunzhi with Wu-Xing various armies struck Jian, routed him badly, capturing men and women more than ten thousand mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yunzhi, general who rouses might, and the Wu-Xing forces shattered Zhang Jian and took ten thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 健復與馬雄、韓晃等輕軍俱走，閎率銳兵追之，及於岩山，攻之甚急。

translations.literal: Jian again with Ma Xiong, Han Huang and others light army all fled; Hong led crack troops pursuing them, caught up at Yanshan, attacked them very urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian, Ma Xiong, and Han Huang fled light; Li Hong ran them down at Yanshan and pressed hard.

sentences.zh: 健等不敢下山，惟晃獨出，帶兩步靫箭，卻據胡床，彎弓射之，傷殺甚眾。

translations.literal: Jian and the others did not dare go down the mountain; only Huang alone came out, wearing two foot quivers of arrows, stepped back to occupy a folding stool, bent bow and shot them, wounding and killing very many.
translations.idiomatic: Trapped on the heights, Han Huang alone sallied forth with paired quivers, sat on a camp stool, and shot wave after wave of loyalists.

sentences.zh: 箭盡，乃斬之。

translations.literal: When arrows were exhausted, thereupon they beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When his arrows ran out they cut him down.

sentences.zh: 健等遂降，並梟其首。

translations.literal: Jian and the others thereupon surrendered, together displaying their heads.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian capitulated; their heads went to the gibbet.

sentences.zh: 孫恩

translations.literal: Sun En.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En

sentences.zh: 孫恩，字靈秀，琅邪人，孫秀之族也。

translations.literal: Sun En, courtesy name Lingxiu, was a man of Langya, of Sun Xiu's clan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En, courtesy name Lingxiu, came from Langya and belonged to Sun Xiu's clan.

sentences.zh: 世奉五斗米道。

translations.literal: For generations they revered the Five Pecks of Rice Way.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long followed the Way of the Five Pecks of Rice.

sentences.zh: 恩叔父泰，字敬遠，師事錢唐杜子恭。

translations.literal: En's uncle Tai, courtesy name Jingyuan, took as teacher Du Zigong of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Sun Tai studied under Du Zigong of Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 而子恭有秘術，嘗就人借瓜刀，其主求之，子恭曰：「當即相還耳。

translations.literal: And Zigong had secret arts; once he borrowed a melon knife from someone; its master asked for it back; Zigong said, "I shall return it immediately.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zigong knew occult arts: borrowing a melon knife, he told its owner, "You shall have it back presently.

sentences.zh: 」既而刀主行至嘉興，有魚躍入船中，破魚得瓜刀。

translations.literal: " Later the knife's master walked to Jiaxing; a fish leaped into the boat; splitting the fish they obtained the melon knife.
translations.idiomatic: When the owner reached Jiaxing, a fish leapt into his boat; inside it lay the lost knife.

sentences.zh: 其為神效往往如此。

translations.literal: His spirit efficacy was often thus.
translations.idiomatic: His miracles were always of that sort.

sentences.zh: 子恭死，泰傳其術。

translations.literal: When Zigong died, Tai transmitted his arts.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Zigong died, Sun Tai inherited his techniques.

sentences.zh: 然浮狡有小才，誑誘百姓，愚者敬之如神，皆竭財產，進子女，以祈福慶。

translations.literal: Yet he was floating and crafty with small talent, deceiving and enticing the hundred clans; fools revered him as spirit, all exhausted wealth and property, advanced sons and daughters, to pray for blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tai was a smooth charlatan: the credulous worshiped him like a god, bankrupting themselves to offer children and treasure for blessings.

sentences.zh: 王珣言于會稽王道子，流之于廣州。

translations.literal: Wang Xun spoke to Prince of Kuaiji Daozi, who banished him to Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun warned Sima Daozi, prince of Kuaiji, who exiled Sun Tai to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 廣州刺史王懷之以泰行郁林太守，南越亦歸之。

translations.literal: Inspector of Guang Province Wang Huai zhi appointed Tai acting Administrator of Yulin; the southern Yue also submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huaizhi, inspector of Guangzhou, named him acting prefect of Yulin; the south submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 太子少傅王雅先與泰善，言于孝武帝，以泰知養性之方，因召還。

translations.literal: Junior tutor to the crown prince Wang Ya earlier was on good terms with Tai; he spoke to Emperor Xiaowu that Tai knew methods of nurturing nature; therefore summoned him back.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya, the crown prince's tutor, told Emperor Xiaowu that Sun Tai knew longevity arts; the emperor recalled him.

sentences.zh: 道子以為徐州主簿，猶以道術眩惑士庶。

translations.literal: Daozi made him chief clerk of Xu Province, still using the Way arts to dazzle gentry and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Daozi made him Xuzhou chief clerk and kept dazzling people with sorcery.

sentences.zh: 稍遷輔國將軍、新安太守。

translations.literal: Gradually he was promoted General Who Supports the State and Administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to general who supports the state and prefect of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 王恭之役，泰私合義兵，得數千人，為國討恭。

translations.literal: In Wang Gong's campaign, Tai privately combined righteous troops, obtained several thousand men, and for the state punished Gong.
translations.idiomatic: During Wang Gong's revolt he raised several thousand loyalist militia on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 黃門郎孔道、鄱陽太守桓放之、驃騎諮議周勰等皆敬事之，會稽世子元顯亦數詣泰求其秘術。

translations.literal: Gentleman at the Yellow Gate Kong Dao, Administrator of Poyang Huan Fangzhi, consultant to the chariot-and-horse general Zhou Xie and others all reverently served him; the heir of Kuaiji Yuanxian also repeatedly visited Tai seeking his secret arts.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Dao, Huan Fangzhi, Zhou Xie, and others courted him; Sima Yuanxian, heir of Kuaiji, constantly sought his secrets.

sentences.zh: 泰見天下兵起，以為晉祚將終，乃扇動百姓，私集徒眾，三吳士庶多從之。

translations.literal: Tai seeing arms rise everywhere thought the Jin mandate would end; thereupon he stirred the hundred clans, privately gathered followers; gentry and commoners of the three Wu mostly followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing chaos everywhere, Sun Tai decided the Jin dynasty was finished; he rallied the Three Wu until multitudes followed him.

sentences.zh: 于時朝士皆懼泰為亂，以其與元顯交厚，咸莫敢言。

translations.literal: At that time court gentlemen all feared Tai would make turmoil; because he was thick with Yuanxian, none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: The court feared him but dared not speak—he was too close to Sima Yuanxian.

sentences.zh: 會稽內史謝輶發其謀，道子誅之。

translations.literal: Interior minister of Kuaijie Xie You exposed his plot; Daozi executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xie You, interior minister of Kuaiji, exposed the plot; Sima Daozi executed Sun Tai.

sentences.zh: 恩逃於海。

translations.literal: En fled to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En fled to the sea.

sentences.zh: 眾聞泰死，惑之，皆謂蟬蛻登仙，故就海中資給。

translations.literal: The host hearing Tai died were perplexed; all said he had sloughed his shell and ascended as immortal; therefore they went to the sea to supply him.
translations.idiomatic: His followers believed Sun Tai had shed his corpse like a cicada and become immortal; they flocked to the coast to sustain Sun En.

sentences.zh: 恩聚合亡命得百餘人，志欲復仇。

translations.literal: En gathered fugitives and obtained more than a hundred men; his aim was to avenge.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En rallied a hundred outlaws bent on revenge.

sentences.zh: 及元顯縱暴吳會，百姓不安，恩因其騷動，自海攻上虞，殺縣令，因襲會稽，害內史王凝之，有眾數萬。

translations.literal: When Yuanxian wantonly oppressed Wu and Hui and the hundred clans were not at peace, En exploited their unrest, attacked Shangyu from the sea, killed the magistrate, thereupon raided Kuaiji, killed Interior Minister Wang Ningzhi, and had a host of several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yuanxian tyrannized Wu, Sun En struck from the sea, took Shangyu, stormed Kuaiji, slew Wang Ningzhi, and amassed tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 於是會稽謝鍼、吳郡陸瑰、吳興丘尪、義興許允之、臨海周胄、永嘉張永及東陽、新安等凡八郡，一時俱起，殺長史以應之，旬日之中，眾數十萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon Kuaiji's Xie Zhen, Wu's Lu Gui, Wu-Xing's Qiu Wang, Yixing's Xu Yunzhi, Linhai's Zhou Zhou, Yongjia's Zhang Yong, and Dongyang, Xin'an—eight commanderies in all—rose at once, killed chief clerks to answer him; within ten days the host was several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Eight commanderies—Kuaiji, Wu, Wu-Xing, Yixing, Linhai, Yongjia, Dongyang, Xin'an—rose together, slew officials, and within days he had hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 於是吳興太守謝邈，永嘉太守謝逸，嘉興公顧胤，南康公謝明慧，黃門郎謝沖、張琨，中書郎孔道，太子洗馬孔福，烏程令夏侯愔等皆遇害。

translations.literal: Thereupon Administrator of Wu-Xing Xie Miao, Administrator of Yongjia Xie Yi, Duke of Jiaxing Gu Yin, Duke of Nankang Xie Minghui, Gentlemen at the Yellow Gate Xie Chong and Zhang Kun, Palace Secretary Kong Dao, crown prince attendant Kong Fu, Magistrate of Wucheng Xiahou Yin and others all met harm.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Miao, Xie Yi, Gu Yin, Xie Minghui, Xie Chong, Zhang Kun, Kong Dao, Kong Fu, Xiahou Yin, and many more were killed.

sentences.zh: 吳國內史桓謙，義興太守魏傿，臨海太守、新蔡王崇等並出奔。

translations.literal: Interior Minister of Wu Huan Qian, Administrator of Yixing Wei Yi, Administrator of Linhai and Prince of Xincai Chong and others all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Qian, Wei Yi, Sima Chong, and others fled.

sentences.zh: 於是恩據會稽，自號征東將軍，號其党曰「長生人」，宣語令誅殺異己，有不同者戮及嬰孩，由是死者十七八。

translations.literal: Thereupon En held Kuaiji, styled himself General Who Conquers the East, named his party "Long-lived People," proclaimed orders to kill those unlike themselves; whoever differed infants were slaughtered with them—hence dead were seven or eight in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En seized Kuaiji, styled himself general who conquers the east, called his followers the Long-Lifers, and ordered the slaughter of all dissenters, infants included—seven or eight in ten died.

sentences.zh: 畿內諸縣處處蜂起，朝廷震懼，內外戒嚴。

translations.literal: Within the capital region the various counties everywhere rose like hornets; the court was shaken and feared; inside and outside were under strict arms.
translations.idiomatic: The heartland exploded in revolt; the court declared martial law.

sentences.zh: 遣衛將軍謝琰、鎮北將軍劉牢之討之，並轉鬥而前。

translations.literal: They sent Guard General Xie Yan and General Who Guards the North Liu Lao zhi to punish them, both turning battle and advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yan and Liu Laozhi marched against them.

sentences.zh: 吳會承平日久，人不習戰，又無器械，故所在多被破亡。

translations.literal: Wu and Hui had long been at peace; people did not practice war, and moreover had no weapons; therefore wherever they were many were broken and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu had known peace for generations—untrained and unarmed, town after town fell.

sentences.zh: 諸賊皆燒倉廩，焚邑屋，刊木堙井，虜掠財貨，相率聚於會稽。

translations.literal: The various bandits all burned granaries, fired towns and houses, cut trees and blocked wells, plundered goods, and in succession gathered at Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: They torched granaries and villages, felled trees, filled wells, looted, and converged on Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 其婦女有嬰累不能去者，囊簏盛嬰兒投于水，而告之曰：「賀汝先登仙堂，我尋後就汝。」

translations.literal: Their women who had infants they could not leave stuffed infants in baskets and threw them in the water, telling them, "I congratulate you on first ascending the immortal hall—I will soon follow you."
translations.idiomatic: Women who could not flee drowned their babies in baskets, crying, "You go first to paradise—I follow soon."

sentences.zh: 初，恩聞八郡回應，告其屬曰：「天下無復事矣，當與諸君朝服而至建康。

translations.literal: Earlier, when En heard eight commanderies answered, he told his followers, "Under heaven there is no more business; I ought with you gentlemen in court dress arrive at Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: When eight commanderies rose, Sun En told his men, "The realm is ours—we will enter Jianye in court robes.

sentences.zh: 」既聞牢之臨江，復曰：「我割浙江，不失作句踐也。

translations.literal: " When he heard Laozhi approached the Yangtze, he again said, "I will cut off the Zhe River—not failing to be another Gou Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Liu Laozhi had reached the river, he said, "I can still hold the Zhe like Gou Jian of Yue.

sentences.zh: 」尋知牢之已濟江，乃曰：「孤不羞走矣。

translations.literal: " Soon knowing Laozhi had already crossed the river, he said, "I am not ashamed to run.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned Liu Laozhi had crossed, he muttered, "Flight is no shame.

sentences.zh: 」乃虜男女二十餘萬口，一時逃入海。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he seized more than two hundred thousand men and women and at once fled into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: He dragged two hundred thousand captives into the sea with him.

sentences.zh: 懼官軍之躡，乃緣道多棄寶物子女。

translations.literal: Fearing government troops tracking, he along the road much abandoned treasure and children.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing pursuit, he strewed loot and captives along the roads.

sentences.zh: 時東土殷實，莫不粲麗盈目，牢之等遽於收斂，故恩復得逃海。

translations.literal: At that time the eastern lands were rich and solid; none were not splendid and lovely filling the eye; Lao zhi and the rest hurried in gathering, therefore En again could flee to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: The rich eastern plain glittered with his discarded plunder; Liu Laozhi's men stopped to scoop it up, letting Sun En escape seaward.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以謝琰為會稽，率徐州文武戍海浦。

translations.literal: The court made Xie Yan Kuaiji and led Xu Province civil and military to garrison the sea shore.
translations.idiomatic: The court named Xie Yan governor of Kuaiji and posted Xuzhou troops along the coast.

sentences.zh: ，恩復入余姚，破上虞，進至刑浦。

translations.literal: En again entered Yuyao, broke Shangyu, advanced to Xing Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En returned to Yuyao, took Shangyu, and pushed to Xing Ford.

sentences.zh: 琰遣參軍劉宣之距破之，恩退縮。

translations.literal: Yan sent aide Liu Xuanzhi to oppose and break him; En shrank back.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yan's aide Liu Xuanzhi repulsed him.

sentences.zh: 少日，復寇刑浦，害謝琰。

translations.literal: After a few days he again raided Xing Ford and killed Xie Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Days later he struck Xing Ford again and killed Xie Yan.

sentences.zh: 朝廷大震，遣冠軍將軍桓不才、輔國將軍孫無終、甯朔將軍高雅之擊之，恩復還於海。

translations.literal: The court was greatly shaken and sent General Who Crowns the Army Huan Bucai, General Who Supports the State Sun Wuzhong, and General Who Calms the North Gao Yazhi against him; En again returned to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: The court panicked and dispatched Huan Bucai, Sun Wuzhong, and Gao Yazhi; Sun En fled offshore again.

sentences.zh: 於是復遣牢之東屯會稽，吳國內史袁山松築扈瀆壘，緣海備恩。

translations.literal: Thereupon they again sent Laozhi east to encamp at Kuaiji; Interior Minister of Wu Yuan Shansong built the Hu fort, along the sea guarding against En.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laozhi was sent east to Kuaiji while Yuan Shansong, interior minister of Wu, walled the Hu shore against him.

sentences.zh: 明年，恩復入浹口，雅之敗績。

translations.literal: The next year En again entered Jia Ford; Yazhi suffered rout.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Sun En entered Jia Ford and routed Gao Yazhi.

sentences.zh: 牢之進擊，恩復還於海。

translations.literal: Laozhi advanced striking; En again returned to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laozhi attacked; Sun En withdrew to sea.

sentences.zh: 轉寇扈瀆，害袁山松，仍浮海向京口。

translations.literal: He turned to raid Hu, killed Yuan Shansong, still floated sea toward Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: He hit the Hu defenses, slew Yuan Shansong, and sailed for Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 牢之率眾西擊，未達，而恩已至，劉裕乃總兵緣海距之。

translations.literal: Laozhi led a host west to strike, had not arrived, yet En had already come; Liu Yu thereupon commanded troops along the sea to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laozhi turned west too late; Liu Yu took coastal troops to meet Sun En.

sentences.zh: 及戰，恩眾大敗，狼狽赴船。

translations.literal: When they fought, En's host was greatly defeated; he scrambled to boats.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu shattered him; Sun En scrambled aboard ship.

sentences.zh: 尋又集眾，欲向京都，朝廷駭懼，陳兵以待之。

translations.literal: Soon he again gathered a host, wished to go toward the capital; the court was terrified and deployed troops awaiting him.
translations.idiomatic: He regrouped for another thrust at the capital; the court braced for attack.

sentences.zh: 恩至新州，不敢進而退，北寇廣陵，陷之，乃浮海而北。

translations.literal: En reached Xinzhou, did not dare advance but withdrew, raided north to Guangling, took it, thereupon floated sea north.
translations.idiomatic: He probed Xinzhou, drew back, seized Guangling, and sailed north.

sentences.zh: 劉裕與劉敬宣並軍躡之于鬱洲，累戰，恩復大敗，由是漸衰弱，復沿海還南。

translations.literal: Liu Yu with Liu Jingxuan combined armies tracking him at Yuzhou; fighting repeatedly, En was again greatly defeated; hence he gradually weakened, again along the coast returned south.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu and Liu Jingxuan ran him down at Yuzhou, broke him again, and drove him south along the coast.

sentences.zh: 裕亦尋海要截，復大破恩于扈瀆，恩遂遠迸海中。

translations.literal: Yu also soon intercepted along the sea, again greatly broke En at Hu; En thereupon fled far into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu intercepted him at Hu and broke him once more; Sun En vanished into the deep sea.

sentences.zh: 及桓玄用事，恩復寇臨海，臨海太守辛景討破之。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan held power, En again raided Linhai; Administrator of Linhai Xin Jing attacked and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Huan Xuan he raided Linhai until Xin Jing defeated him.

sentences.zh: 恩窮戚，乃赴海自沈，妖黨及妓妾謂之水仙，投水從死者百數。

translations.literal: En was reduced to desperation, thereupon threw himself in the sea and drowned; sorcerous partisans and singing-girls called him water immortal; those who followed drowning were in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Sun En drowned himself; hundreds of cultists and concubines called him a water immortal and leapt after him.

sentences.zh: 余眾復推恩妹夫盧循為主。

translations.literal: The remaining host again pushed En's brother-in-law Lu Xun as leader.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors made his brother-in-law Lu Xun their chief.

sentences.zh: 自恩初入海，所虜男女之口，其後戰死及自溺並流離被傳賣者，至恩死時裁數千人存，而恩攻沒謝琰、袁山松，陷廣陵，前後數十戰，亦殺百姓數萬人。

translations.literal: From En's first entering sea, the men and women captives—afterward those who died in battle or drowned themselves together with those drifted apart and sold on—when En died only several thousand survived; yet En in attacks took Xie Yan and Yuan Shansong, took Guangling, front and back several tens of battles, also killed commoners several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: From his first flight to his death, the hundreds of thousands he seized dwindled to a few thousand through battle, suicide, and sale—yet he had killed Xie Yan and Yuan Shansong, sacked Guangling, fought dozens of battles, and left tens of thousands of civilians dead.

sentences.zh: 盧循

translations.literal: Lu Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun

sentences.zh: 盧循，字於先，小名元龍，司空從事中郎諶之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Lu Xun, courtesy name Yuxian, childhood name Yuanlong, was great-grandson of Consultant to the Minister of Works Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun, courtesy Yuxian, childhood name Yuanlong, was great-grandson of Lu Chen, consultant to the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 雙眸冏徹，瞳子四轉，善草隸弈棋之藝。

translations.literal: Both pupils were limpid through, eyeballs turned four ways; he was good at grass script, clerical script, and the art of weiqi.
translations.idiomatic: His eyes were said to shine with shifting pupils; he excelled at calligraphy and go.

sentences.zh: 沙門慧遠有鑒裁，見而謂之曰：「君雖體涉風素，而志存不軌。

translations.literal: Monk Huiyuan had judgment; seeing him he said, "Though your body touches wind and plainness, your aim harbors rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Huiyuan told him, "You wear the air of a recluse but nurse treason.

sentences.zh: 」循娶孫恩妹。

translations.literal: " Xun married Sun En's younger sister.
translations.idiomatic: He married Sun En's sister.

sentences.zh: 及恩作亂，與循通謀。

translations.literal: When En made turmoil, he conspired with Xun.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun En rose, Lu Xun was his accomplice.

sentences.zh: 恩性酷忍，循每諫止之，人士多賴以濟免。

translations.literal: En's nature was cruel and ruthless; Xun often remonstrated to stop him; gentlemen for the most part relied on this to escape harm.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En was savage; Lu Xun often checked him, saving many lives.

sentences.zh: 恩亡，餘眾推循為主。

translations.literal: When En died, the remainder pushed Xun as leader.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun En died the rebels chose Lu Xun.

sentences.zh: 元興二年正月，寇東陽，八月，攻永嘉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanxing, first month, he raided Dongyang; eighth month, attacked Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanxing 2 he struck Dongyang in spring and Yongjia in autumn.

sentences.zh: 劉裕討循至晉安，循窘急，泛海到番禺，寇廣州，逐刺史吳隱之，自攝州事，號平南將軍，遣使獻貢。

translations.literal: Liu Yu punished Xun reaching Jin'an; Xun was pressed and urgent, floated sea to Panyu, raided Guangzhou, expelled Inspector Wu Yin zhi, himself held provincial affairs, styled General Who Pacifies the South, sent envoys offering tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu drove him to Jin'an; Lu Xun sailed to Panyu, ousted Wu Yinzhi, styled himself general who pacifies the south, and sent tribute north.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷新誅桓氏，中外多虞，乃權假循征虜將軍、廣州刺史、平越中郎將。

translations.literal: At that time the court had newly executed the Huan clan; inside and outside had many worries; thereupon temporarily credentialled Xun General Who Punishes Captives, Inspector of Guang Province, Colonel Who Pacifies the Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The court, busy with the Huan purge, papered him over as general who punishes captives, inspector of Guangzhou, and colonel who pacifies the Yue.

sentences.zh: 義熙中，劉裕伐慕容超，循所署始興太守徐道覆，循之姊夫也，使人勸循乘虛而出，循不從。

translations.literal: In the Yixi years Liu Yu campaigned against Murong Chao; Xun's appointed Administrator of Shixing Xu Daofu—Xun's elder sister's husband—sent someone urging Xun to exploit emptiness and march out; Xun did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: While Liu Yu fought Murong Chao in the north, Xu Daofu, Lu Xun's brother-in-law and prefect of Shixing, urged a strike at the empty capital; Lu Xun refused.

sentences.zh: 道覆乃至番禺，說循曰：「朝廷恆以君為腹心之疾，劉公未有旋日，不乘此機而保一日之安，若平齊之後，劉公自率眾至豫章，遣銳師過嶺，雖復君之神武，必不能當也。

translations.literal: Daofu then went to Panyu and said to Xun, "The court always takes you as disease of the belly's core; Lord Liu has no day of return; not riding this chance to secure one day's peace—if after pacifying Qi Lord Liu personally leads a host to Yuzhang, sends crack troops over the ranges—even again your divine martial skill, surely cannot withstand.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daofu came to Panyu and said, "The court sees you as a mortal threat. Liu Yu is far in the north—if you do not strike now, once Qi falls he will march on Yuzhang and send elite columns over the mountains; even you cannot hold them.

sentences.zh: 今日之機，萬不可失。

translations.literal: Today's opportunity, in ten thousand cannot be lost.
translations.idiomatic: This moment must not be wasted.

sentences.zh: 既克都邑，劉裕雖還，無能為也。

translations.literal: Once the capital is taken, though Liu Yu returns, he can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Seize the capital and Liu Yu cannot save it.

sentences.zh: 君若不同，便當率始興之眾直指尋陽。

translations.literal: If you lord do not agree, I should lead Shixing's host straight to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: If you refuse, I will take the Shixing army straight to Xunyang myself.

sentences.zh: 」循甚不樂此舉，無以奪其計，乃從之。

translations.literal: " Xun was very unhappy with this move, had no way to overrule his plan, thereupon followed.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun hated the plan but could not stop Xu Daofu and yielded.

sentences.zh: 初，道覆密欲裝舟艦，乃使人伐船材于南康山，偽云將下都貨之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Daofu secretly wished to fit out boats and ships, therefore sent men to fell ship timber in Nankang hills, falsely saying they would float down to the capital to sell.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daofu had timber cut in the Nankang hills, claiming it would be rafted to market in the capital.

sentences.zh: 後稱力少不能得致，即於郡賤賣之，價減數倍，居人貪賤，賣衣物而市之。

translations.literal: Later he claimed strength was short and could not bring it, immediately in the commandery sold it cheap, price reduced several fold; residents greedy for cheap sold clothes and bought it.
translations.idiomatic: He then claimed he could not transport it and dumped the lumber at fire-sale prices; locals snapped it up.

sentences.zh: 贛石水急，出船甚難，皆儲之。

translations.literal: Gan Rock's water was swift; getting boats out was very hard; all stored it.
translations.idiomatic: The Gan rapids made hauling boats hard, so people hoarded the planks at home.

sentences.zh: 如是者數四，故船版大積，而百姓弗之疑。

translations.literal: Thus four times or so, therefore ship planks greatly piled, yet the hundred clans did not suspect them.
translations.idiomatic: After several rounds of this trick, enough planking for a fleet lay in every village, unsuspected.

sentences.zh: 及道覆舉兵，案賣券而取之，無得隱匿者，乃並力裝之，旬日而辦。

translations.literal: When Daofu raised troops, he checked sale receipts and took them; none could hide; thereupon combined strength to fit them; within ten days it was done.
translations.idiomatic: When he rebelled, he presented the old IOUs and reclaimed every plank; within days a fleet was built.

sentences.zh: 遂舉眾寇南康、廬陵、豫章諸郡，守相皆委任奔走。

translations.literal: Thereupon he raised the host raiding Nankang, Luling, Yuzhang commanderies; defenders all threw office and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He swept through Nankang, Luling, and Yuzhang; officials fled.

sentences.zh: 鎮南將軍何無忌率眾距之，兵敗被害。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the South He Wuji led a host to oppose him; the army was defeated and he met harm.
translations.idiomatic: He Wuji, general who guards the south, opposed him and died in defeat.

sentences.zh: 循遣道覆寇江陵，未至，為官軍所敗，馳走告循曰：「請並力攻京都，若克之，江陵非所憂也。

translations.literal: Xun sent Daofu to raid Jiangling; before arriving, he was defeated by government troops; galloping he told Xun, "Please combine strength attacking the capital; if it is taken, Jiangling is not a worry.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daofu's column toward Jiangling was crushed; he raced back to Lu Xun, saying, "Forget Jiangling—take the capital together.

sentences.zh: 」乃連旗而下，戎卒十萬，舳艫千計，敗衛將軍劉毅于桑落洲，逕至江寧。

translations.literal: " Thereupon connected banners downstream, armored soldiers one hundred thousand, ships and hulls counted by thousands, defeated Guard General Liu Yi at Mulberry Fall Isle, went straight to Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: They sailed downriver with a hundred thousand men and a thousand hulls, crushed Liu Yi at Mulberry Fall Isle, and reached Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 道覆素有膽決，知劉裕已還，欲乾沒一戰，請於新亭至白石，焚舟而上，數道攻之。

translations.literal: Daofu of old had courage and resolution; knowing Liu Yu had already returned, wished to risk all in one battle, requesting from Xinting to Baishi to burn boats and go up, several routes attacking.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daofu, bold by nature, knew Liu Yu was back and wanted to burn the fleet at Xinting–Baishi and storm the city on foot.

sentences.zh: 循多謀少決，欲以萬全之計，固不聽。

translations.literal: Xun was many in plots, short in decisions, wished with a ten-thousand-complete plan, firmly did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun was full of schemes but could not decide; he clung to a "safe" plan and refused.

sentences.zh: 道覆以循無斷，乃歎曰：「我終為盧公所誤，事必無成。

translations.literal: Daofu because Xun had no resolution, thereupon sighed, "I will in the end be misled by Lord Lu; the affair surely will not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daofu groaned, "Lu Xun will ruin us—this will fail.

sentences.zh: 使我得為英雄驅馳，天下不足定也！

translations.literal: If I could be driven by a hero, the realm is not worth settling!
translations.idiomatic: Give me a real leader and the empire would fall in our lap!

sentences.zh: 」裕懼其侵軼，乃柵石頭，斷柤浦，以距之。

translations.literal: " Yu feared his incursion, therefore palisaded Stone City, cut Zhapu, to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu palisaded Stone City and blocked Zhapu against him.

sentences.zh: 循攻柵不利，船艦為暴風所傾，人有死者。

translations.literal: Xun attacked the palisade without success; boats and hulls were capsized by storm wind; people had dead.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun's assault on the palisade failed; a gale swamped his ships.

sentences.zh: 列陣南岸，戰又敗績。

translations.literal: He arrayed battle south of the shore; battle again suffered rout.
translations.idiomatic: He formed battle south of the river and lost again.

sentences.zh: 乃進攻京口，寇掠諸縣，無所得。

translations.literal: Thereupon he advanced attacking Jingkou, raiding and plundering various counties, obtaining nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Jingkou and raided counties for little gain.

sentences.zh: 循謂道覆曰：「師老矣！

translations.literal: Xun said to Daofu, "The army is old!
translations.idiomatic: He told Xu Daofu, "The men are spent!

sentences.zh: 弗能復振。

translations.literal: Cannot again rouse.
translations.idiomatic: They cannot rally.

sentences.zh: 可據尋陽，並力取荊州，徐更與都下爭衡，猶可以濟。

translations.literal: We can hold Xunyang, combine strength to take Jing Province, slowly again with the capital contend the balance—still can succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Fall back to Xunyang, seize Jingzhou together, then bargain with the capital—that can still work.

sentences.zh: 」因自蔡洲南走，復據尋陽。

translations.literal: " Thereupon from Cai Isle he fled south, again held Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He fled from Cai Isle to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 裕先遣群率追討，自統大眾繼進，又敗循於雷池。

translations.literal: Yu first sent group leaders pursuing punishment, himself commanding the great host following, again defeated Xun at Thunder Lake.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent vanguards, followed with the main army, and beat Lu Xun at Thunder Lake.

sentences.zh: 循欲遁還豫章，乃悉力柵斷左裏。

translations.literal: Xun wished to flee returning to Yuzhang, thereupon used full strength to palisade block Zuoli.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun tried to regain Yuzhang and fortified Zuoli.

sentences.zh: 裕命眾攻柵，循眾雖死戰，猶不能抗。

translations.literal: Yu ordered the host to attack the palisade; though Xun's host fought to the death, still could not resist.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu stormed the line; Lu Xun's men fought to the last but broke.

sentences.zh: 裕乘勝擊之，循單舸而走，收散卒得千餘人，還保廣州。

translations.literal: Yu riding victory struck him; Xun fled in a single boat, gathered scattered soldiers obtaining more than a thousand men, returned guarding Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu pressed the rout; Lu Xun escaped in one boat with a thousand survivors and fled to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 裕先遣孫處從海道據番禺城，循攻之不下。

translations.literal: Yu first sent Sun Chu from the sea route to hold Panyu city; Xun attacked it without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu had Sun Chu seize Panyu by sea; Lu Xun could not retake it.

sentences.zh: 道覆保始興，因險自固。

translations.literal: Daofu held Shixing, relying on narrows to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daofu held Shixing's defiles.

sentences.zh: 循乃襲合浦，克之，進攻交州。

translations.literal: Xun thereupon raided Hepu, took it, advanced attacking Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun took Hepu and marched on Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 至龍編，刺史杜慧度譎而敗之。

translations.literal: Reaching Longbian, Inspector Du Huidu deceived him and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: At Longbian, Du Huidu, the inspector, lured him into a trap and won.

sentences.zh: 循勢屈，知不免，先鴆妻子十餘人，又召妓妾問曰：「我今將自殺，誰能同者？

translations.literal: Xun's situation was bent; knowing he could not escape, first poisoned wives and children more than ten persons, again summoned singing-girls asking, "I now will kill myself—who can join?
translations.idiomatic: Trapped, Lu Xun poisoned his family, then asked his concubines, "I mean to die—who will follow?

sentences.zh: 」多云：「雀鼠貪生，就死實人情所難。

translations.literal: " Many said, "Sparrows and mice cling to life; to approach death is truly what human feeling finds hard.
translations.idiomatic: Most answered, "Even beasts cling to life—death is too hard.

sentences.zh: 」有云：「官尚當死，某豈願生！

translations.literal: " Some said, "Officials still should die—how could I wish to live!
translations.idiomatic: Others cried, "If ministers must die, I will not cling to life!

sentences.zh: 」於是悉鴆諸辭死者，因自投于水。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he poisoned all who declined death, thereupon threw himself in the water.
translations.idiomatic: He poisoned every concubine who hesitated, then drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 慧度取其屍斬之，及其父嘏；

translations.literal: Huidu took his corpse and beheaded it, together with his father Gu;
translations.idiomatic: Du Huidu beheaded his corpse and executed his father Qiao Gu.

sentences.zh: 同黨盡獲，傳首京都。

translations.literal: Accomplices were all captured; heads were sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His partisans were rounded up and their heads sent to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 譙縱

translations.literal: Qiao Zong.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zong

sentences.zh: 譙縱，巴西南充人也。

translations.literal: Qiao Zong was a man of Nanchong in Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zong came from Nanchong in Baxi.

sentences.zh: 祖獻之，有重名於西土。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xianzhi had heavy fame in the western lands.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qiao Xianzhi was renowned in the west.

sentences.zh: 縱少而謹慎，蜀人愛之。

translations.literal: Zong from youth was cautious and prudent; Shu men loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Prudent from boyhood, he was beloved in Shu.

sentences.zh: 為安西府參軍。

translations.literal: He was aide on the staff of the General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the staff of the general who pacifies the west.

sentences.zh: 義熙元年，刺史遣縱及侯暉等領諸縣氐進兵東下。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yixi, the inspector sent Zong and Hou Hui and others to lead Di of the various counties east downstream.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi 1 the inspector ordered Qiao Zong, Hou Hui, and others to march the county Di levies downriver.

sentences.zh: 暉有貳志，因梁州人不樂東也，將圖益州刺史毛璩，與巴西陽昧結謀于五城水口，共逼縱為主。

translations.literal: Hui had two hearts; because Liang Province men did not wish to go east, he plotted to scheme against Inspector of Yi Province Mao Qu, and with Yang Mei of Baxi plotted at Wucheng Ford, together pressing Zong to be leader.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Hui, resenting the eastern campaign, conspired with Yang Mei at Wucheng to kill Mao Qu and forced Qiao Zong to head the mutiny.

sentences.zh: 縱懼而不當，走投于水，暉引出而請之，至於再三，遂以兵逼縱於輿上。

translations.literal: Zong feared and would not accept, ran and threw himself in the water; Hui pulled him out and begged him, reaching thrice; thereupon used troops to press Zong on the litter.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zong refused and tried to drown himself; Hou Hui fished him out, begged him three times, and at spearpoint seated him in the leader's carriage.

sentences.zh: 攻璩弟西夷校尉瑾于涪城，城陷，瑾死之，縱乃自號梁、秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: They attacked Qu's younger brother Colonel of the Western Yi Jin at Fucheng; the city fell; Jin died in it; Zong thereupon styled himself Inspector of Liang and Qin provinces.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed Fucheng, killed Mao Jin, and Qiao Zong proclaimed himself governor of Liang and Qin.

sentences.zh: 璩聞縱反，自略城步還成都，遣參軍王瓊率三千人討縱，又遣弟瑗領四千兵繼瓊後進。

translations.literal: When Qu heard Zong rebelled, he returned from Luecheng on foot to Chengdu, sent aide Wang Qiong with three thousand men to punish Zong, again sent younger brother Yuan leading four thousand troops following Qiong's rear advance.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Qu marched back from Luecheng, sent Wang Qiong with three thousand men, and Mao Yuan with four thousand in support.

sentences.zh: 縱遣弟明子及暉距瓊於廣漢，瓊擊破暉等，追至綿竹。

translations.literal: Zong sent younger brother Mingzi and Hui to oppose Qiong at Guanghan; Qiong struck and broke Hui and others, pursued to Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Mingzi and Hou Hui met Wang Qiong at Guanghan; Wang Qiong routed Hou Hui and chased them to Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 明子設二伏以待之，大敗瓊眾，死者十八九。

translations.literal: Mingzi set two ambushes awaiting them, greatly defeated Qiong's host; dead were eight or nine in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Mingzi ambushed him and slaughtered nine tenths of Wang Qiong's men.

sentences.zh: 益州營戶李騰開城以納縱。

translations.literal: Yi Province garrison-household Li Teng opened the city to admit Zong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Teng, a garrison colonist, opened the gates to Qiao Zong.

sentences.zh: 毛璩既死，縱以從弟洪為益州刺史，明子為鎮東將軍、巴州刺史，率其眾五千人屯白帝，自稱成都王。

translations.literal: After Mao Qu died, Zong made cousin Hong Inspector of Yi Province, Mingzi General Who Guards the East and Inspector of Ba Province, led his host of five thousand men to encamp at Baidi, styled himself Prince of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: After Mao Qu fell, Qiao Zong named his cousin Hong governor of Yi, Mingzi general who guards the east and governor of Ba, garrisoned five thousand men at Baidi, and called himself prince of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 明年，遣使稱籓于姚興，將順流東寇，以討車騎將軍劉裕為名，乞師于姚興，且請桓謙為助，興遣之。

translations.literal: The next year he sent envoys declaring vassalage to Yao Xing, intending downstream east to raid, in the name of punishing Chariot and Cavalry General Liu Yu, begging troops from Yao Xing, and requesting Huan Qian as aid; Xing sent them.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he swore allegiance to Yao Xing of Later Qin, asked for troops against Liu Yu, and secured Huan Qian as an ally.

sentences.zh: 九年，劉裕以西陽太守硃齡石為益州刺史，甯朔將軍臧喜、下邳太守劉鐘，蘭陵太守蒯恩等率眾二萬，自江陵討縱。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Liu Yu made Xiyang Administrator Zhu Lingshi Inspector of Yi Province; General Who Calms the North Zang Xi, Xiapi Administrator Liu Zhong, Lanling Administrator Kuai En and others led a host of twenty thousand from Jiangling to punish Zong.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 Liu Yu sent Zhu Lingshi as governor of Yi with Zang Xi, Liu Zhong, and Kuai En—twenty thousand men—from Jiangling against Qiao Zong.

sentences.zh: 初謀元率，僉難其人，齡石資名素淺，裕違眾拔之，授以麾下之半。

translations.literal: When first planning the chief commander, all found the man hard; Lingshi's credentials and name were of old shallow; Yu went against the multitude and raised him, entrusting half the command under his tent.
translations.idiomatic: Choosing a commander, the staff hesitated—Zhu Lingshi was young and obscure—but Liu Yu overruled them and gave him half the army.

sentences.zh: 藏喜，裕妻弟也，位出其右，又隸焉。

translations.literal: Zang Xi was Yu's wife's younger brother, rank stood above his, yet was subordinate to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Xi, Liu Yu's brother-in-law, outranked him yet served under him.

sentences.zh: 齡石次於白帝，縱遣譙道福重兵守涪。

translations.literal: Lingshi halted at Baidi; Zong sent Qiao Daofu with heavy troops to guard Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Lingshi stopped at Baidi while Qiao Zong posted Qiao Daofu to hold Fu.

sentences.zh: 齡石師次平模，去成都二百里，縱遣其大將軍侯暉、尚書僕射譙詵屯平模，夾岸連城，層樓重柵，眾未能攻。

translations.literal: Lingshi's army halted at Pingmo, two hundred li from Chengdu; Zong sent his grand general Hou Hui and Vice Director of the Secretariat Qiao Shen to encamp at Pingmo, cities linked on both banks, storied towers and doubled palisades; the host could not attack.
translations.idiomatic: At Pingmo, two hundred li from Chengdu, Hou Hui and Qiao Shen walled both riverbanks in depth; Zhu Lingshi could not break them.

sentences.zh: 齡石謂劉鐘曰：「天方暑熱，賊今固險，攻之難拔，只困我師。

translations.literal: Lingshi said to Liu Zhong, "Heaven is just now sweltering hot; the bandits today hold fast the narrows; attacking is hard to take—we only trap our army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Lingshi told Liu Zhong, "In this heat their stronghold is impenetrable—we will only waste men.

sentences.zh: 吾欲蓄銳息兵，伺隙而進，卿以為何如？

translations.literal: I wish to store sharpness and rest troops, wait for a gap and advance—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: I say we rest and strike when we see an opening—your view?

sentences.zh: 」鐘曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Zhong said, "It is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhong replied, "Wrong.

sentences.zh: 前揚聲言大將由內水，故道福不敢舍涪，今重軍逼之，出其不意，侯暉之徒已破膽矣。

translations.literal: Earlier we raised voice saying the great general would go by inner water, therefore Daofu dared not leave Fu; now heavy army presses them, beyond their expectation—Hou Hui and company already have broken gall.
translations.idiomatic: We feinted the inner river so Qiao Daofu hugged Fu; a sudden thrust catches them flat-footed—Hou Hui is already terrified.

sentences.zh: 正可因其凶而攻之，勢當必克。

translations.literal: Rightly can we exploit their fear and attack them; the momentum surely must overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Strike while they panic and we cannot lose.

sentences.zh: 克平模之後，自可鼓行而前，成都必不能守。

translations.literal: Once Pingmo is taken, naturally we can beat drums and advance; Chengdu surely cannot hold.
translations.idiomatic: Take Pingmo and we can drum straight to Chengdu—they cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 若綏兵相持，虛實相見，涪軍復來，難為敵也。

translations.literal: If we slow troops and stalemate, empty and solid meet each other, Fu's army comes again—it is hard to be a match.
translations.idiomatic: Delay, and Fu's reinforcements join them—we face a united west.

sentences.zh: 進不能戰，退無所資，二萬餘人因為蜀子虜耳。

translations.literal: Advance cannot fight, retreat has no supplies—more than twenty thousand men thereby become Shu children's captives.
translations.idiomatic: Then we cannot advance or supply ourselves—twenty thousand men become Shu prisoners.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " They followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Lingshi took his advice.

sentences.zh: 翌日，進攻皆克，斬侯暉等，於是遂進。

translations.literal: The next day, advance attack all took, beheaded Hou Hui and others, thereupon advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Next day they stormed through, slew Hou Hui, and pushed on.

sentences.zh: 縱之城守者相次瓦解，縱乃出奔。

translations.literal: Zong's city defenders in succession collapsed; Zong thereupon fled out.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zong's defenses crumbled; he bolted.

sentences.zh: 其尚書令馬耽封倉庫以待王師。

translations.literal: His Director of the Secretariat Ma Dan sealed storehouses awaiting the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Dan, director of the secretariat, sealed the granaries for the Jin army.

sentences.zh: 及齡石入成都，誅縱同祖之親，餘皆安堵，使復其業。

translations.literal: When Lingshi entered Chengdu, he executed Zong's kin of the same grandfather; the rest were all settled in peace, ordered to resume their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Lingshi executed Qiao Zong's close clan but left common folk unmolested.

sentences.zh: 縱之走也，先如其墓，縱女謂縱曰：「走必不免，只取辱焉。

translations.literal: When Zong fled, he first went to his tomb; Zong's daughter said to Zong, "Flee surely cannot escape—only fetch shame.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing past the family graves, his daughter said, "You cannot outrun them—only humiliate yourself.

sentences.zh: 等死，死于先人之墓可也。

translations.literal: Equal death—dying at the forebears' tombs can do.
translations.idiomatic: If we must die, die here among the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 」縱不從，投道福於涪。

translations.literal: " Zong did not follow, threw himself toward Daofu at Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zong refused and ran to Qiao Daofu at Fu.

sentences.zh: 道福怒謂縱曰：「大丈夫居如斯功業，安可棄哉！

translations.literal: Daofu angrily said to Zong, "Great man holding such achievement—how can you abandon it!
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Daofu raged, "You built this realm—how dare you quit?

sentences.zh: 今欲為降虜，豈可而得！

translations.literal: Now wishing to be surrender captives—how can that be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: Surrender? Impossible!

sentences.zh: 人誰不死，何懼之甚！

translations.literal: Men all die—what extreme fear!
translations.idiomatic: All men die—what is there to fear?

sentences.zh: 」因投縱以劍，中其馬鞍。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he threw Zong the sword; it hit his saddle.
translations.idiomatic: He hurled a sword at Qiao Zong, striking his saddle.

sentences.zh: 縱去之，乃自縊。

translations.literal: Zong left him, thereupon hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zong broke away and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 道福謂其徒曰：「吾養爾等，正為今日。

translations.literal: Daofu said to his followers, "I raised you all, just for today.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Daofu told his men, "I fed you for this hour.

sentences.zh: 蜀之存亡，實系在我，不在譙王。

translations.literal: Shu's survival or destruction, truly hangs on me, not on Prince Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's fate rests on me, not on the prince of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 我尚在，猶足一戰。

translations.literal: I still am here—still enough for one battle.
translations.idiomatic: While I live we can fight once more.

sentences.zh: 」士咸許諾。

translations.literal: " The soldiers all promised.
translations.idiomatic: They cheered agreement.

sentences.zh: 乃散金帛以賜其眾，眾受之而走。

translations.literal: Thereupon he scattered gold and silk to bestow on his host; the host received them and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He scattered gold and silk; his men pocketed it and ran.

sentences.zh: 道福獨奔廣漢，廣漢人杜瑾執之。

translations.literal: Daofu alone fled to Guanghan; Guanghan man Du Jin seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Daofu fled alone to Guanghan, where Du Jin seized him.

sentences.zh: 硃齡石徙馬耽於越巂，追殺之。

translations.literal: Zhu Lingshi moved Ma Dan to Yuexi and pursued killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Lingshi exiled Ma Dan to Yuexi and had him killed en route.

sentences.zh: 耽之徙也，謂其徒曰：「硃侯不送我京師，滅眾口也，吾必不免。

translations.literal: When Dan was moved, he said to his followers, "Lord Zhu not sending me to the capital is to silence many mouths—I cannot escape.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Dan told his men, "Zhu Lingshi avoids sending me to the capital to hush talk—I am a dead man.

sentences.zh: 」乃盥洗而臥，引繩而死。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he washed and lay down, drew rope and died.
translations.idiomatic: He bathed, lay down, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 須臾，齡石師至，遂戮屍焉。

translations.literal: In a moment Lingshi's army arrived, thereupon mutilated the corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later Zhu Lingshi's men arrived and desecrated his body.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historians' judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Historians' judgment

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：惠皇失禦，政紊朝危，難起蕭牆，毒痡函夏，九州波駭，五嶽塵飛，干戈日尋，戎車競逐。

translations.literal: The historians say: Emperor Hui lost the reins; government was tangled, court perilous; disaster rose within the screen; poison spread through the summer lands; the nine provinces wave-shocked, the five march-mountains dust-flying; shields and spears sought daily, war chariots raced in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: Emperor Hui lost control; the court unraveled; rebellion began at home and poisoned the realm; the empire shook and armies clashed without end.

sentences.zh: 王彌好亂樂禍，挾詐懷奸，命儔嘯侶，伺間侯隙，助悖逆於平陽，肆殘忍於都邑，遂使生靈塗炭，神器流離，邦國軫《麥秀》之哀，宮廟興《黍離》之痛，豈天意乎？

translations.literal: Wang Mi loved turmoil and rejoiced in calamity, carried deceit and harbored treachery, matched companions and whistled partners, watched gaps and waited cracks, helped rebellion at Pingyang, wantoned cruelty in the capital—thereupon making living souls smeared in charcoal, the sacred vessel drifted apart; states groaned with the grief of "The Wheat's Elegy," palace shrines rose with the pain of "Millet in Rows"—was it heaven's intent? Was it man's doing?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi thrived on chaos, aided usurpers at Pingyang, and turned Luoyang to slaughter until the throne fled and the land mourned like the kings of Shang and Zhou—was that fate or folly?

sentences.zh: 豈人事乎？

translations.literal: Was it man's doing?
translations.idiomatic: Was it human failure?

sentences.zh: 何醜虜之倡狂而亂離之斯瘼者也！

translations.literal: How the ugly captives led the madness and disorder thus wasted the age!
translations.idiomatic: How those barbarian chieftains fed the age's ruin!

sentences.zh: 張昌等或鴟張淮浦，或蟻聚荊衡，招烏合之凶徒，逞豺狼之貪暴，憑陵險隘，倔強江湖，未淹歲稔，咸至誅戮，實自取之，非為不幸。

translations.literal: Zhang Chang and others either owl-stretched on the Huai shore or ant-gathered on Jing and Heng, recruited crow-joined vicious followers, indulged jackal and wolf greed and violence, relied on defiles, stubborn in rivers and lakes; before a full harvest year turned, all reached execution and slaughter—truly they took it themselves, not misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang and kin—whether on the Huai or in Jingzhou—raised rabbles, preyed like wolves, and were crushed within the year; they earned their doom.

sentences.zh: 峻約同惡相濟，生此亂階，孫盧同類相求，嗣成妖逆。

translations.literal: Jun and Yue aided each other's evil, bore these steps of turmoil; Sun and Lu, same kind seeking each other, continued and completed sorcerous rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun and Zu Yue abetted each other; Sun En and Lu Xun carried the contagion on.

sentences.zh: 至乃干戈掃地，災沴滔天，雖樊謝之毒被含靈，李郭之禍延宮闕，方凶比暴，弗是加也。

translations.literal: As for shields and spears sweeping the ground, calamity floods heaven—though Fan and Xie's poison touched all spirits, Li and Guo's disaster reached palace gates, set beside these ferocities, it does not surpass.
translations.idiomatic: Their wars scoured the earth and heaven itself seemed poisoned—worse in scale than even Fan and Xie or Li and Guo.

sentences.zh: 譙縱乘茲釁隙，肆彼奸謀，旋踵而亡，無足論矣。

translations.literal: Qiao Zong rode this crack and vented his treachery; he perished in a turn of the heel—not worth discussing.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zong exploited the breach and schemed, yet collapsed in an instant—hardly worth a word.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：中朝隳政，王彌肇亂。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: The mid-court ruined government; Wang Mi opened chaos.
translations.idiomatic: The verdict reads: When the central court failed, Wang Mi began the storm.

sentences.zh: 神器流離，生靈塗炭。

translations.literal: The sacred vessel drifted apart; living souls smeared in charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: The throne wandered; the people burned.

sentences.zh: 群妖伺隙，構茲多難。

translations.literal: Crowd of demons watched gaps, built this many hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Demons of disorder seized every chance to multiply sorrow.

sentences.zh: 薦食荊衡，陵虐江漢。

translations.literal: They nibbled Jing and Heng, tyrannized the Yangtze and Han.
translations.idiomatic: They devoured Jingzhou and the lake country and terrorized the great rivers.

sentences.zh: 孫盧奸慝，約峻殘賊。

translations.literal: Sun and Lu were wicked and false; Yue and Jun cruel bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En and Lu Xun were deceivers; Zu Yue and Su Jun butchers.

sentences.zh: 窮凶極暴，為鬼為蜮。

translations.literal: Utterly fierce and violent, they became ghosts and goblins.
translations.idiomatic: Their savagery made them fiends.

sentences.zh: 縱竊岷峨，旋至顛踣。

translations.literal: Zong stole Min and E, yet soon reached overturn and stumble.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zong stole Shu from the throne and toppled just as quickly.
